---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Metadata evolution shall preserve compatibility whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 4.5. Explicit Status

Every Metadata artifact shall possess an explicit lifecycle status.

---

# 5. Lifecycle Overview

The Metadata Lifecycle is composed of six architectural states.

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Each state represents a well-defined architectural maturity level.

---

# 6. Lifecycle States

## 6.1. Proposed

A Metadata artifact has been identified as necessary but has not yet been formally defined.

Characteristics:

- architectural proposal;
- no normative status;
- subject to review.

---

## 6.2. Defined

The Metadata artifact has received a complete architectural definition.

Characteristics:

- canonical definition exists;
- semantics established;
- under architectural review.

---

## 6.3. Approved

The Metadata artifact has been formally accepted by architectural governance.

Characteristics:

- approved semantics;
- approved structure;
- eligible for publication.

---

## 6.4. Published

The Metadata artifact becomes part of the official Documentation Framework.

Characteristics:

- normative status;
- publicly referenced;
- available for use by Metadata Profiles.

---

## 6.5. Deprecated

The Metadata artifact should no longer be used for new specifications.

Characteristics:

- retained for compatibility;
- superseded by newer Metadata;
- still documented.

Existing Metadata remains valid.

---

## 6.6. Retired

The Metadata artifact has reached the end of its architectural lifecycle.

Characteristics:

- no longer recommended;
- preserved for historical traceability;
- excluded from future Metadata Profiles.

Historical Metadata Instances remain interpretable.

---

The permitted lifecycle transitions are:

```text

                Proposed

                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Reverse transitions shall not occur except through formal architectural governance.

---

# 8. Lifecycle Responsibilities

The Metadata Lifecycle defines responsibilities for each stage.

| Lifecycle Stage | Responsibility |
|-----------------|----------------|
| Proposed | Identify new Metadata requirements. |
| Defined | Produce canonical architectural definitions. |
| Approved | Validate architectural consistency. |
| Published | Make Metadata available for framework use. |
| Deprecated | Preserve compatibility while discouraging new usage. |
| Retired | Preserve historical reference only. |

---

# 10. Lifecycle Constraints

The Metadata Lifecycle shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 10.1. Controlled Introduction

New Metadata shall enter the lifecycle through the Proposed state.

---

## 10.2. No Implicit Approval

Metadata shall never become normative without explicit approval.

---

## 10.3. Semantic Preservation

Lifecycle transitions shall not redefine Metadata semantics.

---

## 10.4. Controlled Deprecation

Metadata shall not be removed immediately after deprecation.

---

## 10.5. Historical Preservation

Retired Metadata shall remain documented.

Metadata evolution shall consider compatibility with existing Metadata Profiles and Metadata Instances.

Whenever possible:

- existing Metadata Profiles shall remain valid;
- existing Metadata Instances shall remain interpretable;
- deprecated Metadata shall continue to be recognized.

Compatibility shall be preferred over replacement.

---

# 13. Relationship with Metadata Profiles

Metadata Profiles evolve independently from the Metadata Lifecycle.

A Metadata Profile may:

- adopt newly published Metadata;
- continue supporting deprecated Metadata;
- migrate to newer Metadata versions.

Profiles shall not alter the lifecycle status of Metadata.

---

# 14. Relationship with Metadata Schema

The Metadata Lifecycle governs Metadata artifacts.

It does not govern the Metadata Schema itself.

Schema evolution is managed independently while respecting Metadata lifecycle states.

---

The Metadata Lifecycle possesses the following characteristics.

Lifecycle states are explicitly defined.

---

Every lifecycle transition is auditable.

---

## 16.3. Controlled

Evolution follows architectural governance.

---

## 16.4. Stable

Semantic stability is preserved.

---

## 16.5. Extensible

Additional lifecycle states may be introduced through controlled architectural evolution if justified.

---

## 16.6. Independent

The lifecycle remains independent of implementation technologies.

# 1. Introduction

The Documentation Framework relies on Metadata to provide consistent, structured and reliable descriptions of documents.

To preserve architectural integrity, Metadata shall satisfy a set of validation rules that ensure compliance with the Metadata Architecture, Metadata Model and Metadata Schema.

This document defines the architectural principles governing Metadata Validation.

---

# 4. Validation Principles

Metadata Validation follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Validation

Validation verifies architectural conformance.

It shall not introduce new Metadata.

---

## 4.2. Deterministic Validation

Given the same Metadata and the same specification, validation shall always produce the same result.

---

## 4.3. Independent Validation

Validation shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.4. Non-Destructive Validation

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

It only evaluates conformance.

---

## 4.5. Explicit Validation

Validation outcomes shall be explicit and reproducible.

---

# 6. Validation Model

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

           Metadata Validation
                    │
                    ├──────────────────────┐
                    ▼                      ▼
             Validation Rules      Validation Results

```

Validation evaluates Metadata against a predefined set of architectural rules.

---

## 7.3. Semantic Validation

Verifies that Metadata preserves architectural meaning.

Semantic Validation confirms that:

- Metadata Elements are correctly used;
- Metadata Values correspond to their Metadata Elements;
- semantic definitions are preserved.

---

## 7.4. Consistency Validation

Verifies internal consistency among Metadata Elements.

Examples include:

- contradictory Metadata;
- incompatible Metadata combinations;
- duplicated Metadata.

---

# 9. Validation Process

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

          Structural Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Profile Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Semantic Validation
                    │
                    ▼

         Consistency Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Validation Result

```

Implementations may optimize execution while preserving equivalent validation outcomes.

---

# 10. Validation Results

Validation produces explicit outcomes.

Possible outcomes include:

- Valid
- Valid with Warnings
- Invalid

Validation Results shall include sufficient information to identify the violated validation rules.

---

# 11. Validation Severity

Validation findings may possess different severity levels.

Typical severity levels include:

- Information
- Warning
- Error
- Critical

Severity classification does not modify Metadata.

It supports architectural assessment.

---

# 12. Validation Constraints

Metadata Validation shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 12.1. Technology Independence

Validation shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

## 12.2. Repeatability

Validation shall always produce reproducible results.

---

## 12.3. Traceability

Validation Results shall identify the Validation Rules that produced them.

---

## 12.4. Non-Intrusive

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

---

## 12.5. Architectural Consistency

Validation shall preserve the Documentation Framework architecture.

The Documentation Framework is designed to evolve over time.

As new documentation domains, document categories and architectural capabilities emerge, the Metadata component shall support controlled extension without compromising architectural integrity, semantic consistency or backward compatibility.

This document defines the architectural principles governing Metadata Extensibility.

---

# 4. Extensibility Principles

Metadata Extensibility follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Stability

Extensions shall preserve the stability of the Metadata architecture.

---

## 4.2. Backward Compatibility

Extensions shall not invalidate existing Metadata.

---

## 4.3. Canonical Preservation

Extensions shall preserve canonical Metadata definitions.

---

## 4.4. Technology Independence

Extension mechanisms shall remain implementation independent.

---

## 4.5. Controlled Evolution

Extensions shall be introduced only through architectural governance.

---

## 4.5. Controlled Evolution

---

# 6. Extension Model

Conceptually.

```text

            Canonical Metadata
                    │
                    ▼

            Extension Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Architectural Review
                    │
                    ▼

            Approved Extension
                    │
                    ▼

            Extended Metadata

```

Extensions become part of the Metadata architecture only after approval.

---

# 7. Extensible Architectural Elements

The following Metadata artifacts may be extended.

## 7.1. Metadata Elements

New Metadata Elements may be introduced.

Existing Metadata Elements shall not change their semantic meaning.

---

## 7.2. Metadata Groups

New Metadata Groups may be introduced when justified by architectural evolution.

Existing groups shall preserve their responsibilities.

---

## 7.3. Metadata Schema

The Metadata Schema may evolve through the introduction of additional Metadata Elements and Metadata Groups.

Existing structural definitions shall remain valid whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 7.4. Metadata Profiles

New Metadata Profiles may specialize the canonical Metadata Schema.

Profiles shall never redefine Metadata semantics.

---

## 7.5. Metadata Dictionary

The Metadata Dictionary may be extended through the addition of newly approved Metadata Elements.

Existing definitions shall remain authoritative.

# 8. Extension Categories

Metadata extensions may belong to one of the following categories.

## 8.1. Additive Extension

Introduces new Metadata without affecting existing Metadata.

Preferred extension mechanism.

---

## 8.2. Specialization Extension

Creates specialized Metadata Profiles derived from the canonical Metadata Schema.

---

## 8.3. Organizational Extension

Introduces new Metadata Groups to improve structural organization.

---

## 8.4. Evolutionary Extension

Introduces architectural refinements through controlled Metadata evolution.

# 9. Extension Constraints

Metadata extensions shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 9.1. E-001 — No Semantic Redefinition

Existing Metadata semantics shall not be modified.

---

## 9.2. E-002 — No Responsibility Transfer

Extensions shall not alter architectural responsibilities.

---

## 9.3. E-003 — No Architectural Fragmentation

Extensions shall preserve a single canonical Metadata architecture.

---

## 9.4. E-004 — Compatibility Preservation

Extensions shall preserve interoperability whenever reasonably possible.

---

## 9.5. E-005 — Governance Approval

```text
            Extension Proposal

                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

        Compatibility Assessment
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼

            Metadata Evolution

```

The extension process is independent of implementation technologies.

---

# 12. Relationship with Metadata Lifecycle

Metadata Extensibility introduces new architectural capabilities.

The Metadata Lifecycle governs their evolution.

Lifecycle management and extensibility are complementary but independent concerns.

---

# 13. Relationship with Metadata Validation

Metadata Validation verifies that extensions conform to the Metadata architecture.

Validation does not authorize extensions.

Authorization belongs to Metadata Governance.

---

Metadata Extensibility possesses the following characteristics.

## 15.1. Controlled

---

## 15.2. Stable

---

## 15.3. Compatible

---

## 15.4. Independent

Extensions remain technology independent.

---

## 15.5. Incremental

Architecture evolves through successive extensions.

---

## 15.6. Canonical

Extensions become part of one canonical Metadata architecture.

# 1. Introduction

The Documentation Framework defines the architecture of Metadata through principles, concepts, models, schemas and specifications.

This document complements those normative specifications by providing architectural recommendations that promote consistency, maintainability and long-term interoperability.

The practices described herein are advisory rather than normative.

They represent recommended approaches for designing, extending and managing Metadata within the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Guiding Principles

The following principles should guide every Metadata design decision.

## 4.1. Prefer Simplicity

Metadata should remain as simple as possible while fulfilling its intended purpose.

Avoid unnecessary complexity.

---

## 4.2. Preserve Semantic Clarity

Every Metadata Element should possess one explicit and easily understandable meaning.

Avoid ambiguous terminology.

---

## 4.3. Promote Reuse

Existing Metadata Elements should be reused whenever possible.

Introducing new Metadata should always be justified.

---

## 4.4. Maintain Consistency

Metadata should remain consistent throughout the Documentation Framework.

Similar concepts should be described in similar ways.

---

## 4.5. Design for Evolution

Metadata should be designed with future extension in mind.

Avoid designs that unnecessarily restrict future architectural evolution.

# 5. Metadata Design Practices

## 5.1. BP-001 — Design Around Concepts

Design Metadata around architectural concepts rather than implementation requirements.

Metadata should describe information, not software.

---

## 5.2. BP-002 — Prefer Atomic Elements

Each Metadata Element should represent one concept only.

Atomic Metadata is easier to understand, validate and reuse.

---

## 5.3. BP-003 — Avoid Composite Semantics

Do not combine multiple concepts within a single Metadata Element.

Instead, define multiple independent Metadata Elements.

---

## 5.4. BP-004 — Use Stable Terminology

Metadata names should remain stable over time.

Frequent renaming should be avoided.

---

## 5.5. BP-005 — Document Every Metadata Element

Every Metadata Element should be documented within the Metadata Dictionary.

Undocumented Metadata should not become part of the canonical architecture.

# 6. Metadata Organization Practices

## 6.1. BP-006 — Group Related Metadata

Organize Metadata Elements into logical Metadata Groups.

Groups improve readability without changing semantics.

---

## 6.2. BP-007 — Avoid Redundant Metadata

Do not define Metadata that duplicates existing architectural concepts.

---

## 6.3. BP-008 — Prefer Canonical Metadata

Always use canonical Metadata Elements whenever they satisfy the required purpose.

Extensions should only be introduced when necessary.

---

## 6.4. BP-009 — Keep Profiles Focused

Metadata Profiles should contain only the Metadata required for their intended document category.

Avoid overly generic profiles.

# 7. Metadata Evolution Practices

## 7.1. BP-010 — Prefer Extension over Modification

Introduce new Metadata through controlled extensions instead of modifying existing Metadata.

## 7.2. BP-011 — Preserve Compatibility

Whenever possible, Metadata evolution should preserve compatibility with existing Metadata Profiles and Metadata Instances.

## 7.3. BP-012 — Deprecate Before Removal

Immediate removal should be avoided.

---

# 9. Metadata Validation Practices

## 9.1. BP-018 — Validate Early

Metadata should be validated as early as practical during document creation.

---

## 9.2. BP-019 — Separate Validation from Governance

Validation should determine architectural compliance.

Governance should determine architectural acceptance.

The two responsibilities should remain independent.

---

## 9.3. BP-020 — Validate Against Profiles

Metadata should always be validated against the applicable Metadata Profile.

---

- compatibility considerations.

---

# 11. Architectural Anti-Patterns

The following practices should be avoided.

## 11.1. AP-001 — Semantic Overloading

One Metadata Element representing multiple concepts.

---

## 11.2. AP-002 — Duplicate Metadata

Different Metadata Elements representing the same concept.

---

## 11.3. AP-003 — Technology-Driven Metadata

Metadata designed around implementation technologies instead of architectural concepts.

---

## 11.4. AP-004 — Profile Fragmentation

Creating numerous Metadata Profiles with insignificant differences.

---

## 11.5. AP-005 — Uncontrolled Extensions

Introducing Metadata outside the governance process.

---

## 11.6. AP-006 — Hidden Semantics

Embedding architectural meaning in naming conventions or implementation details instead of explicit Metadata definitions.

This document constitutes the normative specification of the Metadata component within the Documentation Framework.

It consolidates the architectural principles, concepts, constraints and specifications defined throughout the Metadata documentation family into a single authoritative specification.

This document defines the contractual requirements that every Metadata implementation shall satisfy in order to conform to the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Normative References

This specification incorporates the following Metadata documents by reference.

| Document | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| DF-MTD-001 | Metadata Architecture |
| DF-MTD-002 | Metadata Concepts |

| DF-MTD-012 | Metadata Best Practices *(Informative)* |
| DF-MTD-013 | Metadata Dictionary |

Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the requirements contained in these documents are considered normative.

---

# 5. Specification Principles

This specification is founded upon the following principles.

## 5.1. Architectural Consistency

All Metadata shall conform to the Documentation Framework architecture.

---

## 5.2. Semantic Stability

Metadata semantics shall remain stable throughout the Metadata Lifecycle.

---

## 5.3. Technology Independence

The Metadata specification shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 5.4. Canonical Definition

Every Metadata concept shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 5.5. Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through the governance mechanisms defined by the Documentation Framework.

## 6.9. R-009 — Traceability

Metadata evolution shall remain traceable throughout its lifecycle.

---

## 6.10. R-010 — Technology Independence

No Metadata definition shall depend upon a specific technology.

# 7. Structural Requirements

Metadata shall satisfy the following structural requirements.

- Metadata shall be organized through Metadata Schemas.
- Metadata Profiles shall specialize Metadata Schemas.
- Metadata Instances shall conform to Metadata Profiles.
- Metadata Elements shall be defined by the Metadata Dictionary.
- Metadata relationships shall preserve architectural consistency.

---

# 8. Semantic Requirements

Metadata shall satisfy the following semantic requirements.

- Every Metadata Element shall possess one canonical meaning.
- Semantic definitions shall remain stable.
- Equivalent Metadata Elements shall not coexist.
- Metadata terminology shall remain consistent.
- Metadata interpretation shall be deterministic.

---

# 13. Constraint Requirements

All Metadata Constraints defined by the Documentation Framework shall be respected.

Constraint violations shall be detectable through Metadata Validation.

---

# 15. Conformance Levels

This specification defines two levels of conformance.

## 15.1. Core Conformance

An implementation conforms at the Core level when it satisfies every mandatory requirement defined by this specification.

---

## 15.2. Extended Conformance

An implementation conforms at the Extended level when it:

- satisfies Core Conformance;
- supports Metadata extensibility;
- supports Metadata governance;
- supports Metadata lifecycle management.

---

## 15.1. Core Conformance

An implementation conforms at the Core level when it satisfies every mandatory requirement defined by this specification.

---

The following document provides implementation guidance but does not define mandatory requirements.

| Document | Classification |
|----------|----------------|
| DF-MTD-012 — Metadata Best Practices | Informative |

Failure to follow Best Practices does not imply non-conformance.

The Metadata Specification possesses the following characteristics.

## 18.1. Normative

Defines mandatory architectural requirements.

---

## 18.2. Canonical

Provides the authoritative specification of the Metadata component.

---

## 18.3. Stable

Evolves only through controlled architectural governance.

---

## 18.4. Technology Independent

Independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 18.5. Extensible

# 4. Example 1 — Metadata Element

| Attribute | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| Identifier | MTD-DOC-001 |
| Name | Document Identifier |
| Category | Identity Metadata |

Metadata Elements may be organized into logical groups.

```text

                    │

                    ├── Document Revision
                    └── Baseline
```

# 6. Example 3 — Metadata Schema

```text

                    │

                    │   ├── Document Identifier
                    │   ├── Version

                    │
```

The schema defines the architectural organization of Metadata.

# 9. Example 6 — Metadata Lifecycle

Metadata evolves through lifecycle states.

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

The Metadata Lifecycle governs the evolution of Metadata definitions.

---

# 10. Example 7 — Metadata Validation

Validation evaluates Metadata against the applicable architectural specifications.

```text

                    Metadata Instance
                    │
                    ▼

                    Validation
                    │
                    ├────────────────────────┐
                    ▼                        ▼

                Compliant              Non-Compliant

```

Validation determines architectural compliance only.

---

# 11. Example 8 — Metadata Governance

Governance authorizes Metadata evolution.

```text

                 Metadata Change Proposal
                            │
                            ▼

                   Architectural Review
                            │
                            ▼

                   Governance Decision
                            │
               ┌────────────┴────────────┐
               ▼                         ▼

            Approved                 Rejected

```

Governance controls Metadata evolution.

Metadata concepts are connected through explicit relationships.

```text

            Metadata Profile
                    │
               specializes
                    ▼

             Metadata Schema
                    │
                contains
                    ▼

            Metadata Elements
                    │
               described by
                    ▼

```

Metadata evolves through controlled extensions.

```text

           Canonical Metadata
                    │
                    ▼

           Extension Proposal
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Approval
                    │
                    ▼
```

Extensions preserve compatibility with the existing Metadata architecture.

# 1. Introduction

## 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the fundamental concepts of the **Templates** component of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the conceptual vocabulary required to describe, understand, structure, reuse, validate, govern, and evolve documentation templates.

The concepts defined here provide the semantic foundation for the Template Model, Template Elements, Template Schema, Template Lifecycle, Template Validation, Template Governance, and subsequent Templates component specifications.

## 1.2. Scope

This document defines concepts directly related to documentation templates, including:

* Template
* Template Type
* Template Structure
* Template Element
* Template Section
* Template Schema
* Template Instance
* Template Parameter
* Template Constraint
* Template Version
* Template Relationship
* Template Specialization
* Template Composition
* Template Conformance

These concepts describe the conceptual nature of templates without defining implementation technologies, repository structures, storage mechanisms, or document-management workflows.

## 1.3. Conceptual Position

Templates belong to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

The Templates component operates together with other Documentation Layer components, particularly:

* Metadata;
* Document Identity;
* Classification.

The Templates component defines reusable structures for documentation. It does not redefine the meaning or responsibilities of these other components.

---

The Templates component defines reusable structures for documentation. It does not redefine the meaning or responsibilities of these other components.

---

# 3. Template Type

## 3.1. Definition

A **Template Type** identifies the conceptual category of a Template according to the kind of documentation structure it defines.

Template Types provide a means of distinguishing templates according to their intended structural or documentary purpose.

A Template Type may be associated with:

* a particular document category;
* a documentation purpose;
* a structural pattern;
* a specialization of another Template Type.

## 3.2. Responsibility

Template Type classification belongs to the conceptual organization of Templates.

It must not be confused with the **Classification** component, which is responsible for document classification.

Templates may define structures compatible with classifications, but Templates do not assume responsibility for classifying document instances.

---

## 3.2. Responsibility

Template Type classification belongs to the conceptual organization of Templates.

It must not be confused with the **Classification** component, which is responsible for document classification.

Templates may define structures compatible with classifications, but Templates do not assume responsibility for classifying document instances.

---

# 6. Template Section

## 6.1. Definition

A **Template Section** is a structural subdivision of a Template used to organize related documentation content.

Sections provide hierarchical organization within a Template.

A section may contain:

* content structures;
* subordinate sections;
* Template Elements;
* repeated structures;
* references to other template structures.

## 6.2. Section Hierarchy

Sections may form hierarchical structures.

For example:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Section
                │
                ├── Section
                │   │
                │   ├── Element
                │   │
                │   └── Element
                │
                ├── Section
                │
                └── Element

```

The hierarchy is part of the Template Structure and does not determine physical document storage.

---

## 6.2. Section Hierarchy

Sections may form hierarchical structures.

For example:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Section
                │
                ├── Section
                │   │
                │   ├── Element
                │   │
                │   └── Element
                │
                ├── Section
                │
                └── Element

```

The hierarchy is part of the Template Structure and does not determine physical document storage.

---

# 8. Template Instance

## 8.1. Definition

A **Template Instance** is a concrete realization of a Template used to structure a specific documentation instance.

The distinction is fundamental:

```text

                 Template
                    │
              instantiation
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
                applied to
                    │
                    ▼

                 Document

```

A Template defines reusable structure.

A Template Instance represents the application of that structure to a specific documentary context.

## 8.2. Instance Independence

A Template Instance does not become the Template itself.

Changes to a Template must therefore be governed so that the relationship between the template definition and existing instances remains explicit and traceable.

# 11. Template Version

## 11.1. Definition

A **Template Version** identifies a defined state of a Template across its controlled evolution.

Template versions provide traceability for structural changes without redefining the identity of the Template itself.

Versioning of Templates must remain distinct from:

* Document Identity;
* document revision;
* operational document versioning;
* baselines.

The Templates component defines the conceptual requirements for Template evolution; it does not redefine the Document Identity component or the Baselines component.

---

# 13. Template Specialization

## 13.1. Definition

**Template Specialization** is the controlled derivation of a more specific Template from an existing Template.

A specialized Template preserves the applicable semantics of its source Template while introducing controlled specialization.

Conceptually:

```text

              Base Template
                    │
              specialization
                    │
                    ▼

           Specialized Template

```

Specialization must not create an unrelated duplicate Template.

It is an explicit mechanism for reuse and controlled refinement.

---

**Template Specialization** is the controlled derivation of a more specific Template from an existing Template.

A specialized Template preserves the applicable semantics of its source Template while introducing controlled specialization.

Conceptually:

```text

              Base Template
                    │
              specialization
                    │
                    ▼

           Specialized Template

```

Specialization must not create an unrelated duplicate Template.

It is an explicit mechanism for reuse and controlled refinement.

---

# 14. Template Composition

## 14.1. Definition

**Template Composition** is the construction of a Template by combining reusable Template structures or elements.

Composition supports modular Template design and reuse.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A ─┐
                        │
                        ├──►  Composite Template
                        │
            Template B ─┘

```

Composition must preserve the semantic identity and constraints of the participating structures.

---

## 14.1. Definition

**Template Composition** is the construction of a Template by combining reusable Template structures or elements.

Composition supports modular Template design and reuse.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A ─┐
                        │
                        ├──►  Composite Template
                        │
            Template B ─┘

```

Composition must preserve the semantic identity and constraints of the participating structures.

---

# 16. Relationship Between Core Concepts

The principal conceptual relationships can be summarized as follows:

```text
    
            Template
            │
            ├── has Template Type
            │
            ├── has Template Structure
            │   │
            │   ├── contains Template Sections
            │   │
            │   └── contains Template Elements
            │
            ├── conforms to Template Schema
            │
            ├── may define Template Parameters
            │
            ├── is governed by Template Constraints
            │
            ├── evolves through Template Versions
            │
            ├── may participate in Template Relationships
            │
            ├── may be specialized
            │
            ├── may be composed
            │
            └── may produce Template Instances

```

A Template Instance is a concrete application of a Template:

```text

                 Template
                    │
             instantiated as
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
                structures
                    │
                    ▼

                 Document

```

---

# 17. Relationship with Other Components

## 17.1. Metadata

Templates define how metadata structures may be represented within documentation.

Templates do not define the meaning or governance of Metadata itself.

The Metadata component remains authoritative for metadata concepts and responsibilities.

## 17.2. Document Identity

Templates may provide a structural location for document identity information.

Templates do not assign, generate, preserve, or govern document identities.

Document Identity remains authoritative for documentary identity.

## 17.3. Classification

Templates may define structures compatible with particular classifications.

Templates do not classify documents.

Classification remains responsible for classification concepts and rules.

## 17.4. Workflow

Templates may provide structures required by workflow-managed documentation.

Templates do not define workflow states, transitions, approvals, or operational processes.

## 17.5. Validation

Templates define structural requirements that can be evaluated by validation mechanisms.

The Templates component defines the applicable conceptual constraints; the Validation architecture is responsible for validation mechanisms.

## 17.6. Automation

Templates provide reusable structures that may be consumed by automation.

Templates do not define automation mechanisms.

# 18. Conceptual Boundaries

The following distinctions are fundamental.

| Concept                     | Responsibility                                             |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Template**                | Defines reusable documentation structure                   |
| **Template Type**           | Defines the conceptual category of a Template              |
| **Template Structure**      | Defines structural organization                            |
| **Template Element**        | Defines a structural or semantic unit                      |
| **Template Section**        | Organizes related structures hierarchically                |
| **Template Schema**         | Defines valid structural composition                       |
| **Template Instance**       | Represents a concrete application of a Template            |
| **Template Parameter**      | Enables controlled Template variation                      |
| **Template Constraint**     | Restricts valid Template structure or use                  |
| **Template Version**        | Identifies a controlled Template state                     |
| **Template Relationship**   | Defines explicit associations between Template concepts    |
| **Template Specialization** | Derives a more specific Template from an existing Template |
| **Template Composition**    | Combines reusable Template structures                      |
| **Template Conformance**    | Establishes compliance with applicable requirements        |

These concepts must not absorb responsibilities belonging to other Documentation Framework components.

---

# 19. Conceptual Principles

The Templates component shall apply the following principles to its conceptual model.

## 19.1. Reusability

Templates shall be defined for reuse rather than for a single document instance.

## 19.2. Explicit Semantics

Every Template concept shall have an explicit and stable meaning.

## 19.3. Structural Separation

Template structure shall remain distinct from document content and physical storage.

## 19.4. Responsibility Separation

Templates shall not assume responsibilities belonging to Metadata, Document Identity, Classification, Workflow, Policies, Registry, Baselines, or other components.

## 19.5. Technology Independence

Template concepts shall remain independent of specific markup languages, software platforms, repositories, or implementation technologies.

## 19.6. Controlled Variation

Variation shall be expressed through explicit mechanisms such as parameters, specialization, and composition rather than uncontrolled duplication.

## 19.7. Traceability

Template evolution and relationships shall remain identifiable and traceable.

## 19.8. Architectural Consistency

Template concepts shall remain consistent with the Layered Architecture and established Documentation Framework terminology.

Variation shall be expressed through explicit mechanisms such as parameters, specialization, and composition rather than uncontrolled duplication.

## 19.7. Traceability

Template evolution and relationships shall remain identifiable and traceable.

## 19.8. Architectural Consistency

Template concepts shall remain consistent with the Layered Architecture and established Documentation Framework terminology.

---

# 20. Conceptual Invariants

The following invariants apply to the Templates conceptual model:

1. A Template is not a Document Instance.
2. A Template Instance is not the Template definition.
3. Template Structure is independent of physical storage.
4. Template Elements are defined within Template Structures.
5. Template Schemas constrain valid Template Structures.
6. Template Constraints restrict valid Template composition or use.
7. Template specialization must preserve applicable inherited semantics.
8. Template composition must preserve explicit component semantics.
9. Template concepts must not redefine concepts owned by other components.
10. Template evolution must remain controlled and traceable.

---

# 21. Conceptual Model Summary

The Templates component establishes a layered conceptual model:

```text

                             Template
                                │
               ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
               │                │                │
            Template         Template         Template
              Type          Structure          Schema
                                │
                   ┌────────────┴────────────┐
                   │                         │
           Template Sections         Template Elements
                   │
                   ▼

          Template Parameters
                   │
                   ▼

          Template Constraints
                   │
                   ▼

           Template Instance
                   │
                   ▼

                Document

```

Templates may additionally participate in controlled:

```text

    Specialization
    Composition
    Relationships
    Versioning
    Conformance

```

This model provides the conceptual foundation for the subsequent structural and behavioral documentation of the Templates component.

## 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the structural model of the **Templates** component of the Documentation Framework.

It formalizes the relationships and structural dependencies between the concepts defined in **DF-TPL-002 — Template Concepts**, establishing a coherent model for representing templates, their structures, elements, schemas, parameters, constraints, versions, instances, specialization, composition, and conformance.

The model provides the structural foundation for the subsequent Template documentation documents.

# 2. Model Position

The Template Model belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

Templates operate as reusable structural definitions for documentation.

The model establishes the relationship between a template and the structural artifacts required to apply that template to documentation.

At a high level:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Template Type
            │
            ├── Template Structure
            │   │
            │   └── Template Section
            │       │
            │       └── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Schema
            │
            ├── Template Parameter
            │
            ├── Template Constraint
            │
            ├── Template Version
            │
            ├── Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Template Specialization
            │
            ├── Template Composition
            │
            └── Template Instance

```

The model describes conceptual structures and relationships. It does not prescribe a physical repository, file format, programming language, serialization mechanism, or storage technology.

---

# 4. Template Model Overview

The model consists of several related structural areas.

```text

                                      ┌───────────────────┐
                                      │   Template Type   │
                                      └─────────┬─────────┘
                                                │
                                            classifies
                                                │
                                                ▼

                ┌────────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
                │ Template       ├──────┤              │
                │ Relationship   │      │   Template   │
                └────────────────┘      │              │
                                        └──────┬───────┘
                                               │
                        ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
                        │                      │                      │
                        ▼                      ▼                      ▼

                Template Structure      Template Schema        Template Version
                        │
                        │
             ┌──────────┴──────────┐
             │                     │
             ▼                     ▼

      Template Section     Template Element
             │
             │
             └──────────────────────┐
                                    │
                                    ▼

                            Template Parameter
                                    │
                                    ▼

                           Template Constraint

                 Template
                    │
                    ▼

         Template Specialization
                    │
                    ▼

           Template Composition

                 Template
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
                    ▼

               Conformance

```

This overview represents conceptual relationships rather than implementation structures.

---

# 5. Core Model Entities

## 5.1. Template

The **Template** is the central entity of the model.

A Template represents a reusable definition of documentation structure.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Type
            │
            ├── Structure
            │
            ├── Schema
            │
            ├── Parameters
            │
            ├── Constraints
            │
            ├── Versions
            │
            ├── Relationships
            │
            ├── Specializations
            │
            ├── Composition
            │
            └── Instances

```

A Template defines what structural organization a conforming document should follow.

A Template does not itself constitute a Document Instance.

### 5.1.1. Template Model Responsibilities

The Template entity provides the structural root for:

* template organization;
* structural definition;
* schema association;
* parameter definition;
* constraint association;
* version management;
* template relationships;
* specialization;
* composition;
* template instantiation.

---

## 5.2. Template Type

A **Template Type** provides the conceptual classification of a Template within the Templates component.

The relationship is:

```text

              Template Type
                    │
                classifies
                    │
                    ▼

                 Template

```

A Template Type does not replace or redefine the Documentation Framework's document classification mechanisms.

It describes the type of template rather than the classification of a document instance.

---

## 5.3. Template Structure

A **Template Structure** represents the conceptual organization of a Template.

It provides the structural container for template sections and their elements.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Template Structure
                │
                └── Template Section
                    │
                    └── Template Element

```

Template Structure represents conceptual organization.

It does not represent:

* directories;
* files;
* repositories;
* storage containers;
* physical paths.

---

## 5.4. Template Section

A **Template Section** represents a logical subdivision of a Template Structure.

Sections organize template elements into meaningful structural units.

```text

            Template Structure
            │
            ├── Section
            │   │
            │   └── Element
            │
            └── Section
                │
                └── Element

```

A Template Structure may contain multiple Template Sections.

A Template Section belongs to a Template Structure.

---

## 5.5. Template Element

A **Template Element** represents a structural unit within a Template Section.

```text

            Template Section
            │
            ├── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Element
            │
            └── Template Element

```

Elements represent the atomic or logically indivisible structural components required by a template.

The detailed taxonomy and semantics of Template Elements are deferred to **DF-TPL-004 — Template Elements**.

---

## 5.6. Template Schema

A **Template Schema** represents the formal structural definition of a Template.

The schema describes the structure sufficiently to establish structural conformance.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Structure
            │
            └── Schema

```

The Template Schema is associated with the Template rather than with a particular storage or serialization technology.

Detailed schema rules are defined in **DF-TPL-005 — Template Schema**.

---

## 5.7. Template Parameter

A **Template Parameter** represents a defined point of controlled variation within a Template.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Parameter
            │   │
            │   └── Value supplied during application
            │
            └── Structure

```

Parameters allow a reusable Template to accommodate controlled differences without requiring a separate Template definition for every variation.

A parameter belongs to the Template definition.

A supplied parameter value belongs to a particular application of that Template.

---

## 5.8. Template Constraint

A **Template Constraint** represents a restriction applied to a Template, its structure, elements, parameters, or relationships.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Constraint
                │
                └── applies to Template Model component

```

Constraints establish conditions that must be respected for a Template or Template Instance to conform to the applicable Template definition.

Detailed constraint types and rules are defined in **DF-TPL-010 — Template Constraints**.

---

## 5.9. Template Version

A **Template Version** represents a controlled state in the evolution of a Template definition.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Version 1
            │
            ├── Version 2
            │
            └── Version 3

```

A Template Version belongs to the evolution of a Template.

Template Version is distinct from:

* Document Identity;
* document revision;
* document baseline;
* document instance state.

Template versioning describes the evolution of the reusable template definition, not the identity or lifecycle of documents created from it.

---

## 5.10. Template Instance

A **Template Instance** represents the concrete application of a Template to a particular documentation creation context.

```text

                 Template
                    │
                applied to
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
            │
            ├── resolved structure
            │
            ├── resolved parameters
            │
            └── applicable constraints

```

A Template Instance is not itself equivalent to a Document Instance.

It represents the application of the template definition from which documentation may be created or structured.

The Template Instance therefore provides the bridge between reusable template definition and concrete template application without transferring document-management responsibilities into Templates.

# 7. Structural Model

## 7.1. Template Structural Hierarchy

The fundamental structural hierarchy is:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Template Structure
                │
                └── Template Section
                    │
                    └── Template Element

```

This hierarchy establishes the primary organization of template content.

The hierarchy is structural rather than physical.

## 7.2. Structural Containment

The containment relationships are:

```text

    Template
        contains Template Structure

    Template Structure
        contains Template Sections

    Template Section
        contains Template Elements

```

Containment expresses structural membership.

It does not imply:

* filesystem containment;
* database containment;
* ownership by a repository;
* storage dependency.

## 7.3. Structural Ordering

Template Sections and Template Elements may have an explicitly defined structural order when ordering is significant to the Template.

The model therefore permits:

```text

            Template Structure
            │
            ├── Section [1]
            │
            ├── Section [2]
            │
            └── Section [3]

```

and:

```text

            Section [1]
            │
            ├── Element [1]
            │
            ├── Element [2]
            │
            └── Element [3]

```

Ordering is a property of the template structure and must not be inferred from physical storage order.

# 8. Template Composition Model

Template composition allows a Template to be constructed from reusable structural definitions.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            ├── Component Structure A
            │
            ├── Component Structure B
            │
            └── Component Structure C

```

Composition establishes that a Template may incorporate structures defined by other Templates or reusable template structures where permitted by the applicable model rules.

Composition must preserve:

* structural clarity;
* semantic consistency;
* explicit dependencies;
* conformance;
* responsibility boundaries.

Composition must not create implicit dependencies that cannot be represented by the Template Model.

Detailed composition rules are part of the subsequent Templates specification.

---

# 9. Specialization Model

Template specialization represents the derivation of a more specific Template from an existing Template.

```text

              Base Template
                    │
               specializes
                    │
                    ▼

           Specialized Template

```

A specialized Template retains the applicable structural semantics of its base Template while introducing permitted specialization.

The relationship can be represented as:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── specialization  ─────►  Template B

```

Specialization must be explicit.

It must not be inferred solely from similarity between Templates.

A specialized Template remains a distinct Template definition.

---

# 10. Parameterization Model

Parameterization provides controlled variation within a Template.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Parameter A
            │
            ├── Parameter B
            │
            └── Parameter C

```

A parameter consists conceptually of:

```text

            Parameter
            │
            ├── Definition
            │
            ├── Expected value characteristics
            │
            ├── Structural or semantic applicability
            │
            └── Constraint association

```

During template application:

```text

           Template Definition
                    │
                    ├── Parameter Definitions
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
            │
            └── Parameter Values

```

Parameter definitions belong to the Template.

Parameter values belong to a particular Template Instance or application context.

This distinction prevents mutable application values from altering the Template definition itself.

---

# 11. Constraint Model

Constraints may apply at different structural levels.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Template-level constraint
            │
            ├── Structure-level constraint
            │
            ├── Section-level constraint
            │
            ├── Element-level constraint
            │
            ├── Parameter-level constraint
            │
            └── Relationship-level constraint

```

The model therefore treats constraints as associated structural restrictions rather than as independent document-management policies.

Constraints may define conditions such as:

* required structural components;
* permitted structural relationships;
* cardinality;
* ordering;
* parameter applicability;
* composition restrictions;
* specialization restrictions;
* conformance conditions.

Detailed constraint semantics are defined in **DF-TPL-010 — Template Constraints**.

---

# 12. Version Model

Template evolution is represented through Template Versions.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Version 1
            │
            ├── Version 2
            │
            └── Version 3

```

A Template Version represents a controlled state of the Template definition.

A version may affect:

* Template Structure;
* Template Schema;
* Template Elements;
* Parameters;
* Constraints;
* Relationships;
* Composition;
* Specialization rules.

Version changes must preserve the distinction between:

```text

            Template Version
            │
            └── evolution of Template definition

            Document Revision
            │
            └── evolution of Document Instance

```

These are separate concepts belonging to different responsibilities.

Detailed lifecycle semantics are defined in **DF-TPL-006 — Template Lifecycle**.

---

# 13. Instance Model

Template application produces a Template Instance.

```text

                 Template
                    │
               instantiate
                    │
                    ▼
   
            Template Instance
            │
            │
            ├── Template Version
            │
            ├── resolved Structure
            │
            ├── resolved Parameters
            │
            └── applicable Constraints

```

A Template Instance is associated with the Template definition from which it was produced.

The instance may resolve:

* the applicable Template Version;
* parameter values;
* structural composition;
* specialization;
* applicable constraints.

The instance does not acquire responsibility for:

* assigning document identity;
* managing document metadata;
* classifying documents;
* approving documents;
* publishing documents;
* storing documents.

Those responsibilities belong to other Documentation Framework components or systems.

---

# 14. Conformance Model

Conformance expresses whether a Template Instance satisfies the structural requirements of the applicable Template definition.

Conceptually:

```text

                 Template
                    │
                 defines
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Schema
                    │
                constrains
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
              evaluated for
                    │
                    ▼

               Conformance

```

Conformance may consider:

* required structure;
* permitted structure;
* element presence;
* structural relationships;
* parameter validity;
* applicable constraints;
* composition;
* specialization;
* Template Version compatibility.

Conformance is a property of the relationship between an applied template structure and its defining template.

Operational validation procedures are defined separately in **DF-TPL-007 — Template Validation**.

---

# 15. Cross-Component Model Boundaries

The Template Model interacts with other Documentation Framework components without absorbing their responsibilities.

| Component                      | Relationship with Template Model                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Metadata**                   | Templates may define structures in which metadata is represented or expected, but Templates do not define the Metadata component        |
| **Document Identity**          | Templates may provide structural locations for identity information, but Templates do not assign or govern document identity            |
| **Classification**             | Templates may be associated with structural expectations related to document classification, but Templates do not define classification |
| **Workflow**                   | Templates may be used by workflow activities, but Templates do not define workflow                                                      |
| **Policies**                   | Template constraints are structural constraints and are distinct from governance policies                                               |
| **Registry**                   | Templates may be referenced by registry mechanisms, but Templates do not manage registration                                            |
| **Validation**                 | Templates provide conformance requirements; validation mechanisms determine whether those requirements are satisfied                    |
| **Automation**                 | Templates may be consumed by automated generation or validation mechanisms, but do not define automation                                |
| **Document Management System** | A DMS may apply Templates when managing document instances, but Template Model remains independent of operational document management   |

The central boundary is:

```text

            Templates
            │
            ├──────  define reusable documentation structure
            │
            X  ────  do not manage documentation operations

```

---

# 16. Model Invariants

The Template Model establishes the following invariants.

## 16.1. Template Identity Independence

A Template is conceptually independent of:

* filenames;
* directory paths;
* repositories;
* storage systems;
* serialization formats.

## 16.2. Structural Independence

Template Structure represents conceptual organization and must not depend on a particular physical representation.

## 16.3. Definition/Application Separation

A Template definition and a Template Instance are distinct entities.

```text

         Template

            !=

     Template Instance

```

## 16.4. Template/Document Separation

A Template is not a Document Instance.

```text

         Template

            !=

     Document Instance

```

## 16.5. Version Separation

Template Version is distinct from document revision and document baseline.

## 16.6. Parameter Separation

Parameter definitions belong to the Template definition, while parameter values belong to a specific application context.

## 16.7. Explicit Relationships

Specialization, composition, and other Template relationships must be explicitly represented.

## 16.8. Responsibility Separation

The Template Model must not absorb responsibilities belonging to Metadata, Document Identity, Classification, Workflow, Registry, or other components.

## 16.9. Structural Consistency

A Template Structure must remain consistent with the Template definition and applicable Template Schema.

## 16.10. Conformance Determinability

The model must provide sufficient structural information for conformance to be determinable.

Specialization, composition, and other Template relationships must be explicitly represented.

## 16.8. Responsibility Separation

The Template Model must not absorb responsibilities belonging to Metadata, Document Identity, Classification, Workflow, Registry, or other components.

## 16.9. Structural Consistency

A Template Structure must remain consistent with the Template definition and applicable Template Schema.

## 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the elements that may constitute a Template Structure within the Templates component of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the conceptual taxonomy, purpose, characteristics, and structural role of Template Elements defined by the Template Model.

The objective is to provide a consistent vocabulary for describing the structural building blocks of reusable documentation Templates.

# 2. Element Model Position

Template Elements occupy the lowest structural level of the primary Template Structure.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Template Structure
                │
                └── Template Section
                    │
                    └── Template Element

```

A Template Element represents a structural unit used to define the organization or expected content of a Template.

Template Elements are conceptual objects.

They are not equivalent to:

* files;
* directories;
* database records;
* physical document objects;
* source-code constructs.

---

# 4. Element Characteristics

A Template Element may be characterized by the following conceptual properties.

| Characteristic     | Purpose                                      |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| **Element Type**   | Identifies the semantic kind of element      |
| **Name**           | Provides a human-readable designation        |
| **Description**    | Explains the element's intended purpose      |
| **Position**       | Identifies the element's structural position |
| **Order**          | Defines relative ordering when significant   |
| **Occurrence**     | Defines permitted or required repetition     |
| **Content**        | Defines the expected structural content      |
| **Parameters**     | Defines controlled variation                 |
| **Relationships**  | Defines associations with other elements     |
| **Constraints**    | Defines applicable structural restrictions   |
| **Applicability**  | Defines where or when the element applies    |

These characteristics describe the model and do not prescribe a physical representation.

---

# 5. Element Categories

Template Elements may be organized into the following conceptual categories:

```text

            Template Element
            │
            ├── Structural Element
            │
            ├── Content Element
            │
            ├── Reference Element
            │
            ├── Metadata Element
            │
            ├── Identity Element
            │
            ├── Classification Element
            │
            ├── Parameterized Element
            │
            └── Reusable Element

```

These categories describe structural roles.

They do not establish additional Documentation Framework components.

---

# 6. Structural Elements

A **Structural Element** defines organization within a Template.

Structural Elements may be used to represent:

* grouping;
* ordering;
* nesting;
* boundaries;
* structural dependencies.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Section
            │
            └── Structural Element
                │
                ├── Content Element
                │
                └── Content Element

```

Structural Elements define organization rather than document content semantics.

---

# 7. Content Elements

A **Content Element** represents an expected content-bearing part of a Template.

Examples include conceptual requirements for:

* titles;
* descriptions;
* explanatory content;
* lists;
* tables;
* examples;
* other documentation content.

The Template Element defines the structural expectation.

It does not define the actual content of a particular Document Instance.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Content Element
                │
                └── expected content

```

The actual content is supplied when the Template is applied.

---

# 9. Metadata Elements

A **Metadata Element** represents a structural location or requirement for metadata within a Template.

The Templates component does not define metadata itself.

Instead:

```text

            Metadata Component
                    │
             defines metadata
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Element
                    │
       provides structural location
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Structure

```

A Metadata Element therefore establishes how metadata may participate structurally in a Template without redefining the Metadata component.

Metadata semantics remain the responsibility of the Metadata component.

---

# 10. Identity Elements

An **Identity Element** represents a structural location or requirement for document identity information within a Template.

Templates may require or organize identity information, but they do not assign, generate, or govern document identity.

The responsibility boundary is:

```text

        Document Identity
        │
        └── defines document identity
                        │
                        ▼

       Template
       │
       └── defines structural location
                        │
                        ▼

Identity Element

```

The semantics of document identity remain defined by the Document Identity component.

---

# 11. Classification Elements

A **Classification Element** represents a structural location or requirement for classification-related information.

Templates may provide structural locations for classification information without defining classification itself.

```text

              Classification
                    │
          defines classification
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Element
                    │
         organizes representation
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Structure

```

Classification semantics remain the responsibility of the Classification component.

---

# 12. Parameterized Elements

A **Parameterized Element** is a Template Element whose structure or behavior may vary according to one or more Template Parameters.

```text

             Template Element
                    │
                    ├── Parameter
                    │
                    ▼

             Resolved Element

```

Parameterization enables controlled variation while preserving the identity of the Template itself.

A parameterized element may vary in aspects such as:

* content requirements;
* structural presence;
* naming;
* cardinality;
* optionality;
* references;
* applicable structure.

Parameter definitions belong to the Template.

Parameter values belong to the Template Instance or application context.

---

# 14. Element Composition

Template Elements may be composed into larger structures.

```text

            Template Section
            │
            ├── Element A
            │
            ├── Element B
            │   │
            │   ├── Element B.1
            │   │
            │   └── Element B.2
            │
            └── Element C

```

Composition establishes structural relationships between elements.

An element may therefore act as:

* a standalone structural unit;
* a container for subordinate elements;
* a component of a reusable structure.

Composition must preserve the semantic meaning of each participating element.

---

# 15. Element Containment

The primary containment relationship is:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Template Structure
                │
                └── Template Section
                    │
                    └── Template Element

```

An element belongs to a Template Section.

A Template Element may contain subordinate elements when hierarchical composition is permitted.

```text

            Element A
            │
            ├── Element B
            │
            └── Element C

```

Containment is conceptual and does not imply physical storage containment.

---

# 16. Element Ordering

Elements may have an explicit order within their containing structure.

```text

            Section
            │
            ├── Element 1
            │
            ├── Element 2
            │
            └── Element 3

```

Ordering may be:

* required;
* significant;
* optional;
* unconstrained.

The applicable ordering semantics are determined by the Template definition and later formalized by the Template Schema.

Physical order in a file, repository, or storage system must not be assumed to define Template order.

---

# 17. Element Occurrence

A Template Element may have an occurrence requirement.

Conceptually, occurrence may be represented as:

```text

            Element
            │
            ├── minimum occurrence
            │
            └── maximum occurrence

```

This permits structural requirements such as:

```text

    Required element
        minimum = 1

    Optional element
        minimum = 0

    Repeatable element
        maximum > 1

    Single element
        maximum = 1

```

Exact occurrence semantics belong to the Template Schema and Constraint definitions.

---

# 18. Element Optionality

An element may be:

* required;
* optional;
* conditionally applicable.

```text

    Required
        ─────►  must be present

    Optional
        ─────►  may be present

    Conditional
        ─────►  presence depends on defined applicability

```

Optionality is a structural property.

It must not be confused with workflow state, document approval, or policy enforcement.

---

# 20. Element Relationships

Template Elements may participate in explicit relationships.

Examples include:

```text

            Element A
            │
            ├── contains     ─────►  Element B
            │
            ├── references   ─────►  Element C
            │
            ├── depends on   ─────►  Element D
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Element E

```

Relationships express structural or semantic associations.

They must not be inferred from physical proximity.

Detailed relationship types are defined by **DF-TPL-009 — Template Relationships**.

---

# 22. Element and Template Schema

Template Elements provide the conceptual structures that are subsequently represented by the Template Schema.

```text

            Template Elements
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Structure
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Schema

```

The Template Schema formalizes the structural rules required to represent and evaluate a Template.

This document therefore defines the elements conceptually without prescribing schema syntax.

Schema representation is defined by **DF-TPL-005 — Template Schema**.

---

# 23. Element and Template Instance

When a Template is applied, Template Elements participate in the resulting Template Instance.

```text

             Template Element
                    │
         applied through Template
                    │
                    ▼

        Template Instance Element

```

The application may resolve:

* parameters;
* optional elements;
* conditional elements;
* composition;
* specialization;
* applicable constraints.

The resulting structure belongs to the Template Instance.

The Template definition itself remains unchanged by a particular application.

---

# 24. Element Lifecycle Considerations

Template Elements evolve as part of the Template definition.

An element may be:

* introduced;
* modified;
* deprecated;
* replaced;
* removed.

Element evolution is governed by the lifecycle of the containing Template and its Template Versions.

```text

            Template Version 1
                    │
                    ├── Element A
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Version 2
            │
            ├── Element A
            │
            └── Element B

```

Detailed lifecycle rules are defined by **DF-TPL-006 — Template Lifecycle**.

---

# 25. Element Responsibility Boundaries

Template Elements must remain within the responsibility of Templates.

| Concern                            | Template Element Responsibility |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Structural organization**        | Defines                         |
| **Structural content expectation** | Defines                         |
| **Reusable structure**             | Supports                        |
| **Parameterization**               | Supports                        |
| **Element relationships**          | Represents                      |
| **Structural constraints**         | Associates                      |
| **Metadata semantics**             | Does not define                 |
| **Document identity semantics**    | Does not define                 |
| **Classification semantics**       | Does not define                 |
| **Workflow**                       | Does not define                 |
| **Repository organization**        | Does not define                 |
| **Document storage**               | Does not define                 |
| **Document lifecycle**             | Does not define                 |

This separation preserves the independence of Documentation Framework components.

---

# 26. Element Model Invariants

The following invariants apply to Template Elements.

## 26.1. Structural Membership

A Template Element belongs to a Template Structure through a Template Section or permitted structural composition.

## 26.2. Explicit Semantics

Every Template Element must have an identifiable structural purpose.

## 26.3. Explicit Relationships

Relationships between elements must be explicit when they affect structural or semantic interpretation.

## 26.4. Definition/Application Separation

A Template Element definition must remain distinct from its representation within a Template Instance.

## 26.5. Component Responsibility

Template Elements must not redefine concepts owned by other Documentation Framework components.

## 26.6. Physical Independence

Template Elements must remain independent of physical storage, repository, filename, directory, and serialization technology.

## 26.7. Controlled Variation

Variation between applications must be represented through established mechanisms such as Template Parameters, specialization, composition, or applicable structural rules.

## 26.8. Conformance Support

The element model must provide sufficient information for applicable structural conformance to be determined.

---

```text
                        ├── Content
                        │
                        ├── Reference

                        ├── Metadata-related
                        │
                        ├── Identity-related
                        │
                        ├── Classification-related
                        │
                        ├── Parameterized
                        │
                        └── Reusable

```

The element model provides the structural vocabulary required to describe reusable Templates while preserving the responsibility boundaries established by the Documentation Framework architecture.
