## 1. Introduction

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the **Template Schema** of the Documentation Framework.

The Template Schema provides the structural representation required to describe a Template according to the concepts and relationships defined by the Templates component.

It establishes how a Template, its structural components, and their associations are represented at schema level.

The Template Schema is technology-independent and does not prescribe a particular serialization format, implementation technology, storage mechanism, or repository structure.

### 1.2. Scope

This document defines the structural schema for:

* Templates;
* Template Types;
* Template Structures;
* Template Sections;
* Template Elements;
* Template Parameters;
* Template Constraints;
* Template Relationships;
* Template Versions;
* structural references between Template components;
* structural representation of Template composition;
* structural representation of Template specialization;
* structural representation of Template Instances.

This document does not define the detailed semantics of:

* Template lifecycle;
* Template validation;
* Template governance;
* Template relationships;
* Template constraints;
* Template extensibility.

Those concerns are defined by the corresponding Templates component documents.

### 1.3. Schema Position

The Template Schema is the structural representation of the Template Model.

The conceptual progression is:

```text

            Template Concepts
                    │
                    ▼

              Template Model
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Elements
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Schema
            │
            ├───▶  Template Lifecycle
            │
            ├───▶  Template Validation
            │
            ├───▶  Template Governance
            │
            ├───▶  Template Relationships
            │
            ├───▶  Template Constraints
            │
            └───▶  Template Extensibility

```

The distinction is therefore:

| Level             | Responsibility                                                  |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Concepts**      | Defines what Template concepts mean                             |
| **Model**         | Defines conceptual entities and their relationships             |
| **Elements**      | Defines the categories and characteristics of Template Elements |
| **Schema**        | Defines their structural representation                         |
| **Validation**    | Determines whether representations conform                      |
| **Governance**    | Defines controlled management                                   |
| **Relationships** | Defines relationship semantics                                  |
| **Constraints**   | Defines constraint semantics                                    |
| **Extensibility** | Defines extension mechanisms                                    |

```text
            │
            ├── ClassificationElement
            │
            ├── ParameterizedElement
            │
            └── ReusableElement

```

The schema identifies the applicable Element category and represents the properties required for its structural position.

The schema does not redefine the semantics of these categories.

---

## 5. Structural Representation

### 5.1. Containment

The principal structural containment hierarchy is:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Structure
                │
                └── Section
                    │
                    └── Element

```

Containment establishes structural membership.

It does not imply:

* physical containment;
* storage ownership;
* repository ownership;
* document ownership.

### 5.2. Structural References

Not every relationship between Template entities is represented through containment.

Entities may therefore be connected through explicit references.

```text

Template
    │
    ├── Structure
    │
    └── References
          │
          └── Target Entity

```

References must identify the intended schema entity without depending on physical storage location.

## 6. Template Section Schema

A Section is represented by a structural definition containing the information necessary to identify and position the Section.

Abstract representation:

```text

            TemplateSection
            │
            ├── Identifier
            │
            ├── Name
            │
            ├── Position
            │
            ├── Applicability
            │
            └── Elements

```

### 6.1. Identifier

The Section Identifier distinguishes the Section within its applicable Template Structure.

### 6.2. Name

The Section Name provides the human-readable name of the Section.

### 6.3. Position

Position represents the Section's structural ordering when ordering applies.

### 6.4. Applicability

Applicability identifies whether and under which conditions the Section participates in the Template structure.

Detailed applicability semantics are outside the scope of this schema document.

### 6.5. Elements

Elements represent the components contained by the Section.

## 7. Template Element Schema

A Template Element is structurally represented according to its category and applicable properties.

Abstract representation:

```text

            TemplateElement
            │
            ├── Category
            │
            ├── Identifier
            │
            ├── Name
            │
            ├── Position
            │
            ├── Occurrence
            │
            ├── Applicability
            │
            ├── Content
            │
            ├── Parameters
            │
            ├── Constraints
            │
            └── Relationships

```

Not every property is applicable to every Element.

The applicable representation is determined by the Element category and Template definition.

### 7.1. Element Category

The category identifies the structural role of the Element.

### 7.2. Identifier

The Element Identifier provides a stable reference within the Template Schema.

### 7.3. Name

The Element Name provides the human-readable name of the Element.

### 7.4. Position

Position represents the Element's structural order within its parent structure when ordering applies.

### 7.5. Occurrence

Occurrence represents the permitted number of occurrences of the Element.

### 7.6. Applicability

Applicability identifies whether the Element participates in the Template Structure and, where applicable, the conditions under which it applies.

### 7.7. Content

Content represents the content definition associated with a Content Element or another Element for which content is applicable.

The schema does not prescribe a concrete content format.

## 8. Ordering Representation

Ordering represents the relative structural position of Sections and Elements.

Example:

```text

            Template Structure
            │
            ├── Section A  [Position 1]
            │
            ├── Section B  [Position 2]
            │
            └── Section C  [Position 3]

```

Within a Section:

```text

            Section
            │
            ├── Element A  [Position 1]
            │
            ├── Element B  [Position 2]
            │
            └── Element C  [Position 3]

```

Ordering is semantic structural information.

It must not be interpreted as:

* file-system order;
* directory order;
* serialization order;
* database record order.

A concrete implementation may serialize components in another order provided that the defined structural ordering remains recoverable.

---

## 9. Occurrence Representation

Occurrence defines the allowed number of instances of a structural component.

Abstract representation:

```text

            Occurrence
            │
            ├── Minimum
            │
            └── Maximum

```

Occurrence may represent:

* mandatory components;
* optional components;
* repeated components;
* bounded repetition;
* unbounded repetition.

Examples:

```text

    Required:
        Minimum = 1
        Maximum = 1

    Optional:
        Minimum = 0
        Maximum = 1

    Repeated:
        Minimum = 0
        Maximum = *

```

These examples illustrate structural representation only.

Detailed occurrence constraint semantics belong to the Template Constraints documentation.

---

## 10. Parameter Schema

A Template Parameter represents controlled variation within a Template.

The schema represents the parameter definition.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── TemplateParameter
                │
                ├── Name
                │
                ├── Definition
                │
                ├── Applicability
                │
                └── Constraints

```

The distinction between definition and value is maintained:

```text

            Template Schema
            │
            └── Parameter Definition
                        │
                        ▼

                Template Instance
                │
                └── Parameter Value

```

The Template Schema therefore defines what may vary without defining the concrete value selected for a particular Template Instance.

The schema does not prescribe a programming-language type system or parameter implementation.

---

## 11. Constraint Representation

The Template Schema represents constraints as associations between a constraint definition and its target.

Abstract representation:

```text

            TemplateConstraint
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            └── Definition

```

Possible targets include:

```text

Template
Section
Element
Parameter
Relationship

```

The schema establishes where a constraint applies.

It does not define:

* constraint semantics;
* constraint evaluation;
* validation algorithms;
* validation results;
* enforcement mechanisms.

Those concerns are defined by DF-TPL-010 and DF-TPL-007.

---

## 12. Relationship Representation

The Template Schema represents relationships independently from structural containment.

Abstract representation:

```text

            TemplateRelationship
            │
            ├── Source
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            └── Definition

```

This permits a relationship to connect entities that do not have a parent-child relationship.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── relationship  ─────►  Template B

```

or:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── relationship  ─────►  Element B

```

The schema defines the structural representation of the association.

Detailed relationship semantics and relationship categories are defined by DF-TPL-009.

---

## 13. Template Composition Representation

Template Composition permits a Template Structure to incorporate reusable structures from another Template or reusable Template component.

Abstract representation:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── Structure
                │
                └── Composition Reference
                              │
                              ▼

                     Template B Structure

```

The schema represents the composition reference and its structural position.

It does not define:

* composition resolution algorithms;
* composition conflict resolution;
* composition precedence;
* implementation mechanisms.

Those concerns belong to the applicable Templates behavior and extensibility documentation.

---

## 14. Template Specialization Representation

Template Specialization represents a Template derived from another Template while preserving the conceptual relationship between them.

Abstract representation:

```text

              Base Template

                    ▲
                    │
               specializes
                    │
           Specialized Template

```

The schema represents the reference to the specialized Template's source Template.

Specialization does not imply that the specialized Template is a new unrelated Template.

Detailed specialization rules are addressed by the Templates component's extensibility model.

---

## 15. Template Version Representation

The schema identifies the Template Version associated with the represented Template definition.

Abstract representation:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── TemplateVersion
                │
                └── VersionIdentifier

```

Template Version represents the evolution state of the Template definition.

It is distinct from:

```text

    Template Version
           !=
    Document Identity

    Template Version
           !=
    Document Revision

    Template Version
           !=
    Document Edition

    Template Version
           !=
        Baseline

```

A document created using a particular Template Version retains its own Document Identity independently of the Template Version.

---

## 16. Template Instance Representation

A Template Instance represents a concrete application of a Template.

The structural relationship is:

```text

                 Template
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Schema
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance

```

A Template Instance may contain concrete:

* content;
* parameter values;
* structural occurrences;
* applicable sections;
* applicable elements.

The Template Instance must remain distinguishable from the Template definition.

```text

           Template Definition
                    │
            defines structure
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
          represents application
                    │
                    ▼

            Document Instance

```

The Templates component does not assign Document Identity to the resulting Document Instance.

---

## 18. Schema Invariants

The following invariants apply to the Template Schema.

### 18.1. Template Root Invariant

Every Template Schema has one Template as its root conceptual entity.

### 18.2. Structure Invariant

Every represented Section belongs to a Template Structure.

### 18.3. Element Context Invariant

Every represented Element has a defined structural context.

### 18.4. Reference Resolution Invariant

Every schema reference identifies a resolvable schema entity.

### 18.5. Parameter Resolution Invariant

Every parameter reference corresponds to a defined Template Parameter.

### 18.6. Relationship Invariant

Every represented relationship identifies its participating entities.

### 18.7. Occurrence Invariant

Occurrence information is associated with the structural component to which it applies.

### 18.8. Version Invariant

Every Template Schema identifies the Template Version represented by the schema.

### 18.9. Semantic Preservation Invariant

The schema representation must preserve the semantics established by the Template Model.

### 18.10. Responsibility Invariant

The Template Schema must not assume responsibility for concepts owned by other Documentation Framework components.

### 18.11. Technology Independence Invariant

The schema must remain independent of any particular implementation technology, serialization format, repository, or storage mechanism.

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the relationship model used by the Templates component of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the semantic meaning, participants, categories, directionality, cardinality, and representation of relationships between Templates and their structural elements.

The purpose of the relationship model is to provide an explicit and consistent mechanism for expressing how Templates, Template Structures, Template Sections, and Template Elements are related.

# 3. Relationship Model

A **Template Relationship** represents an explicitly defined relationship between two Template model entities.

A relationship has:

* a source participant;
* a target participant;
* a relationship type;
* a direction;
* a defined semantic meaning;
* an applicable cardinality;
* an optional set of additional properties.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Source
            │
            ├── Relationship Type
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Direction
            │
            ├── Cardinality
            │
            └── Applicability

```

The relationship model does not require a particular serialization or implementation technology.

---

# 4. Relationship Participants

Template Relationships may involve entities defined by the Template Model.

The principal participants are:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Template Structure
            │
            ├── Template Section
            │
            ├── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Parameter
            │
            ├── Template Constraint
            │
            ├── Template Version
            │
            └── Template Instance

```

Not every entity participates in every relationship category.

The most important relationship participants are:

* Template;
* Template Structure;
* Template Section;
* Template Element.

Template Version provides version context for relationships but does not replace the relationship between the underlying entities.

Template Instance represents an application of a Template and is therefore treated separately from relationships between Template definitions.

---

# 5. Relationship Representation

A relationship should be conceptually representable by the following structure:

```text

            Relationship
            │
            ├── Source
            │
            ├── Type
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Direction
            │
            ├── Cardinality
            │
            └── Applicability

```

Where:

| Property          | Meaning                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **Source**        | Entity from which the relationship originates    |
| **Type**          | Semantic category of the relationship            |
| **Target**        | Entity toward which the relationship is directed |
| **Direction**     | Directional interpretation of the relationship   |
| **Cardinality**   | Number of permitted participants                 |
| **Applicability** | Conditions under which the relationship applies  |

Additional properties may be introduced by the Template Schema and Constraint models.

Relationship representation must not imply a particular database, file format, programming language, or repository structure.

---

# 6. Relationship Categories

Template Relationships are classified according to their semantic purpose.

The principal categories are:

```text

            Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Containment
            │
            ├── Reference
            │
            ├── Dependency
            │
            ├── Composition
            │
            ├── Specialization
            │
            └── Association

```

## 6.1. Containment Relationship

A **Containment Relationship** expresses structural membership of one Template entity within another.

Examples include:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Structure

            Template Structure
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Section

            Template Section
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

Containment defines structural ownership within a Template Structure.

The detailed schema representation of containment is defined by DF-TPL-005.

## 6.2. Reference Relationship

A **Reference Relationship** expresses an explicit link to another Template entity without making the target a structural child.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Template B

```

A reference does not imply:

* containment;
* composition;
* specialization;
* physical co-location.

References provide explicit semantic linkage without changing structural ownership.

## 6.3. Dependency Relationship

A **Dependency Relationship** indicates that one Template or Template Element relies on another Template entity for a defined purpose.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Template B

```

Dependency does not by itself imply composition or specialization.

The existence and semantics of a dependency must remain explicit.

## 6.4. Composition Relationship

A **Composition Relationship** expresses that a Template incorporates another Template or Template Structure as part of its reusable structure.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

```

Composition is stronger than a simple reference because the target contributes structurally to the resulting Template.

Composition is a defined reuse mechanism of the Template Model.

## 6.5. Specialization Relationship

A **Specialization Relationship** expresses that one Template derives from another Template while preserving its general semantic basis.

Conceptually:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── specialized by  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The specialized Template may extend, restrict, or otherwise refine the structure of the base Template subject to the applicable Template Constraints.

Specialization is distinct from Composition:

```text

            Specialization
                Base Template
                │
                └─────►  Derived Template

            Composition
                Template A
                │
                └─────►  incorporates Template B

```

## 6.6. Association Relationship

An **Association Relationship** expresses a semantic relationship between Template entities that does not correspond to containment, reference, dependency, composition, or specialization.

Association provides a general relationship category for explicit semantic links that require representation without implying stronger structural semantics.

---

## 6.1. Containment Relationship

A **Containment Relationship** expresses structural membership of one Template entity within another.

Examples include:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Structure

            Template Structure
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Section

            Template Section
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

Containment defines structural ownership within a Template Structure.

The detailed schema representation of containment is defined by DF-TPL-005.

## 6.2. Reference Relationship

A **Reference Relationship** expresses an explicit link to another Template entity without making the target a structural child.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Template B

```

A reference does not imply:

* containment;
* composition;
* specialization;
* physical co-location.

References provide explicit semantic linkage without changing structural ownership.

## 6.3. Dependency Relationship

A **Dependency Relationship** indicates that one Template or Template Element relies on another Template entity for a defined purpose.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Template B

```

Dependency does not by itself imply composition or specialization.

The existence and semantics of a dependency must remain explicit.

## 6.4. Composition Relationship

A **Composition Relationship** expresses that a Template incorporates another Template or Template Structure as part of its reusable structure.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

```

Composition is stronger than a simple reference because the target contributes structurally to the resulting Template.

Composition is a defined reuse mechanism of the Template Model.

## 6.5. Specialization Relationship

A **Specialization Relationship** expresses that one Template derives from another Template while preserving its general semantic basis.

Conceptually:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── specialized by  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The specialized Template may extend, restrict, or otherwise refine the structure of the base Template subject to the applicable Template Constraints.

Specialization is distinct from Composition:

```text

            Specialization
                Base Template
                │
                └─────►  Derived Template

            Composition
                Template A
                │
                └─────►  incorporates Template B

```

## 6.6. Association Relationship

An **Association Relationship** expresses a semantic relationship between Template entities that does not correspond to containment, reference, dependency, composition, or specialization.

Association provides a general relationship category for explicit semantic links that require representation without implying stronger structural semantics.

---

# 7. Template-to-Template Relationships

Templates may have relationships with other Templates.

Examples include:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template B

```

These relationships must retain their semantic distinction.

A reference must not be interpreted as composition.

A dependency must not automatically be interpreted as specialization.

A composition must not automatically be interpreted as inheritance.

A specialization must not automatically be interpreted as physical reuse.

---

# 8. Template-to-Element Relationships

A Template may relate directly to Template Elements.

The principal structural relationship is containment:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

A Template may also establish other relationships when explicitly required by the Template Model.

For example:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Reusable Element

```

The relationship type determines the semantic interpretation.

An Element referenced by a Template is not necessarily structurally contained by that Template.

---

# 9. Element-to-Element Relationships

Template Elements may be related to other Template Elements.

Examples include:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Element B

            Element A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Element B

            Element A
            │
            └── associates with  ─────►  Element B

```

Element-to-Element relationships allow structural semantics to be represented without requiring every relationship to be expressed through a Template or Section.

Such relationships must remain explicit and must not introduce implicit containment.

---

# 10. Relationship Directionality

Relationships may be directional or conceptually symmetric.

## 10.1. Directional Relationships

Directional relationships have a defined source and target.

Examples:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template B

```

The direction is semantically significant.

Reversing the relationship changes its meaning:

```text

            Template B
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template A

```

is not equivalent to the original relationship.

## 10.2. Symmetric Associations

Some associations may be interpreted symmetrically.

For example:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── associated with  ─────►  Element B

```

When the semantics are symmetric, the relationship representation must not introduce an artificial directional meaning.

## 10.3. Inverse Interpretation

A directional relationship may have an inverse interpretation.

For example:

```text

            Derived Template
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Base Template

```

may be viewed inversely as:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── has specialization  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The inverse view does not create a second independent relationship.

```text
            Base Template
            │
            └── has specialization  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The inverse view does not create a second independent relationship.

---

# 11. Relationship Cardinality

Relationship cardinality defines how many instances of one participant may be related to another.

Typical cardinalities include:

```text

    1 : 1
    1 : N
    N : 1
    N : N

```

Examples:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Structure

```

may establish a one-to-one relationship where the Template Model requires a single Template Structure.

Conversely:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

may permit multiple Elements.

Cardinality is a structural property of the relationship and must be represented consistently with the Template Schema.

Detailed cardinality constraints are defined by DF-TPL-010.

---

# 12. Relationship Identity

A Template Relationship must be distinguishable from other relationships when required for traceability.

Relationship identity may be established by its conceptual combination of:

```text

                  Source
                    +
            Relationship Type
                    +
                  Target
                    +
        Applicable Version Context

```

The exact technical representation of relationship identity is implementation-independent.

Relationship identity must support:

* traceability;
* validation;
* controlled evolution;
* relationship-specific governance where required.

---

# 13. Relationship Version Context

Relationships may exist in the context of a specific Template Version.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Version
            │
            └── defines  ─────►  Relationship

```

A relationship may therefore:

* be introduced by a Template Version;
* remain unchanged across versions;
* be modified in a later version;
* become obsolete in a later version.

Template Version remains distinct from the relationship itself.

A relationship change does not create a new semantic relationship merely because the containing Template has a new version.

---

# 14. Relationship and Composition

Composition establishes a structural reuse relationship.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B
                                  │
                                  └── contributes structure

```

The composed Template may contribute:

* Sections;
* Elements;
* reusable structures;
* defined parameters;
* other reusable Template structures.

Composition must remain explicit.

A simple reference to a Template does not constitute composition.

Composition semantics must also remain compatible with Template Constraints and Template Validation.

---

# 15. Relationship and Specialization

Specialization establishes a derivational relationship between Templates.

Conceptually:

```text

          Base Template
                │
                └── specialization relationship
                    │
                    ▼

             Derived Template

```

A specialized Template retains a defined semantic relationship with its base Template.

Specialization may be used to:

* refine a general Template;
* provide a more specific Template;
* extend a reusable Template;
* establish controlled structural variation.

Specialization must not be confused with Template Version.

A new Template Version represents evolution of the same Template definition.

A specialized Template represents a distinct Template related to another Template.

---

# 16. Relationship and Validation

Relationships are subject to Template Validation.

Validation may determine whether:

* the relationship is structurally valid;
* the relationship type is applicable;
* the participants are compatible;
* cardinality requirements are satisfied;
* composition is valid;
* specialization is valid;
* referenced entities exist;
* cross-template relationships conform to applicable rules.

Validation does not define relationship semantics.

The responsibility boundary is:

```text

            Template Relationships
            │
            └── defines relationship meaning

            Template Constraints
            │
            └── defines relationship restrictions

            Template Validation
            │
            └── evaluates conformance

```

---

# 19. Cross-Component Relationship Boundaries

Template Relationships may interact with concepts defined by other Documentation Framework components.

These interactions do not transfer responsibility to Templates.

| Component             | Relationship with Templates                                                  |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Metadata**          | Templates may require metadata-related structural locations or compatibility |
| **Document Identity** | Templates may define identity-related structural locations                   |
| **Classification**    | Templates may define classification-related structural locations             |
| **Workflow**          | Workflow may operate using Template-derived structures                       |
| **Validation**        | Validation evaluates relationship conformance                                |
| **Automation**        | Automation may process Template relationships                                |
| **Registry**          | Registry may reference Templates and their relationships                     |

Templates do not define:

* metadata semantics;
* document identity semantics;
* classification semantics;
* workflow semantics;
* registry semantics;
* repository relationships.

---

# 20. Relationship Invariants

The following invariants apply to Template Relationships.

### 20.1. Invariant 1 — Explicit Semantics

Every relationship must have a defined semantic type.

### 20.2. Invariant 2 — Explicit Participants

Every relationship must identify its applicable participants.

### 20.3. Invariant 3 — Explicit Direction

A directional relationship must define its direction.

### 20.4. Invariant 4 — No Implicit Composition

A reference or dependency must not implicitly become a composition.

### 20.5. Invariant 5 — No Implicit Specialization

A composition or dependency must not implicitly become specialization.

### 20.6. Invariant 6 — Structural Consistency

Containment relationships must remain consistent with the Template Schema.

### 20.7. Invariant 7 — Version Distinction

Template Version and Template Relationship are distinct concepts.

### 20.8. Invariant 8 — Component Independence

Template Relationships must remain independent of physical storage and repository organization.

### 20.9. Invariant 9 — Responsibility Separation

Relationship definitions must not redefine concepts owned by other DF components.

### 20.10. Invariant 10 — Traceability

Relationship changes must remain traceable when required by Template governance.

---

# 23. Relationship Model Summary

The Template Relationship model provides an explicit semantic mechanism for connecting Template entities.

Its principal relationship categories are:

```text

            Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Containment
            │
            ├── Reference
            │
            ├── Dependency
            │
            ├── Composition
            │
            ├── Specialization
            │
            └── Association

```

The model distinguishes:

* structural containment from semantic association;
* reference from dependency;
* composition from specialization;
* Template relationships from Template Versions;
* relationship definition from relationship validation;
* relationship semantics from relationship constraints.

This provides the structural basis required for consistent Template reuse, composition, specialization, traceability, and controlled evolution.

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the lifecycle of Templates within the Documentation Framework.

The Template Lifecycle establishes the conceptual states through which a Template may progress during its existence and the transitions between those states.

The lifecycle provides a controlled behavioral model for the evolution of Template definitions while preserving the separation between Template definition, Template usage, Template validation, and Template governance.

## 2. Lifecycle Position

The Template Lifecycle operates on the Template definition.

The primary distinction is:

```text

            Template Definition
            │
            ├── Lifecycle
            │
            ├── Version
            │
            ├── Structure
            │
            ├── Parameters
            │
            ├── Constraints
            │
            └── Relationships

```

The lifecycle therefore concerns the existence and evolution of a Template definition.

It does not represent the lifecycle of a document created from that Template.

```text

            Template Lifecycle
                    │
                    ▼

           Template Definition
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
                    ▼

            Document Instance

```

The lifecycle of a Document Instance belongs to the appropriate document management and workflow responsibilities.

---

## 4. Lifecycle Model

The abstract Template Lifecycle is:

```text

                  ┌─────────────┐
                  │    Draft    │
                  └──────┬──────┘
                         │
                         ▼

                  ┌─────────────┐
                  │   Defined   │
                  └──────┬──────┘
                         │
                         ▼

                  ┌─────────────┐
                  │    Active   │
                  └──────┬──────┘
                         │
               ┌─────────┴─────────┐
               │                   │
               ▼                   ▼

        ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
        │  Deprecated │     │   Retired   │
        └──────┬──────┘     └─────────────┘
               │
               ▼

        ┌─────────────┐
        │   Retired   │
        └─────────────┘
```

The lifecycle represents conceptual states.

Concrete governance rules may impose additional conditions on transitions.

---

## 5. Lifecycle States

### 5.1. Draft

A Template is in the **Draft** state while its definition is under development.

A Draft Template may be incomplete.

Typical characteristics include:

* structure under development;
* elements under definition;
* parameters under definition;
* relationships under development;
* constraints under development;
* incomplete documentation.

A Draft Template is not assumed to be generally available for production use.

### 5.2. Defined

A Template is **Defined** when its structural definition has been established sufficiently to constitute a recognizable Template.

The Defined state indicates that the Template has progressed beyond initial drafting.

A Defined Template may still be subject to formal validation or governance activities.

The Defined state therefore does not, by itself, imply operational availability.

### 5.3. Active

A Template is **Active** when it is approved for its intended use within the applicable documentation context.

An Active Template may be used as the basis for Template Instances and document creation where the applicable policies permit such use.

The Active state represents the normal operational state of a Template.

### 5.4. Deprecated

A Template is **Deprecated** when it remains historically or technically relevant but is no longer the preferred Template for new use.

A Deprecated Template may remain available for:

* interpretation of existing documents;
* maintenance of existing Template Instances;
* historical reference;
* controlled migration;
* compatibility purposes.

Deprecation does not imply immediate removal.

### 5.5. Retired

A Template is **Retired** when it is no longer intended for normal use.

A Retired Template remains part of the historical Template record where preservation is required.

Retirement does not imply deletion.

A Retired Template may remain necessary to interpret documents or Template Instances created while it was Active.

---

### 5.2. Defined

A Template is **Defined** when its structural definition has been established sufficiently to constitute a recognizable Template.

The Defined state indicates that the Template has progressed beyond initial drafting.

A Defined Template may still be subject to formal validation or governance activities.

The Defined state therefore does not, by itself, imply operational availability.

### 5.3. Active

A Template is **Active** when it is approved for its intended use within the applicable documentation context.

An Active Template may be used as the basis for Template Instances and document creation where the applicable policies permit such use.

The Active state represents the normal operational state of a Template.

### 5.5. Retired

A Template is **Retired** when it is no longer intended for normal use.

A Retired Template remains part of the historical Template record where preservation is required.

Retirement does not imply deletion.

A Retired Template may remain necessary to interpret documents or Template Instances created while it was Active.

---

## 6. Lifecycle Transitions

### 6.1. Draft to Defined

The transition:

```text

                  Draft
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined

```

occurs when the Template definition has reached the level required to constitute a defined Template.

The transition does not itself imply approval for operational use.

### 6.2. Defined to Active

The transition:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Active

```

occurs when the Template has satisfied the applicable requirements for operational use.

The detailed approval and governance conditions are defined outside the lifecycle model.

### 6.3. Active to Deprecated

The transition:

```text

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated

```

occurs when a Template remains relevant but should no longer be selected as the preferred Template for new use.

Typical causes include:

* replacement by a newer Template;
* architectural evolution;
* improved Template design;
* changed documentation requirements;
* controlled migration to another Template.

### 6.4. Deprecated to Retired

The transition:

```text

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

occurs when the Template is no longer intended for normal use and its operational role has ended.

Historical preservation may still be required.

### 6.5. Active to Retired

An Active Template may transition directly to Retired when circumstances require immediate termination of normal use.

Such a transition is expected to be exceptional and subject to applicable governance.

### 6.6. Deprecated to Active

A Deprecated Template may be restored to Active when it becomes appropriate for normal use again.

```text

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active

```

This transition must preserve Template Version traceability.

### 6.7. Defined to Draft

A Defined Template may return to Draft when substantial changes are required before it can continue progressing through the lifecycle.

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Draft

```

This transition represents renewed development rather than lifecycle loss.

---

```text

                    │
                    ▼

                  Draft

```

---

## 7. Lifecycle State Semantics

Lifecycle state and Template Version are related but distinct concepts.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Lifecycle State
            │
            └── Template Version

```

A Template Version identifies the version of the Template definition.

The lifecycle state identifies the current lifecycle condition of that definition.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            ├── Version 1.0
            │
            └── State: Retired

            Template A
            │
            ├── Version 2.0
            │
            └── State: Active

```

A new Template Version does not automatically imply a lifecycle transition.

Likewise, a lifecycle transition does not inherently create a new Template Version.

The applicable versioning rules belong to the Template Version model.

---

## 8. Template Evolution

Template evolution may result in new Template Versions.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Version 1
            │
            ├── Version 2
            │
            └── Version 3

```

Lifecycle states may apply to the evolving Template definition.

A common evolution pattern is:

```text

              Version 1
              │
              └── Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated

              Version 2
              │
              └── Draft
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active

```

This allows a newer Template Version to become Active while an earlier Version becomes Deprecated.

The lifecycle therefore supports controlled Template evolution without conflating versions with lifecycle states.

---

## 9. Template Lifecycle and Template Instances

A Template Instance may remain associated with a Template Version after that Template has changed lifecycle state.

For example:

```text

            Template Version 1
            │
            ├── Deprecated
            │
            └── Template Instances created previously

```

Deprecating or retiring a Template does not inherently invalidate existing Template Instances.

This distinction is important for historical documents and traceability.

An existing document may therefore remain associated with:

```text

            Document
            │
            └── Template
                │
                └── Template Version
                    │
                    └── Historical lifecycle state

```

The Templates component preserves the structural relationship.

Document management and preservation policies determine how such historical instances are handled operationally.

---

## 10. Lifecycle and Validation

Lifecycle and validation are separate responsibilities.

The lifecycle may define that a Template must satisfy applicable conditions before entering the Active state.

However, the lifecycle does not define how those conditions are evaluated.

The separation is:

```text

            Template Lifecycle
                    │
        defines transition context
                    │
                    ▼

           Template Validation
                    │
          evaluates conformance
                    │
                    ▼

            Validation Result

```

DF-TPL-007 — Template Validation defines validation behavior.

---

## 11. Lifecycle and Governance

Lifecycle states provide the behavioral structure required for governance, but they do not define governance policies.

For example:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
           governance decision
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active

```

The lifecycle identifies the transition.

Governance defines:

* who may authorize it;
* what evidence is required;
* what approvals are necessary;
* what records must be preserved.

These responsibilities belong to DF-TPL-008 — Template Governance.

---

## 12. Lifecycle and Constraints

Template constraints may influence whether a Template can transition to a subsequent lifecycle state.

However, constraint semantics remain separate from lifecycle behavior.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Constraints
            │
            └── Lifecycle

```

DF-TPL-010 — Template Constraints defines constraint semantics.

The lifecycle only consumes the applicable result or condition; it does not redefine constraint meaning.

---

## 13. Lifecycle and Relationships

A Template may have relationships with other Templates during its lifecycle.

Examples include:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── replaces  ─────►  Template B

```

The lifecycle does not define the semantics of these relationships.

Relationship semantics belong to DF-TPL-009 — Template Relationships.

---

## 14. Lifecycle Invariants

The following invariants apply to the Template Lifecycle.

### 14.1. State Invariant

A Template has one applicable lifecycle state at a given point in its lifecycle.

### 14.2. Transition Invariant

A lifecycle state change occurs through a defined lifecycle transition.

### 14.3. Traceability Invariant

Lifecycle transitions must not destroy the historical identity of the Template or its Versions.

### 14.4. Version Separation Invariant

Lifecycle state and Template Version remain distinct concepts.

### 14.5. Instance Preservation Invariant

Changing the lifecycle state of a Template does not inherently invalidate existing Template Instances.

### 14.6. Historical Preservation Invariant

Retired Templates remain preservable when required for historical interpretation or traceability.

### 14.7. Responsibility Invariant

The lifecycle does not assume responsibility for validation, governance, storage, workflow, or document management.

### 14.8. Technology Independence Invariant

The lifecycle model remains independent of implementation technology.

## 15. Lifecycle Termination

Retirement represents the normal terminal state of a Template lifecycle.

```text

         Retired
            │
            ✘

```

A Retired Template is not normally returned to operational use.

If a previously Retired Template becomes necessary again, the preferred approach is normally to create or derive an appropriate new Template Version or Template definition rather than silently reversing its historical retirement.

Any exceptional reactivation must preserve historical traceability.

---

## 17. Lifecycle Summary

The Template Lifecycle can be summarized as:

```text

                  Draft
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

With controlled alternative transitions:

```text

    Defined     ─────►  Draft

    Deprecated  ─────►  Active

    Active      ─────►  Retired

```

The lifecycle provides:

* explicit Template states;
* controlled state transitions;
* distinction between operational and historical Templates;
* separation between lifecycle and version;
* preservation of historical Template usage;
* a behavioral basis for validation and governance.

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the validation behavior of Templates within the Documentation Framework.

Template Validation determines whether a Template, its schema, and applicable Template Instances conform to the structural and semantic requirements established by the Templates component.

Validation provides the mechanisms by which Template conformance can be evaluated without assuming responsibility for Template lifecycle, governance, storage, or document management.

## 2. Validation Position

Template Validation operates on the representations defined by the Templates component.

The principal relationship is:

```text

            Template Concepts
                    │
                    ▼

              Template Model
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Elements
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Schema
                    │
                    ▼

           Template Validation

```

Validation evaluates whether a concrete representation conforms to the applicable model, schema, constraints, and semantic requirements.

Validation therefore consumes definitions established by other Templates documents rather than redefining them.

---

## 4. Validation Targets

Template Validation may operate on different levels of the Templates model.

```text

            Validation Target
            │
            ├── Template
            │
            ├── Template Schema
            │
            ├── Template Structure
            │
            ├── Template Section
            │
            ├── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Parameter
            │
            ├── Template Relationship
            │
            └── Template Instance

```

A validation operation must identify the target against which validation is being performed.

### 4.1. Template Validation

Template validation evaluates the Template definition as a whole.

It may include:

* structural validation;
* element validation;
* schema validation;
* parameter validation;
* relationship validation;
* constraint validation;
* semantic validation.

### 4.2. Schema Validation

Schema validation evaluates whether the Template representation conforms to the Template Schema.

### 4.3. Template Instance Validation

Template Instance validation evaluates whether a concrete Template Instance conforms to the applicable Template definition.

---

### 4.2. Schema Validation

Schema validation evaluates whether the Template representation conforms to the Template Schema.

### 4.3. Template Instance Validation

Template Instance validation evaluates whether a concrete Template Instance conforms to the applicable Template definition.

---

## 5. Validation Levels

Template Validation is organized into progressively broader validation levels.

```text

                Structural
                    │
                    ▼

                 Element
                    │
                    ▼

                  Schema
                    │
                    ▼

              Compatibility
                    │
                    ▼

                 Semantic
                    │
                    ▼

              Cross-Template

```

Not every validation operation must execute every level.

The applicable levels depend on the validation target and validation context.

---

## 6. Structural Validation

Structural Validation verifies the fundamental organization of a Template representation.

It evaluates conditions such as:

* Template Structure existence;
* Section containment;
* Element containment;
* structural hierarchy;
* structural references;
* ordering representation;
* occurrence representation.

Example:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Structure
                │
                └── Section
                    │
                    └── Element

```

Structural validation determines whether this organization is structurally valid.

---

## 8. Schema Validation

Schema Validation determines whether the concrete Template representation conforms to the Template Schema.

It includes evaluation of:

* required schema components;
* structural containment;
* references;
* parameter definitions;
* relationship representations;
* version representation;
* schema invariants.

The distinction is:

```text

             Template Schema
                    │
                    ▼

               Schema Rules
                    │
                    ▼

                Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Conformance Result

```

Schema Validation evaluates representation.

It does not define the schema itself.

---

## 9. Metadata Compatibility Validation

Templates interact with the Metadata component.

Validation may therefore verify compatibility between a Template and applicable metadata requirements.

Examples include:

* required metadata locations being represented;
* metadata references resolving;
* metadata structures being compatible with the Template;
* metadata-related Template Elements being structurally consistent.

Template Validation does not redefine Metadata semantics.

Metadata remains the responsibility of the Metadata component.

---

## 10. Document Identity Compatibility Validation

Templates may contain Identity Elements that provide structural locations for document identity information.

Validation may verify that:

* required identity structures are represented;
* Identity Elements are structurally valid;
* identity-related references resolve.

Template Validation does not assign or manage Document Identity.

Document Identity remains the responsibility of the Document Identity component.

---

## 11. Classification Compatibility Validation

Templates may contain Classification Elements that provide structural locations for classification information.

Validation may verify:

* classification structures are represented;
* applicable references resolve;
* classification-related elements are structurally consistent.

Template Validation does not define document classification.

Classification remains the responsibility of the Classification component.

---

## 12. Parameter Validation

Parameter Validation evaluates the structural definition and use of Template Parameters.

It may verify:

* parameter definitions exist;
* parameter references resolve;
* required parameters are represented;
* parameter applicability is consistent;
* parameter-related constraints are satisfied.

The distinction between definition and value remains:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Parameter Definition
                         │
                         ▼

                 Template Instance
                 │
                 └── Parameter Value

```

Validation of a concrete parameter value occurs in the context of the applicable Template Instance.

---

## 13. Constraint Validation

Constraints defined for a Template are subject to validation.

The relationship is:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Constraint
                    │
                    ▼

                Validation

```

Validation evaluates whether applicable constraints are satisfied.

The detailed semantics of constraints are defined by DF-TPL-010 — Template Constraints.

Therefore, this document defines the validation behavior but does not redefine the meaning of individual constraint types.

---

## 15. Semantic Validation

Semantic Validation evaluates whether a Template representation preserves the intended meaning established by the Templates conceptual model.

Semantic validation may detect situations where a structure is technically representable but conceptually inconsistent.

Examples include:

* incompatible Template components;
* contradictory structural meanings;
* inappropriate use of Element categories;
* inconsistent parameter applicability;
* semantic conflicts between composed structures.

Semantic validation is therefore distinct from simple structural validation.

```text

     Structural Validity
             !=
      Semantic Validity

```

A Template may be structurally well-formed while still being semantically invalid.

---

## 17. Validation Sequence

A complete validation operation may follow the following conceptual sequence:

```text

      1. Identify Validation Target
                    │
                    ▼

         2. Structural Validation
                    │
                    ▼

          3. Element Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           4. Schema Validation
                    │
                    ▼

        5. Component Compatibility
                    │
                    ▼

         6. Parameter Validation
                    │
                    ▼

         7. Constraint Validation
                    │
                    ▼

        8. Relationship Validation
                    │
                    ▼

          9. Semantic Validation
                    │
                    ▼

      10. Cross-Template Validation
                    │
                    ▼

          11. Validation Result

```

The sequence is conceptual.

An implementation may optimize the execution order provided that the resulting validation semantics are preserved.

---

## 18. Validation Findings

A validation operation produces findings when one or more conditions are not satisfied.

A finding identifies, as applicable:

```text

            Validation Finding
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Category
            │
            ├── Severity
            │
            ├── Condition
            │
            ├── Description
            │
            └── Reference

```

### 18.1. Target

Identifies the Template component associated with the finding.

### 18.2. Category

Identifies the validation category that produced the finding.

Examples include:

* Structural;
* Element;
* Schema;
* Compatibility;
* Parameter;
* Constraint;
* Relationship;
* Semantic;
* Cross-Template.

### 18.3. Severity

Severity indicates the significance of the finding.

The detailed severity taxonomy may be defined by the applicable validation implementation or governance rules.

### 18.4. Condition

Identifies the condition that was not satisfied.

### 18.5. Description

Provides a human-readable explanation of the finding.

### 18.6. Reference

Identifies the applicable Template definition, schema component, constraint, relationship, or other authoritative source.

## 19. Validation Results

A validation operation produces a Validation Result.

The conceptual result states are:

```text

            Validation Result
            │
            ├── Conformant
            │
            ├── Non-Conformant
            │
            └── Indeterminate

```

### 19.1. Conformant

The validated target satisfies the applicable validation requirements.

### 19.2. Non-Conformant

One or more applicable requirements are not satisfied.

The result includes the associated validation findings.

### 19.3. Indeterminate

A conformance determination cannot be completed because required information or evaluation conditions are unavailable.

An Indeterminate result must not be interpreted as Conformant.

---

An Indeterminate result must not be interpreted as Conformant.

---

## 20. Validation Scope

Validation may be performed at different scopes.

### 20.1. Component Scope

Validation applies to one Template component.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Element

```

### 20.2. Template Scope

Validation applies to a complete Template definition.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Structure
            │
            ├── Parameters
            │
            ├── Constraints
            │
            ├── Relationships
            │
            └── Version

```

### 20.3. Template Instance Scope

Validation applies to a concrete Template Instance.

### 20.4. Cross-Template Scope

Validation applies to multiple related Templates.

The selected scope must be explicit for a validation operation.

---


### 20.4. Cross-Template Scope

Validation applies to multiple related Templates.

The selected scope must be explicit for a validation operation.

---

## 21. Validation and Lifecycle

Validation and lifecycle are separate concerns.

The lifecycle determines the behavioral state of a Template.

Validation determines conformance.

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Lifecycle State
            │
            └── Validation Result

```

A validation result does not itself constitute a lifecycle transition.

Conversely, a lifecycle transition may require validation according to applicable governance rules.

---

## 22. Validation and Governance

Governance determines how validation results may be used for lifecycle decisions.

For example:

```text

                Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Validation Result
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

           Lifecycle Transition

```

Validation does not define who may approve a Template or which governance process must be followed.

Those responsibilities belong to DF-TPL-008 — Template Governance.

---

## 23. Validation and Template Version

Validation applies to a specific Template definition and therefore to a specific Template Version where versioning is applicable.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Version
                │
                ├── Schema
                │
                └── Validation

```

A validation result must therefore be traceable to the Template Version against which validation was performed.

A validation result for one Template Version must not automatically be interpreted as a validation result for another Version.

---

## 24. Validation Invariants

The following invariants apply to Template Validation.

### 24.1. Target Invariant

Every validation operation identifies a validation target.

### 24.2. Context Invariant

Validation is performed against an explicitly applicable Template definition, schema, or validation context.

### 24.3. Traceability Invariant

Validation findings remain traceable to the validated target and applicable requirement.

### 24.4. Version Invariant

Validation results are associated with the Template Version against which validation was performed.

### 24.5. Result Invariant

Indeterminate validation must not be interpreted as conformance.

### 24.6. Responsibility Invariant

Validation does not assume responsibility for lifecycle, governance, storage, repository management, or document identity.

### 24.7. Semantic Invariant

Validation must preserve the semantics defined by the Templates component.

### 24.8. Technology Independence Invariant

The validation model remains independent of a particular implementation technology.

Template Validation provides a structured mechanism for determining Template conformance.

Its principal validation dimensions are:

```text

                Structural
                    │
                    │
                 Element
                    │
                    │
                  Schema
                    │
                    │
              Compatibility
                    │
                    │
                Parameter
                    │
                    │
                Constraint
                    │
                    │
               Relationship
                    │
                    │
                 Semantic
                    │
                    │
              Cross-Template

```

The resulting determination is:

```text

    Conformant
    Non-Conformant
    Indeterminate

```

Validation therefore provides the behavioral bridge between the structural definitions of Templates and their controlled use.

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the governance of Templates within the Documentation Framework.

Template Governance establishes the principles and behavioral rules by which Template definitions are controlled, authorized, maintained, evolved, deprecated, and retired.

Governance ensures that Templates remain consistent with the Documentation Framework architecture and that changes to Templates are controlled and traceable.

## 2. Governance Position

Template Governance operates on the Template definition and its controlled evolution.

```text

                    Template Definition
                    │
                    ├── Structure
                    │
                    ├── Elements
                    │
                    ├── Schema
                    │
                    ├── Parameters
                    │
                    ├── Constraints
                    │
                    ├── Relationships
                    │
                    ├── Version
                    │
                    ▼

           Template Governance

```

Governance controls changes to the Template while preserving the responsibilities of the other Documentation Framework components.

The relationship between lifecycle, validation, and governance is:

```text

             Template Change
                    │
                    ▼

                Validation
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

           Lifecycle Transition

```

These activities are related but remain distinct responsibilities.

---

## 4. Governance Principles

### 4.1. Controlled Evolution

Templates must evolve through controlled changes.

Uncontrolled modification of an established Template must not be considered a valid form of Template evolution.

### 4.2. Explicit Authority

Every governed Template must have a clearly identifiable authority responsible for its definition and evolution.

### 4.3. Traceability

Governed Template changes must remain traceable to their origin, decision, and resulting Template Version.

### 4.4. Preservation

Historical Template definitions must be preserved when required for interpretation, compatibility, or traceability.

### 4.5. Architectural Consistency

Template changes must remain consistent with the Documentation Framework architecture.

### 4.6. Separation of Responsibilities

Template Governance must not absorb responsibilities belonging to:

* Metadata;
* Document Identity;
* Classification;
* Workflow;
* Validation;
* Registry;
* Knowledge Graph;
* DMS;
* CMS.

### 4.7. Reuse

Existing Templates should be reused or specialized when they satisfy the applicable requirements.

New Templates should not be created solely to duplicate an existing Template.

### 4.8. Explicit Change

Changes affecting Template semantics, structure, or behavior must be explicitly identified.

### 4.8. Explicit Change

---

## 7. Template Ownership

Template ownership identifies responsibility for maintaining the Template definition.

Ownership is distinct from:

* authorship of a document created from the Template;
* physical ownership of a file;
* repository ownership;
* Document Identity.

The relationship is:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Governance Authority
            │
            └── Template Owner

```

Ownership provides accountability for Template evolution.

---

## 9. Change Assessment

Before a Template change is approved, its potential impact should be assessed.

Assessment may consider:

* structural impact;
* semantic impact;
* Template Instance impact;
* dependent Template impact;
* relationship impact;
* constraint impact;
* validation impact;
* documentation impact;
* compatibility impact.

Conceptually:

```text

                     Proposed Change
                            │
                            ▼

                    Impact Assessment
                    │
                    ├── Structural Impact
                    │
                    ├── Semantic Impact
                    │
                    ├── Dependency Impact
                    │
                    ├── Compatibility Impact
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision

```

Impact assessment does not replace validation.

---

## 11. Template Approval

Approval is the governance decision authorizing a Template definition or change for the applicable purpose.

Approval is distinct from validation.

```text

                Validation
                    │
                    ▼

         Conformance Information
                    │
                    ▼

            Governance Review
                    │
                    ▼

            Approval Decision

```

A Template may be structurally valid without being approved for operational use.

Likewise, approval must not be interpreted as a substitute for technical validation.

---

## 12. Governance and Lifecycle

Governance controls lifecycle transitions but does not define the lifecycle states.

The relationship is:

```text

           Governance Decision
                    │
                    ▼

           Lifecycle Transition

```

For example:

```text

                 Defined
                    │
                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active

```

or:

```text

                  Active
                    │
           Deprecation Decision
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated

```

The lifecycle states and transitions are defined by DF-TPL-006 — Template Lifecycle.

---

## 13. Governance and Validation

Validation provides evidence about Template conformance.

Governance uses that information when making applicable decisions.

```text

                 Template
                    │
                    ▼

                Validation
                    │
                    ▼

            Validation Result
                    │
                    ▼

           Governance Decision

```

Governance does not redefine validation criteria or validation algorithms.

Those responsibilities belong to DF-TPL-007 — Template Validation.

---

## 14. Template Version Governance

Template changes must preserve the distinction between Template Version and lifecycle state.

A governed change may result in a new Template Version.

```text

            Template Version 1
                    │
            Controlled Change
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Version 2

```

Governance determines whether the change requires a new Version according to the applicable versioning rules.

A new Template Version must remain traceable to the change that produced it.

Template Version must remain distinct from:

* Document Identity;
* Document Revision;
* Document Edition;
* Baseline.

---

## 19. Governance Records

Governance decisions should be associated with appropriate records.

A conceptual governance record may contain:

```text

            Governance Record
            │
            ├── Template
            │
            ├── Template Version
            │
            ├── Change
            │
            ├── Decision
            │
            ├── Authority
            │
            ├── Date
            │
            ├── Rationale
            │
            └── Result

```

The exact representation of governance records belongs to the applicable governance implementation.

The Templates component defines their conceptual role only.

---

## 20. Governance Traceability

Template governance must maintain traceability between:

```text

                  Change
                    │
                    ▼

                  Review
                    │
                    ▼

                Validation
                    │
                    ▼

                 Decision
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Version
                    │
                    ▼

             Lifecycle State

```

This traceability allows the evolution history of a Template to be reconstructed.

It also supports analysis of the impact of Template changes on dependent documentation structures.

---

## 21. Governance and Template Relationships

Governance must consider relationships affected by Template changes.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template B

```

A change to Template B may affect Template A.

Similarly:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composed from  ─────►  Template B

```

A change to Template B may affect the composed structure of Template A.

Governance therefore requires awareness of applicable relationships without defining their semantics.

Detailed relationship semantics belong to DF-TPL-009 — Template Relationships.

---

## 23. Governance and Template Extensibility

Template extensions may introduce additional structural or semantic capabilities.

Governance must ensure that extensions remain consistent with the established Template architecture.

Extensions must not silently redefine established Template concepts.

Detailed extension mechanisms belong to DF-TPL-011 — Template Extensibility.

---

## 24. Governance Decision Outcomes

A governance decision concerning a Template change may result in:

```text

            Proposed
            │
            ├── Accepted
            │
            ├── Rejected
            │
            ├── Deferred
            │
            └── Returned for Revision

```

An accepted change may proceed to the applicable Template lifecycle transition.

A rejected change does not alter the governed Template definition.

A deferred change remains unresolved until a subsequent governance decision.

A returned change requires further development or assessment.

---

## 25. Governance Invariants

### 25.1. Authority Invariant

A governed Template has an identifiable authority.

### 25.2. Change Control Invariant

Changes to governed Templates must be subject to the applicable change-control process.

### 25.3. Traceability Invariant

Approved Template changes remain traceable to their resulting Template Version.

### 25.4. Preservation Invariant

Historical Template definitions must remain preservable when required.

### 25.5. Separation Invariant

Governance must not assume responsibilities belonging to other Documentation Framework components.

### 25.6. Validation Separation Invariant

Governance decisions must remain distinct from validation results.

### 25.7. Lifecycle Separation Invariant

Governance decisions must remain distinct from lifecycle states.

### 25.8. Version Separation Invariant

Template Version must remain distinct from document identity and document revision concepts.

### 25.9. Architectural Invariant

Governed Template changes must remain consistent with the Documentation Framework architecture.

### 25.10. Technology Independence Invariant

Template Governance must remain independent of implementation technology.

