## 1. Purpose, authority and scope

This document defines the working contracts for the review initiated on 2026-09-30 from the supplied Context.zip. Its authority for conducting this review derives from the user's explicit instructions in Load-Review-Context.md, edition 4, and the subsequent CONTINUAR command for Step 3. It does not evidence publication, framework-wide release approval, or operational implementation of Reviews.

Reviews is an existing architectural component: DF-ARC-005 §6.3 assigns technical reviews, architectural reviews and consistency verification to it. This policy and DF-RVW-002 belong to that component; their location does not create a new Layer or component. Review artifacts are maintained under the existing 03-Governance/Reviews area, with Behavior and Reference documentation categories.

The rules below govern working editions and this review's tracking. They are the responsible process source for these review conventions. Identity semantics remain owned by Document Identity; classification semantics by Classification; descriptive schemas/profiles by Metadata; framework architecture by Architecture. Those sources must incorporate the applicable decisions through their scheduled REVIEW/UPDATE/VALIDATE cycles. Their remaining discrepancies are recorded in DF-RVW-002, rather than reported as integrated consistency.

Where received documents conflict with the user's adopted rules, the adopted rules govern the working review. The received rule remains preserved as input/historical evidence and is pending reconciliation; it is not a second governing rule for the same working operation. No completed rollout across existing sources is claimed by creating this policy.

## 2. Normalized documents and functional files

Every file named README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md in this corpus is a non-normalized functional file. It retains its name and does not require Document ID, Family, Type, Component, Version, Revision, Status or Baseline by virtue of document normalization. Do not infer a finding from absence of those fields. Do not automatically delete legitimate existing information.

These files remain in inventories, SHA-256 manifests, content reviews and applicable structural, terminology, reference and consistency checks. CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md retain their own entry/milestone IDs, states, dates and historical conventions. Their maintenance is not conditional on normalized document metadata.

The input corpus comprises 79 documents within normalization scope and 8 non-normalized files. Two normalized review documents are introduced by Step 3. Machine-readable exports attached to DF-RVW-002 are representations of its inventories and matrices, not independent normalized documents or new authorities. Each export identifies its parent document and edition in its manifest or accompanying report.

## 3. Classification contract

### 3.1. Uniform Type

Type identifies the primary responsibility of every normalized document and uses exactly one value from {Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference}. There are no special Type values for Foundation, Architecture, global roadmaps or review artifacts.

| Type | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Foundations, principles, concepts, conceptual models/elements and architectural decisions. |
| Structure | Organization, composition, schemas, structural relationships, restrictions and element catalogs. |
| Behavior | Processes, lifecycle, validation, governance, extensibility and planned evolution. |
| Reference | Consultation, terminology, consolidated specifications, examples, recommendations and historical records. |

Use the spelling Behavior. Base, Core, Schema, Dictionary and Lifecycle are not additional Type values. A historical evolution account is Reference; a process or evolution plan is Behavior. Assess content and primary responsibility rather than filename or directory alone. Normative or informative authority is established by explicit statements/references, never by Type=Reference alone. Validation is not approval.

### 3.2. Family and Component

| Document category | Family | Component |
|---|---|---|
| Belongs to a component | Canonical component name | Same canonical name, when the field is used. |
| Foundation without a component | Foundation | Absent/not applicable. |
| Architecture without a component | Architecture | Absent/not applicable. |
| Global roadmap or global implementation strategy | Roadmap | Absent/not applicable. |
| This review's policy/report | Reviews | Reviews. |

Roadmap is an explicitly scoped documentary planning area for global, non-component plans. It reuses the received Family value in DF-RDM-001/002, not an invented component or Layer. These two documents use Type=Behavior. The existing Component=Documentation Framework in DF-RDM-002 must be assessed and removed from its working header in the scheduled UPDATE: the framework is the container, not a component of itself.

Component roadmaps belong to the component they plan and therefore use Family=component, Type=Behavior and matching Component, regardless of central storage under Roadmaps. Current component names are Metadata, Document Identity, Classification and Templates. DocumentIdentity is a directory alias, not a competing canonical component name.

Do not remove Component indiscriminately. The global roadmap decision is localized and does not remove it from component documents. Family/Type changes do not determine document identity or structural Layer allocation.

### 3.3. Class

Class remains a separate, optional semantic dimension. This policy does not create a complete Class vocabulary or make it mandatory. Retain received values as evidence, then assess each use in its document cycle. A value that merely repeats Type or misstates authority must be reconciled with evidence. New review artifacts omit Class because no additional distinction is needed. Optional does not mean unrestricted: any value used must have an explicit, non-conflicting definition.

## 4. Identity convention for this corpus and review artifacts

### 4.1. Representation and uniqueness

The identity domain is Documentation Framework. Its representation prefix is DF. A working normalized document identifier follows DF-SSS-NNN, where SSS is a registered three-letter uppercase allocation-series code and NNN is a three-digit positive allocation number, 001–999. The full identifier is unique within the domain. Numbers are allocated within a series; equal numeric suffixes across different series are not collisions.

Series codes are stable allocation namespaces, not the document's current Family, Type, component, location, version or revision. Preserve existing valid identifiers when those characteristics change. A series' original purpose is recorded for traceability, but it does not recalculate an existing document ID after reassignment/reclassification.

| Series | Received origin/purpose | Step 3 action |
|---|---|---|
| FND | Foundation documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| ARC | Framework Architecture documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| MTD | Metadata documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| DID | Document Identity documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| CLS | Classification documents | Preserve unambiguous allocations; resolve the nominal CLS-003 collision. |
| TPL | Templates documents | Preserve existing allocations. |
| RDM | Planning documents | Preserve allocations even when Family becomes a component name. |
| RVW | Review policy and consolidated review report | Allocate 001 to this policy and 002 to DF-RVW-002 after collision checks. |

This is a corpus convention, not a format imposed on identities in other domains or an identifier-generation implementation. Scheduled reconciliation of DF-DID-005/010/014 owns its integration into the identity contract. Foundation and Classification must qualify the earlier Family/Type-based convention accordingly.

### 4.2. Allocation, reservations and retirement

New allocation requires an explicit series record and collision scan of headers, filenames, references, historical/reserved records and this review's allocation register. Do not reuse allocated/retired numbers. A gap does not prove availability; when allocation history is unavailable, record that limitation and use a documented allocation decision rather than infer a historical reservation. Missing IDs are not assigned to the eight functional files excluded in §2.

000 is not allocated under this working convention; it is not implicitly a README code. RVW-001/002 are the only new allocations at Step 3; no future numbers are reserved. At 999, do not widen the syntax or silently recycle: register another unused three-letter series with traceable continuation and preserve all old IDs. A new domain is a separate semantic decision, not a shortcut for renumbering this corpus.

Maintain an allocation register in DF-RVW-002's exports, including series, number, identifier, path, allocation status and evidence. Retired IDs remain reserved. The source archive and the input manifest preserve received declarations, including invalid ones; preservation is evidence, not acceptance of a collision.

### 4.3. Localized correction and historical syntax

No general ID migration is required by the adopted classification change. The nominal DF-CLS-003-ClassificationModel.md wrongly declares DF-CLS-001 and repeats the Architecture prose. Its correction is pending a distinct document recovery/update and path-scoped map. It is not a global DF-CLS-001→DF-CLS-003 replacement or an alias that makes one identifier resolve to two documents.

Operational references must resolve to the intended final identity/path after a coordinated correction. Historical examples such as META-DCL-001, or earlier roadmap forms containing RDM as an extra segment, must be explicitly qualified where historical or revised where they purport to prescribe the current working convention. Do not rewrite history as if the new convention had always existed.

Metadata Element IDs, document IDs, finding IDs, CHANGELOG numbers and Milestone IDs are separate entities. Creating this policy does not assign Metadata Element IDs or create element lifecycle/publication records.

## 5. Version, Revision, Status and Baseline

### 5.1. Received evidence

The 79 in-scope input documents declare Version 1.0 and Baseline 1.0; 73 declare Revision 0 and six Foundation documents do not declare Revision. Historical sources distinguish significant Version evolution from backward-compatible Revision changes: DF-FND-002 §6.6 and DF-FND-004 §§4.10/6.8. Neither establishes a complete numerical successor contract for this review. The following working rule formalizes that gap while preserving input evidence.

### 5.2. Edition successors

Version uses the observed major.minor numeric form. Revision is a monotonic integer per document across version changes during this review.

| Change | Version action | Revision action |
|---|---|---|
| Compatible correction/clarification/reclassification preserving contractual meaning | Keep Version. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Compatible additive contract capability | Increment minor by one. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Incompatible contract/convention change | Increment major by one and set minor to 0. | Increment declared Revision by one; use 1 when absent. |
| Validation/reporting with no source content change | Keep Version. | Keep Revision; track the event centrally. |
| New normalized review document | Initial Version 1.0. | Initial Revision 1; no invented Revision 0 history. |

Explain compatibility per UPDATE. Changing a classification label does not automatically change Version; replacing what a classification/schema contract permits may be incompatible even if no IDs change. Assess changes to identity syntax/resolution separately from a filename correction. Do not reset an existing Revision counter on Version changes during this review. Future alternative numbering requires a traceable policy change, not an implied reset.

Each completed persisted working edition with changed content receives its successor. Draft editing before an edition is finalized is preparation, not evidence of completed intermediate editions. If a validated/finalized edition needs a correction, create another successor and retain the failed validation event. No source revision is incremented merely to record this policy's adoption.

### 5.3. Working lifecycle and Baseline

Edited working documents start at Status=Draft, including successors of received Approved/Canonical documents. A subsequent explicit submission may use Review; formal approval/publication requires its own decision/evidence. Leave untouched source statuses unchanged. Canonical in a received header is preserved as historical evidence, not automatically granted to a successor or silently converted into Approved.

A newly created or modified working edition has Baseline=Not assigned unless its exact inclusion is evidenced. Record original Status and Baseline in the edition history and input manifest. Do not change the original Baseline snapshot. Draft is a lifecycle state; Not assigned is an explicit absence marker in the human-readable working header, not a new Baseline identifier.

At Step 3 creation, this policy and DF-RVW-002 were Draft, Version 1.0, Revision 1, Baseline Not assigned. Current working coordinates follow their headers and exact edition histories. Passing their scoped checks does not approve/publish them or place them in a Baseline. The conventions for these working headers do not populate the canonical Metadata Dictionary or create a Metadata Profile lifecycle event by implication.

## 6. REVIEW, UPDATE, VALIDATE and evidence

Keep Step 1–7 and document substep numbers 4.01–4.87 stable. Step 3.1 identifies this policy; Step 3.2 identifies the consolidated report. The eight functional files keep their scheduled content/reference substeps but have no normalization requirement.

REVIEW reports findings, sections, severity, proposed correction and closure evidence without modifying the reviewed source. UPDATE shows exact material before/after, compatibility assessment, full updated source, diff, edition history, central CHANGELOG entry and Milestone. Mark source corrections pending validation. VALIDATE compares the exact updated edition with its input and affected sources, checks related occurrences and records outcome/limits with SHA-256 evidence. A failure creates a traceable corrective step.

Before any cross-document normative change or path/ID migration, identify the batch, rationale, affected documents and previous/new mapping. Do not claim integrated consistency during partial rollout. Resolve semantic references and actual dependencies separately; do not use a renamed relationship type to conceal a mandatory dependency cycle.

Finding states used for this review are Open, Corrected—pending validation, Closed—verified and Not applicable—scope decision. These tracking states are not document Status, element lifecycle or Milestone Status. Closure requires evidence; scope exclusion requires the specific decision. INV-02 is Not applicable because the user excluded the eight functional files, not because IDs were assigned or validation passed.

The input/final/validated manifests record paths, identity and edition where applicable, SHA-256 and scope. Evidence exports are attached to DF-RVW-002. A manifest's own hash belongs in its delivery receipt/enclosing package, not recursively inside its own contents. A document's hash is recorded outside the document itself. Validation logs do not force recursive revisions of themselves.

## 7. Central CHANGELOG and Milestones

Reuse CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md, retaining their historical content. They remain non-normalized. Keep the CHANGELOG's sequential #, reverse chronology, Author, Type, Document, Impact and Description columns. Add Reviewed and Validated event types to distinguish executed reviews/checks from document content updates; these event Types are not document Type values. Existing Created/Updated/etc. and impact values remain in force.

### 7.1. Cumulative documentary authorship

The normalized document header's **Author** field lists all evidenced authors who contributed to the document, including its original author and contributors to later editions. Use **semicolon followed by a space (`; `)** between distinct authors. Preserve established names and role qualifications; retain first evidenced contribution order and do not duplicate an author for each revision. Example: `Arnaldo Figueira; Codex — AI assistant`.

Carry forward evidenced original/prior authors when preparing a successor. Record each later contributor when that contribution is supported by source history, exact edition/diff evidence or explicit reliable attribution. Preserve edition history separately so the cumulative header does not imply that every listed author performed every change. When original authorship is absent or unknown, list only known contributors and retain that limitation; do not guess an author from ownership, filename, user identity or authorization. A later substantiated attribution receives a traceable correction.

A user who actually edits document content is recorded as an author when that contribution and identity are established. Permission, instructions, approval or file custody alone do not prove an authored contribution. Later disk changes must be examined as resulting bytes with attribution evidence; earlier validation results do not automatically apply. The author list is provenance, not a blanket assignment of approval or responsibility for consequences of every later final product.

### 7.2. Event-specific CHANGELOG authorship

The CHANGELOG **Author** column records the evidenced contributors who performed that particular event, using the same `; ` separator when the event has multiple authors. It is not copied automatically from the cumulative document header. Use `Codex — AI assistant` for events performed solely by this assistant; do not attribute the event to the user merely because the user authorized it. Preserve historical event authors rather than retroactively adding every document author to each row.

For each update, record source path/ID, old/new edition, material change, finding, validation state, report/diff link and Milestone in the Description. Append a later validation event rather than rewriting a pending-validation update into a historical success. Do not log future intentions as completed changes.

### 7.3. Milestone scope and history

Preserve M0–M7. Create M8–M14 for the review's verifiable results, with the existing Not Started/In Progress/Completed milestone states and O/S/C record states. A milestone's state derives from its own records for its declared work scope. Completion of a historical implementation milestone is not closure of a new review milestone.

M8 establishes the received corpus, including explicit limitations. M9 establishes this review's policy, artifact identities, central tracking and scoped checks. M10 covers Foundation cycles; M11 Architecture cycles; M12 the four input Documentation components; M13 localized identity/path/reference reconciliation; M14 integrated validation and final delivery. M9 excludes propagation into all domain sources, which is assigned to M10–M13.

No estimated completion date is invented. Completion dates are actual dates when criteria are satisfied. No new Blocked/Not applicable milestone state is introduced; describe blockers or non-applicable migration scope in the relevant milestone's evidence. A review Milestone=Completed means its documentary criteria were met, not approval, publication, release or Baseline membership.

# 1. Introduction

The Metadata Roadmap defines the implementation and evolution strategy of the Metadata component within the Documentation Framework.

Metadata represents one of the fundamental architectural components of the framework.

As established in the Design Rationale, the explicit separation between document content and Metadata constitutes one of the first and most important architectural decisions of the Documentation Framework.

This roadmap describes how the Metadata component should evolve while preserving that architectural principle.

---

# 4. Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework, Metadata belongs to the Documentation Layer.

Conceptually.

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌───────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                  │
                    │ Document Identity         │
                    │ Classification            │
                    │ Templates                 │
                    └───────────────────────────┘

```

Metadata provides the descriptive information required by nearly every other architectural component.

---

# 5. Architectural Dependencies

## 5.1. Depends On

- Foundation

## 5.2. Required By

- Document Identity
- Classification
- Registry
- Workflow
- Policies
- Baselines
- Relationships
- Knowledge Graph
- Validation
- Automation

Metadata is therefore considered one of the core architectural services of the Documentation Framework.

---

## 5.1. Depends On

- Foundation

## 5.2. Required By

- Document Identity
- Classification
- Registry
- Workflow
- Policies
- Baselines
- Relationships
- Knowledge Graph
- Validation
- Automation

Metadata is therefore considered one of the core architectural services of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 6. Implementation Strategy

The Metadata component shall evolve incrementally.

Each stage introduces additional capabilities without breaking previously established Metadata structures.

---

## 6.1. Stage 1 — Core Metadata

### 6.1.1. Objective

Define the minimum Metadata required to uniquely describe a document.

### 6.1.2. Deliverables

- Metadata model
- Metadata terminology
- Metadata conventions

### 6.1.3. Initial Fields

- Document ID
- Title
- Family
- Type
- Status
- Version
- Revision
- Baseline
- Language

### 6.1.4. Result

Every document becomes self-describing.

---

## 6.2. Stage 2 — Structural Metadata

### 6.2.1. Objective

Describe the structural characteristics of documents.

### 6.2.2. Deliverables

Additional Metadata describing.

- document hierarchy;
- parent document;
- logical grouping;
- component ownership.

### 6.2.3. Result

Documents become structurally identifiable.

---

## 6.3. Stage 3 — Lifecycle Metadata

### 6.3.1. Objective

Represent document evolution.

### 6.3.2. Deliverables

Metadata supporting.

- creation;
- updates;
- approval;
- publication;
- archival.

### 6.3.3. Result

Metadata supports document lifecycle management.

---

## 6.4. Stage 4 — Governance Metadata

### 6.4.1. Objective

Support governance mechanisms.

### 6.4.2. Deliverables

Fields describing.

- owner;
- reviewer;
- approver;
- review cycle;
- publication state.

### 6.4.3. Result

Governance mechanisms become Metadata-driven.

---

## 6.5. Stage 5 — Traceability Metadata

### 6.5.1. Objective

Support architectural traceability.

### 6.5.2. Deliverables

Metadata supporting.

- dependencies;
- references;
- relationships;
- superseded documents;
- replacement history.

### 6.5.3. Result

Metadata enables document traceability.

---

## 6.6. Stage 6 — Discovery Metadata

### 6.6.1. Objective

Support knowledge discovery.

### 6.6.2. Deliverables

Metadata for.

- keywords;
- tags;
- categories;
- topics;
- search optimization.

### 6.6.3. Result

Metadata supports advanced document discovery.

---

## 6.7. Stage 7 — Automation Metadata

### 6.7.1. Objective

Support automation.

### 6.7.2. Deliverables

Metadata consumed by.

- validators;
- generators;
- documentation pipelines;
- publishing tools.

### 6.7.3. Result

Automation becomes Metadata-driven.

---

## 6.1. Stage 1 — Core Metadata

### 6.1.1. Objective

Define the minimum Metadata required to uniquely describe a document.

### 6.1.2. Deliverables

- Metadata model

# Metadata Component

---

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, governing and standardizing the metadata that describes documents within the Documentation Framework.

---

# Overview

The **Metadata** component defines the canonical metadata architecture of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the concepts, structures, lifecycle, governance and specifications required to describe documents in a consistent, technology-independent and architecturally stable manner.

Metadata provides the common semantic foundation upon which the remaining Documentation Framework components are built.

---

# Purpose

The Metadata component is responsible for defining:

- the Metadata architecture;
- Metadata concepts;
- Metadata models;
- Metadata elements;
- Metadata schemas;
- Metadata validation;
- Metadata governance;
- Metadata extensibility.

The component does **not** define:

- document content;
- document storage;
- repositories;
- workflows;
- permissions;
- implementation technologies.

---

# Responsibilities

The Metadata component is responsible for:

- defining canonical Metadata concepts;
- defining Metadata Elements;
- defining Metadata Schemas;
- defining Metadata Profiles;
- defining Metadata Relationships;
- defining Metadata Constraints;
- defining Metadata Lifecycle;
- defining Metadata Validation;
- defining Metadata Governance;
- defining Metadata Extensibility;
- maintaining the Metadata Dictionary;
- publishing the Metadata Specification.

---

# Component Scope

The Metadata component defines **what metadata is** and **how it is architecturally described** within the Documentation Framework.

It does not define:

- how documents are managed;
- how repositories operate;
- how metadata is physically stored;
- how metadata is implemented;
- how metadata is exchanged between systems.

Those responsibilities belong to other Documentation Framework components.

---

# Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework architecture, Metadata is a **Documentation Component**.

Conceptually.

```text

# Classification Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, assigning and governing the semantic classification of documents within the Documentation Framework.

# 1. Overview

The **Classification** component defines how documents are organized into semantic categories according to a defined classification model.

Classification provides a semantic mechanism for organizing documents within the Documentation Framework while remaining independent of their physical representation.

The component establishes the concepts, models, elements, structures, rules and governance required to define and maintain classification systems.

---

# 2. Purpose

The purpose of the Classification component is to provide a consistent and controlled mechanism for classifying documentation.

Classification enables documents to be organized according to their semantic characteristics rather than according to their physical location.

The component provides the architectural foundation required for:

- semantic organization;
- document discovery;
- document grouping;
- classification-based relationships;
- validation;
- governance;
- automation.

---

# 3. Architectural Position

Classification belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

Conceptually:

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌───────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                  │
                    │ Document Identity         │
                    │ Classification            │
                    │ Templates                 │
                    └───────────────────────────┘

```

Classification works together with Metadata and Document Identity while maintaining its own architectural responsibility.

---

# 4. Responsibility

The Classification component is responsible for:

- defining classification concepts;
- defining classification models;
- defining classification elements;
- defining classification schemas;
- defining classification assignments;
- defining classification relationships;
- defining classification constraints;
- defining classification lifecycle;
- defining classification validation;
- defining classification governance;
- defining classification extensibility;
- defining authoritative classification terminology.

Classification does not define:

- document identity;
- document metadata in general;
- document templates;
- document workflows;
- physical repository organization.

Those responsibilities belong to other components of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 5. Architectural Independence

Classification is independent of the physical representation of documentation.

The semantic organization defined by Classification shall not depend on:

- directory structures;
- filenames;
- repositories;
- storage technologies;
- document formats;
- implementation technologies.

A physical organization may reflect conceptual distinctions established by Classification, but the physical representation does not define those distinctions.

The relationship is therefore:

```text

         Classification Semantics
                    │
                    ▼

       Architectural Representation
                    │
                    ▼

          Physical Representation

```

and not:

```text

          Physical Representation
                    │
                    ▼

         Classification Semantics

```

---

# 6. Relationship with Other Components

## 6.1. Metadata

Metadata provides descriptive information about documents that may participate in classification.

Classification uses that information without redefining the responsibility of Metadata.

---

## 6.2. Document Identity

Document Identity provides the logical identity of the documents to which classifications may be assigned.

Classification does not establish document identity.

---

## 6.3. Templates

Templates may define standardized structures for representing classification information.

Classification defines the semantic classification model rather than the template used to represent it.

---

## 6.4. Workflow

Workflow may use classification information when determining or controlling document processes.

Classification does not define workflow behavior.

---

## 6.5. Policies

Policies may establish rules governing the use or administration of classifications.

Classification provides the classification structures to which such policies may apply.

---

## 6.6. Registry and Discovery

Classification may provide semantic information used by Registry and Discovery mechanisms to organize and locate documentation.

---

## 6.7. Knowledge Graph

Classification concepts and relationships may contribute semantic information to the Knowledge Graph.

---

# 7. Documentation Structure

The Classification component is defined through the following documents:

| Order | Document | Description |
|------:|----------|-------------|
| 1 | DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture | Defines the architectural position, responsibility and boundaries of Classification. |
| 2 | DF-CLS-002 — Classification Concepts | Defines the fundamental concepts of Classification. |
| 3 | DF-CLS-003 — Classification Model | Defines the conceptual model governing classification. |
| 4 | DF-CLS-004 — Classification Elements | Defines the elements that constitute a classification system. |
| 5 | DF-CLS-005 — Classification Schema | Defines the formal structure of classification systems. |
| 6 | DF-CLS-006 — Classification Lifecycle | Defines the lifecycle of classification structures and assignments. |
| 7 | DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation | Defines classification validation and conformance rules. |
| 8 | DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance | Defines governance and control of classification systems. |
| 9 | DF-CLS-009 — Classification Relationships | Defines relationships between classification elements and related entities. |
| 10 | DF-CLS-010 — Classification Constraints | Defines constraints that preserve classification integrity. |
| 11 | DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility | Defines mechanisms for extending classification systems. |
| 12 | DF-CLS-012 — Classification Best Practices | Documents recommended practices for classification design and maintenance. |
| 13 | DF-CLS-013 — Classification Dictionary | Defines authoritative Classification terminology. |
| 14 | DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification | Consolidates the normative Classification specification. |
| 15 | DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples | Provides representative examples of Classification usage. |

---

# 8. Documentation Progression

The documentation follows four major stages.

## 8.1. Conceptual Foundation

```text

    DF-CLS-001
    DF-CLS-002
    DF-CLS-003

```

Defines the architectural and conceptual foundations of Classification.

## 8.2. Structural Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-004
    DF-CLS-005

```

Defines the elements and structures used to represent classifications.

## 8.3. Operational Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-006
    DF-CLS-007
    DF-CLS-008
    DF-CLS-009
    DF-CLS-010
    DF-CLS-011

```

Defines lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints and extensibility.

## 8.4. Consolidation and Reference

```text

    DF-CLS-012
    DF-CLS-013
    DF-CLS-014
    DF-CLS-015

```

Provides best practices, terminology, normative specification and examples.

---

# 9. Classification Model

The Classification component establishes a conceptual distinction between:

```text

                    Classification System
                    │
                    ├── Classification Model
                    │
                    ├── Classification Elements
                    │
                    ├── Classification Relationships
                    │
                    ├── Classification Constraints
                    │
                    └── Classification Assignments

```

The detailed definitions of these concepts belong to the respective Classification specifications.

---

# 10. Classification and Metadata Type

Metadata `Type` may participate in classification.

However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.

Classification shall not redefine Metadata `Type` merely to support its own model.

The relationship between `Type`, semantic classification and physical organization shall be addressed consistently across the Documentation Framework.

In particular, the existence of physical directory distinctions shall not be interpreted as evidence that those directories define the semantics of `Type`.

---

# 11. Validation

Classification shall support validation at multiple levels:

1. element existence;
2. structural validity;
3. value validity;
4. semantic validity;
5. cross-element consistency;
6. cross-document consistency;
7. architectural consistency.

The detailed validation rules are defined by **DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation**.

---

# 12. Governance

Classification systems shall be subject to controlled governance.

Governance concerns include:

- ownership;
- responsibility;
- approval;
- change control;
- review;
- publication;
- deprecation;
- retirement.

The detailed governance model is defined by **DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance**.

---

# 13. Extensibility

Classification shall support controlled evolution.

Extensions may include:

- new classification categories;
- new classification elements;
- new attributes;
- schema extensions;
- new relationships;
- additional classification models.

Extensions shall preserve established semantics and maintain compatibility with existing classification definitions where required.

The detailed extensibility model is defined by **DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility**.

---

# 14. Authoritative Specification

The complete normative definition of Classification is consolidated in:

**DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification**

The other Classification documents provide the concepts, models, structures, rules and supporting material from which the specification is established.

The specification is therefore the authoritative reference for the complete Classification component.

---

# 15. Examples

Representative examples are maintained separately in:

**DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples**

Examples are intended to demonstrate the application of the Classification specification without becoming normative definitions themselves.

---

# 16. Roadmap

The development sequence of the Classification component is defined by:

**DF-RDM-030 — Classification Roadmap**

The roadmap describes the progressive development of the component but does not itself define the Classification architecture.

---

# 17. Design Principles

The Classification component follows the following principles:

- **Semantic Independence** — Classification represents semantic organization rather than physical storage.
- **Architectural Separation** — Classification maintains clear boundaries with other Documentation Framework components.
- **Explicit Semantics** — classification concepts shall have explicit and unambiguous meanings.
- **Consistency** — classification definitions shall remain internally and cross-component consistent.
- **Traceability** — classification changes shall remain traceable.
- **Controlled Evolution** — classification systems shall evolve through defined lifecycle and governance mechanisms.
- **Extensibility** — classification shall support controlled extension.
- **Single Source of Truth** — authoritative classification concepts shall have a single canonical definition.
- **Technology Independence** — classification shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

# 18. Component Completion

The Classification component is considered architecturally complete when its documentation establishes:

- the architectural responsibility of Classification;
- its fundamental concepts;
- its conceptual model;
- its elements;
- its schema;
- its lifecycle;
- its validation rules;
- its governance;
- its relationships;
- its constraints;
- its extensibility mechanisms;
- its best practices;
- its authoritative terminology;
- its normative specification;
- representative examples.

---

# 19. Future Evolution

Future versions of the Classification component may introduce additional capabilities such as:

- advanced taxonomy models;
- ontology-based classification;
- semantic classification;
- automated classification;
- AI-assisted classification;
- classification quality metrics;
- interoperability mechanisms;
- semantic impact analysis.

Such extensions shall preserve the architectural boundaries and principles established by the Documentation Framework.

---

# 20. Change History

| Date | Version | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| 2026-08-09 | 1.0 | Initial Classification component README. |

# Templates Componnet

The **Templates** component is an architectural component of the Documentation Framework responsible for defining, organizing, governing and standardizing reusable structures for documentation.

Templates provide consistent structural patterns for documents that share common purposes, characteristics or organizational requirements.

---

## Purpose

The purpose of the Templates component is to provide a standardized and reusable mechanism for defining documentation structures.

Templates enable recurring documentation patterns to be defined once and reused consistently across the Documentation Framework.

The component contributes to:

* structural consistency;
* documentation reuse;
* predictable organization;
* maintainability;
* structural validation;
* documentation generation.

---

## Architectural Position

Templates belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

```text

            Documentation Framework
            │
            ├── Foundation
            ├── Architecture
            │
            ├── Documentation
            │   ├── Metadata
            │   ├── DocumentIdentity
            │   ├── Classification
            │   └── Templates
            │
            ├── Governance
            ├── Discovery
            ├── Automation
            └── Integration

```

Templates operates alongside other Documentation Layer components while maintaining clear separation of responsibilities.

---

## Responsibilities

The Templates component is responsible for:

* defining template architecture;
* defining template concepts;
* defining template models;
* defining template elements;
* defining template structures;
* defining template schemas;
* defining template lifecycle;
* defining template validation;
* defining template governance;
* defining template relationships;
* defining template constraints;
* defining template extensibility;
* defining reusable documentation structures;
* supporting standardized documentation creation;
* supporting structural conformance.

---

## Boundaries

Templates defines **documentation structure**.

It does not define or own:

* permanent document identity;
* Metadata semantics;
* document classification semantics;
* document storage;
* document repositories;
* document permissions;
* document workflows;
* document governance policies;
* document registries;
* knowledge graph semantics;
* implementation technologies.

When a template represents information owned by another component, the authoritative definition remains with that component.

---

## Relationships with Other Components

### Metadata

Metadata defines the information used to describe documents.

Templates may define where and how Metadata is structurally represented within a document.

Templates do not redefine Metadata semantics.

### Document Identity

Document Identity defines the permanent identity of documents.

Templates may provide a structural location for document identity information.

Templates do not assign or redefine document identity.

### Classification

Classification defines the classification of documents.

Templates may provide a structural location for classification information.

Templates do not define classification semantics.

### Workflow

Workflow may consume template definitions when standardized document structures are required during document lifecycle activities.

### Registry

Registry may use template information to support the identification or organization of documents according to established structures.

### Validation

Validation may use template definitions to verify structural conformance.

### Automation

Automation may consume template definitions for automated documentation generation and related activities.

---

## Design Principles

The Templates component follows these principles:

1. **Structural Responsibility**
   Templates are responsible for documentation structures.

2. **Reusability**
   Equivalent documentation structures should be defined once and reused.

3. **Consistency**
   Equivalent documentation purposes should use consistent structural patterns.

4. **Separation of Responsibilities**
   Templates shall not assume responsibilities belonging to other components.

5. **Technology Independence**
   Templates shall remain independent of specific implementation technologies.

6. **Repository Independence**
   Templates shall remain independent of document repositories.

7. **Storage Independence**
   Templates shall remain independent of storage mechanisms.

8. **Single Source of Truth**
   Each template concept shall have one authoritative definition.

9. **Controlled Evolution**
   Template definitions shall evolve through controlled changes.

10. **Extensibility**
    Template structures shall support controlled extension and specialization.

---

## Documentation Structure

The Templates component documentation is organized according to the component development roadmap.

```text

            Templates/
            ├── README.md
            │
            ├── DF-TPL-001-Templates-Architecture.md
            ├── DF-TPL-002-Template-Concepts.md
            ├── DF-TPL-003-Template-Model.md
            ├── DF-TPL-004-Template-Elements.md
            ├── DF-TPL-005-Template-Schema.md
            ├── DF-TPL-006-Template-Lifecycle.md
            ├── DF-TPL-007-Template-Validation.md
            ├── DF-TPL-008-Template-Governance.md
            ├── DF-TPL-009-Template-Relationships.md
            ├── DF-TPL-010-Template-Constraints.md
            ├── DF-TPL-011-Template-Extensibility.md
            ├── DF-TPL-012-Template-Best-Practices.md
            ├── DF-TPL-013-Template-Dictionary.md
            ├── DF-TPL-014-Template-Specification.md
            └── DF-TPL-015-Template-Examples.md

```

The exact physical location of these documents is determined by the Documentation Framework component structure and the Templates roadmap.

---

## Development Roadmap

The Templates component is developed through the following stages:

| Stage | Document   | Purpose                 |
| ----- | ---------- | ----------------------- |
| 1     | DF-TPL-001 | Templates Architecture  |
| 2     | DF-TPL-002 | Template Concepts       |
| 3     | DF-TPL-003 | Template Model          |
| 4     | DF-TPL-004 | Template Elements       |
| 5     | DF-TPL-005 | Template Schema         |
| 6     | DF-TPL-006 | Template Lifecycle      |
| 7     | DF-TPL-007 | Template Validation     |
| 8     | DF-TPL-008 | Template Governance     |
| 9     | DF-TPL-009 | Template Relationships  |
| 10    | DF-TPL-010 | Template Constraints    |
| 11    | DF-TPL-011 | Template Extensibility  |
| 12    | DF-TPL-012 | Template Best Practices |
| 13    | DF-TPL-013 | Template Dictionary     |
| 14    | DF-TPL-014 | Template Specification  |
| 15    | DF-TPL-015 | Template Examples       |

The roadmap defines the sequence in which the Templates component is developed.

---

## Architectural Independence

Templates is independent of:

* programming languages;
* databases;
* file systems;
* document editors;
* repositories;
* storage technologies;
* rendering engines;
* documentation generators;
* version-control systems.

Concrete implementations may provide representations or processing mechanisms for templates without changing their architectural meaning.

---

## Conformance

A Templates implementation conforms to the component architecture when it:

* preserves the responsibility boundaries of Templates;
* uses reusable documentation structures;
* maintains separation from Metadata semantics;
* maintains separation from Document Identity semantics;
* maintains separation from Classification semantics;
* remains independent of repositories and storage;
* remains independent of implementation technologies;
* supports controlled template evolution;
* maintains authoritative template definitions.

---

## 2.6. Document Identity

Document Identity owns the logical identity contract: Domain+Identifier identifies a normalized document independently of classification, content, filename, location, Version and Revision. Title is a mutable label, not an identity key.

Preserve valid allocations when descriptive classification changes. Correct erroneous declarations with a coordinated path-scoped map and historical evidence; do not create ambiguous aliases. Detailed identity schemas and the corpus representation convention must be reconciled in the Document Identity sources.

---

## 2.11. Baselines

Baselines defines immutable, coherent snapshots of explicitly selected approved document editions. Each member references a document identity and an exact Version/Revision or equivalent immutable edition reference. A Baseline has its own identity and is not an individual document Version.

A new Draft successor does not change an earlier Baseline or inherit membership. Baselines is primarily allocated to Governance and contributes to the conceptual Preservation concern. Approval, selection and reproducibility evidence remain distinct.

---

## 3.11. Document Identity

Domain+Identifier determines permanent logical identity. Name, classification, content, Version, Revision and location may evolve without changing a valid allocation. References and edition coordinates are associated information, not a second identity key. Detailed canonical identity schemas remain owned by Document Identity.

---

## 3.12. Document ID Structure

The received historical example META-DCL-001 interpreted META as Family and DCL as Type. This edition preserves that example as historical evidence and replaces its use as a current identity-construction rule.

<!-- view: ab3-3 -->
**View ab3-3 — historical versus current corpus identity representation.**

| Representation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| META-DCL-001 | Received historical example: META=Family, DCL=Type, 001=sequence; not the current rule. |
| DF-SSS-NNN | Current corpus convention: DF domain prefix, registered stable allocation series SSS, positive number NNN. |
| DF-FND-004 | Existing allocation retained; Family Foundation and Type Architecture are separate mutable descriptive values. |
<!-- end-view -->

Within this corpus, DF-SSS-NNN uses DF as the representation prefix for the Documentation Framework identity domain, a registered three-letter uppercase allocation series SSS and a positive three-digit number NNN (001–999). Series codes do not recalculate when current Family, Type or component membership changes. Existing FND/ARC/MTD/DID/CLS/TPL/RDM allocations remain stable; RVW is allocated for review artifacts. Equal numbers in different series are not full-ID collisions.

The detailed allocation/reservation/retirement convention is recorded in DF-RVW-001 §4 pending reconciliation into Document Identity. Do not infer availability from a gap, recycle retired IDs, widen syntax silently or assign 000 to README files. No general ID migration is required here. The nominal CLS-003 correction is separate and path-scoped; no global CLS-001→CLS-003 replacement is authorized by this summary.

---

## 3.14. Relationship Between Metadata and Identity

Metadata represents descriptive references and edition values. Document Identity owns stable key semantics; Classification owns category meanings. These relationships are descriptive/authority relations, not an unlabeled mandatory dependency chain.

<!-- view: ab3-4 -->
**View ab3-4 — descriptive versus identity relationships.**

| Source | Relation | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metadata Instance | describes | Document edition |
| Document Identity | identifies | Logical document |
| Metadata Instance | contains descriptive reference to | Document Identity |
| Classification | defines meaning of classification values used by | Metadata Instance |
<!-- end-view -->

Metadata Instance values may evolve with an edition. A valid logical document key remains stable; historical erroneous declarations are corrected with preserved provenance.

---

## 4.5. Document Edition States

Status is associated with the applicable document edition. A current working view identifies one effective state for that edition; earlier editions retain their own historical state evidence.

<!-- view: ab4-2 -->
**View ab4-2 — edition lifecycle vocabulary; historical states remain attached to editions.**

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | Working content; no approval inferred. |
| Review | Submitted for review under applicable policy. |
| Approved | Approval evidence refers to the exact edition. |
| Deprecated | The applicable edition or document use is superseded under policy. |
| Archived | Preserved historical state; return rules require explicit policy. |
<!-- end-view -->

The list is illustrative, not a compulsory linear path for every document. A new working Draft does not revoke an older edition’s approval or alter an existing immutable Baseline.

---

## 4.10. Versioning

The logical Document entity, its Version/Revision edition coordinates, its edition Status and its Baseline membership are distinct dimensions. Policies defines the numbering convention; Workflow applies lifecycle contracts to identified editions.

For this review, DF-RVW-001 §5 specifies working successor numbering and Draft/unassigned treatment. This Blueprint does not infer missing historical revisions or impose that review convention retroactively on received editions. Validation without source change does not increment the source Revision.

---

## 4.11. Baselines

Baselines references a coherent selection of approved immutable document editions. Policies establishes inclusion conditions; Workflow and Reviews provide applicable state/quality evidence; selection is explicit and independently recorded.

Editing or checking a document does not create a Baseline, confer approval or inherit prior membership. A prior approved edition may remain selected while its new working successor is Draft and unassigned. Baselines is primarily allocated to Governance while contributing to Preservation.

---

## 6.3. Baseline Concept

A Baseline is an independently identified immutable selection of coherent approved document editions. It is not an individual document Version and does not merely refer to whichever revision is current.

<!-- view: ab6-1 -->
**View ab6-1 — snapshot membership; references select immutable editions.**

| Baseline member | Selected edition |
| --- | --- |
| Document A identity | Exact Version/Revision or immutable equivalent. |
| Document B identity | Exact Version/Revision or immutable equivalent. |
| Membership | Explicit approved selection; not a reference to whichever edition is current. |
<!-- end-view -->

Membership selects document identity plus exact Version/Revision or an equivalent immutable edition reference. Reproducibility requires preservation of the selected content and relevant context; physical evidence may include a hash without prescribing a storage technology.

---

## 6.6. Inclusion Criteria

Inclusion requires policy-defined eligibility and an explicit selection record. The conceptual contract includes approval for the exact edition, valid descriptive information, consistent identity, verified relevant relationships and reproducible edition references.

Reviews/validation evidence does not replace approval or selection. The executing process records evidence under these contracts; this edition neither creates a new approved Baseline nor completes missing historical membership evidence.

---

## 8.11. Architectural Dependencies

A mandatory dependency identifies a consumer that requires a provider contract. Write its edge consumer→provider and record the contract, scope and justification. Conceptual refinement, documentary authority reference, data projection, navigation and chronological activity are separately typed relations.

<!-- view: ab8-5 -->
**View ab8-5 — selected intended contract dependencies; consumer→provider.**

| Consumer | Provider | Relationship kind | Justification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Registry | Metadata | Required descriptive contract | Index edition-specific values. |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Required identity contract | Key logical document nodes. |
| Knowledge Graph | Relationships | Required relationship contract | Interpret typed edges and their provenance. |
| Workflow | Metadata / Policies | Required descriptive/governance contracts | Interpret state and permitted transitions. |
| Baselines | Document Identity / Metadata | Required edition-reference contracts | Select and preserve exact document editions. |
<!-- end-view -->

The selected intended contract dependencies replace the unlabeled Metadata→Registry→Knowledge Graph→Baselines chain. They do not imply a required Registry→Knowledge Graph→Baselines execution sequence or a mandatory Discovery service dependency for snapshot selection. Exact editions and verification evidence can be supplied under the relevant contracts.

A full mandatory graph requires reconciliation with ARC-003/004/005 and the affected component specifications. Do not claim a verified global DAG here; do not conceal a genuine mandatory cycle by changing its edge label. Where the current sources differ, record the conflict and reconcile the responsible source during its scheduled cycle. Referencing a component specification from this Foundation overview is a documentary authority reference, not an execution dependency of Foundation on an upper-layer service.

---

## 3.6. The Concept of Document Identity

The model distinguishes represented knowledge, logical document entities, their permanent identity and physical representations. These are associations, not successive structural Layers or a mandatory execution chain.

<!-- view: dr3-1 -->
**View dr3-1 — Entity/representation associations.**

| Element / relation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Knowledge | Represented subject matter. |
| Document → Identity | Has one logical identity under its applicable normalized contract. |
| Document → physical representation | May have located representations; not a second identity key. |
<!-- end-view -->

The identity domain and identifier belong to Document Identity. An exact edition adds Version/Revision or an immutable equivalent; a representation location is neither a second identity key nor the identity of the knowledge itself.

---

## 6.8. Separation Between Revision and Baseline

A logical document identity is stable through ordinary evolution. Version/Revision identifies the applicable edition; Status describes that edition under its lifecycle contract. A Baseline identifies a collective selected configuration of exact editions and context.

This review uses the edition-successor rules in the Review Policy: compatible correction preserves Version and increments Revision; compatible additive contract increments minor Version; incompatible contract increments major Version; Revision remains monotonic. With no received Revision, the first edited successor declares Revision 1 without inventing historical Revision 0. Validation alone does not increment an unchanged source.

---

## 9.8. Principle of Controlled Evolution

Another important principle is controlled evolution.

The architecture was designed to evolve.

But that evolution must preserve the existing coherence.

New components should not alter the fundamental principles.

They should extend them instead.

---

## 5.4. Metadata

Metadata defines and represents structured descriptors used to describe, identify by reference, classify, govern and discover documentary entities/editions. Document Identity, Classification and Governance retain the meanings of their domain concepts; representing their values does not transfer semantic ownership to Metadata.

| Abstraction | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Dictionary | Defines descriptors and semantic meaning with references to domain owners |
| Schema | Organizes and references descriptor definitions and structural constraints |
| Profile | Restricts allowed usage, values and cardinality for a declared context without redefining semantics |
| Instance | Holds values for one document edition under exactly one effective Profile |

Conceptual separation of descriptors and content does not guarantee independent evolution, content-free verification or automatic consistency. Both may require coordinated edition changes. Applicability and mandatory usage follow the declared contract/Profile, not an invented universal header. This synopsis neither completes the received Dictionary/Profile gaps nor allocates Metadata Element IDs or publication records.

---

## 5.5. Document Identity

Document Identity defines permanent logical identity through **Domain+Identifier** and the applicable allocation/preservation contracts. Classification, title, filename, directory, repository, storage technology, Version and Revision can change without recalculating a valid logical allocation. References and lifecycle associations are not a second identity key.

The adopted corpus representation is DF-SSS-NNN: DF is the domain prefix, SSS a registered stable three-letter allocation series and NNN a positive three-digit number, 001–999. A series is not the current Family or Type. Existing valid IDs are retained; this source remains DF-ARC-003. The convention's details reside in DF-RVW-001 §4 pending scheduled Document Identity reconciliation.

Allocation/reservation/retirement rules are definitions, distinct from executing an allocation. No algorithm, new allocation, 000 functional-file identity or general migration is introduced here. The received CLS-003 collision remains a separate unresolved correction; references must resolve to the intended entity.

---

## 5.6. Classification

Classification defines semantic categories supporting organization, navigation, governance and discovery. Metadata represents classification values; directories and identity-series codes do not determine them.

For every normalized document, Type identifies the primary responsibility using exactly **Architecture, Structure, Behavior or Reference**. There are no Concepts, Base/Core or Foundation exceptions. Historical consultation is Reference; a process or planned evolution is Behavior. Family is the canonical component name or an explicitly admitted non-component documentary area. This document uses Architecture as its documentary area and Type Architecture for conceptual definitions.

Component, when used, identifies actual component membership. Class is optional and requires an explicit non-conflicting definition. Family/Type/Class, primary structural allocation, permanent identity, edition coordinates and Governance Status remain distinct. A category or Type=Reference alone confers neither normative authority nor approval.

---

# 8. Concept Dependencies

A required dependency identifies a consumer that needs a provider contract in a declared scope. Its direction is **consumer→provider**. Representation, semantic-authority reference, projection, navigation and execution order remain separately typed. Domain-definition references do not by themselves impose an operational runtime service dependency.

The following selected intended contracts reconcile this overview with Blueprint §8.11. They are architectural declarations for the stated scope, not a verified complete graph or implementation inventory.

|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | Metadata | Descriptive values with source-edition provenance | When indexing edition descriptors; refresh or identify stale values |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Entity identity for logical document nodes | When keying document nodes; other entity kinds use their own endpoint identity contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Relationships | Typed connection records and provenance | When projecting the semantic network and interpreting dependency kinds |
| Workflow | Metadata | Represented state/edition descriptors | When interpreting documentary state values for a governance transition |
| Workflow | Policies | Applicable transition and evidence rules | When deciding permitted governance operations; execution remains with the applicable process |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | When selecting/preserving document-edition members |
| Baselines | Metadata | Exact edition-reference/descriptive contract | When selecting/preserving exact editions; relevant relationship context must also be pinned or evidenced |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

These contracts replace the received Knowledge→Documentation→Document→Metadata→Identity→Classification→Relationships→Registry→Graph hierarchy. The old chain is retained in the input/diff/provenance map, not accepted as a current required service sequence. Its subject/representation relations are made explicit in §§4/6; genuine required consumption is retained here.

A full graph also needs owner-source reconciliation, consumer/provider evidence, peer-domain contracts and any required context-specific dependencies beyond these rows. Metadata descriptors may reference Identity, Classification and Governance meanings without requiring their runtime services for every representation. Exact editions and verification evidence can be supplied without an indispensable Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain.

Where sources disagree on structural direction, contract ownership or actual required cycles, record the conflict and reconcile the responsible sources. Do not rename a genuinely required edge as an association/reference to hide a cycle. This UPDATE verifies neither a globally acyclic graph nor complete dependency compatibility. ARC-004/005 and the detailed component sources retain their scheduled reconciliation.

---

# 11. Evolution Guidelines

Concepts are intended to retain stable meaning where feasible. A new abstraction requires a demonstrated need, an assessment of whether existing concepts suffice, explicit relationships and an impact analysis of consumers, domain ownership and structural scope. Extension may require contract or boundary changes; it is not guaranteed to leave the existing architecture untouched.

Changing an existing definition requires recorded architectural justification and compatibility assessment. Under the adopted review policy:

| Change | Version | Revision |
|---|---|---|
| Compatible correction/clarification preserving contractual meaning | Retain major.minor | Increment monotonically |
| Compatible additive capability | Increment minor | Increment monotonically |
| Incompatible contract/convention | Increment major and reset minor to 0 | Increment monotonically across Version changes |
| Validation with no source change | Retain | Retain; record the event centrally |

An absent Revision first becomes 1; this received source already declared R0, so this successor increments to R1. Incompatible change also requires consumer/transition evidence and later verification; a number alone does not reconcile every consumer. No earlier edition or historical approval is retroactively fabricated.

# 7. Documentation Layer

## 7.1. Purpose

Documentation defines documentary representation, logical identity, mutable classification and reusable structures. It represents Knowledge while contributing to Discovery, Governance and Preservation under applicable contracts; this participation does not change primary allocation.

---

## 7.2. Components

- Metadata
- Document Identity
- Classification
- Templates

---

## 7.3. Responsibilities

Metadata describes identified editions through applicable descriptors. Document Identity owns logical identity semantics; Classification owns category semantics; Templates defines reusable structural representations. Governance owns lifecycle and approval meaning even when Metadata represents those values.

Within Metadata, Dictionary defines descriptors and meaning, Schema organizes references to definitions, Profile constrains applicable usage, and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. This summary creates neither catalog records nor a canonical Profile and does not replace the scheduled owner specifications.

Document identity, exact edition, Version/Revision, edition Status and Baseline membership remain distinct. Stable corpus allocations do not change merely because Family, Type or location changes. Conceptual separation of content and descriptors allows coordinated evolution; it does not guarantee automatic consistency or independent revisions.

# 12. Layer Dependencies

A required dependency is directed **consumer→provider**: the consumer needs the stated provider contract in the declared scope. Allocation, documentary authority reference, semantic association, data projection, navigation and execution order are separately typed and must not be inferred solely from row order or arrows.

For cross-Layer required contracts governed here, the support order is Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation, Integration. Lower means an earlier support area in this declared order, not a lower visual row. A consumer's cross-Layer required provider belongs to an earlier support area. This does not require every consumer to depend on every earlier Layer or form an adjacent serial chain. Same-Layer required contracts are permitted under explicit ownership/interfaces and the cycle rule. Changing this structural constraint requires assessed architectural revision under §17, not an unrecorded upward-dependency exception.

Knowledge Graph→Relationships and Workflow→Policies are legitimate same-Layer pairs. The rows are architectural declarations for their stated scopes, not a verified complete graph or implementation inventory.

The received seven-box dependency chain is preserved in input/diff/view provenance, not accepted as a mandatory service or execution sequence. Its allocation meaning belongs to §4. Foundation documents referencing component sources, or Metadata representing Governance/Identity/Classification meanings, do not automatically create runtime dependencies. Conversely, an indispensable provider contract remains required even if its data arrives through a projection or an interface is labelled a reference.

The complete graph requires owner/consumer reconciliation, explicit context-specific edges and cycle/compatibility assessment beyond these rows. Unresolved peer claims remain recorded; no global acyclicity or integrated conformity is asserted.

---

# 13. Dependency Rules

The following rules govern declared structural allocation and required consumption. Their applicability is explicit; documentary navigation and semantic associations are not a substitute for evidence of actual required dependencies.

---

## 13.1. Rule 1 — Downward Dependencies

Apply the support order defined in §12 to required cross-Layer provider contracts. Record the consumer, provider, primary areas, contract, scope and responsible source edition. Same-Layer consumption is assessed through the component interface and ownership contracts.

No required edge is inferred from vertical position or an illustrative execution arrow. No arbitrary required higher-area dependency is accepted by relabelling it as reference/navigation; a changed allocation or support constraint requires a traceable compatibility/impact decision under §17.

---

## 13.2. Rule 2 — No Circular Dependencies

Circular required dependencies are prohibited in the governed contract scope, including cycles among components within an area and across areas. Assess actual required edges and source evidence, not just the area ordering. A missing edge or a different relationship label cannot establish acyclicity.

Where an actual required cycle or conflicting provider declaration is found, retain it visibly in the evidence and reconcile the responsible contracts/allocations. This working source does not certify a complete cycle-free framework graph.

---

## 13.3. Rule 3 — Independent Evolution

Preserve separation and compatible provider contracts where feasible. Independent component/Layer development remains subject to consumer constraints, coordinated descriptive/content changes and exact-edition compatibility assessment. Shared concerns do not require independent releases, and separate areas do not guarantee them.

---

## 13.4. Rule 4 — Explicit Interfaces

Required interactions name the actual provider contract, consumer use, scope and authoritative source edition. Registered components provide capability boundaries; Foundation/Architecture sources provide applicable definitions. Distinguish a definition reference from an operational interface requirement.

Implementations must identify actual input/output representations and executor evidence within their scope. This structural summary does not fabricate a missing detailed interface specification or implementation.

---

## 13.5. Rule 5 — Responsibility Isolation

Each registered component has exactly one primary structural allocation in this working model. Primary ownership does not confine all participation to one concern or forbid explicit consumer/provider collaboration. Preserve authoritative domain semantics while recording cross-cutting participation and traceable projections.

Metadata remains in Documentation; Workflow and Baselines remain in Governance. Knowledge/Preservation participation creates neither a competing owner nor an additional structural allocation. Primary reallocation requires the assessed architectural change process in §17.

---

# 18. Conclusion

The structural model distinguishes seven areas, one primary allocation per capability, cross-cutting concerns, semantic ownership and scoped required consumption. It supports assessed maintainability and evolution without guaranteeing those outcomes or implemented operational capability.
