# 5. Documentation Components

Documentation represents Knowledge through descriptive, logical-identity, classification and reusable-structure contracts. Its four capabilities retain separate semantic ownership while contributing to Governance, Discovery and Preservation.

---

## 5.1. Metadata

### 5.1.1. Purpose

Represents structured descriptors for identified documentary entities/editions under applicable owner contracts.

---

### 5.1.2. Responsibilities

Describe documents and support identity, classification, governance and discovery by represented values/references. Document Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain meanings. Dictionary defines descriptors, Schema organizes references, Profile constrains usage and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. Coordinated content/descriptor evolution is permitted; no catalog/Profile or mandatory absent value is invented.

---

## 5.2. Document Identity

### 5.2.1. Purpose

Defines stable logical document identity and its applicable allocation/preservation contracts.

---

### 5.2.2. Responsibilities

For normalized documents in scope, distinguish logical domain identity from exact edition, mutable Family/Type, physical location, Status and membership. Adopted corpus DF-SSS-NNN series are stable allocation namespaces independent of current classification; this overview performs no migration or allocation. The functional exclusions in §3 apply before normalized identity obligations. Traceability requires actual identified editions/references, not a guarantee inferred from this purpose.

---

## 5.3. Classification

### 5.3.1. Purpose

Defines semantic category meaning and applicable documentary assignments.

---

### 5.3.2. Responsibilities

Classify normalized documents using a canonical component or admitted documentary-area Family and exactly one responsibility-based Type from Architecture, Structure, Behavior, Reference. Optional Class requires an explicit definition. Classification supports governance/discovery without owning their state/approval or search semantics. Mutable classification is distinct from permanent identity, primary component allocation and physical storage; detailed owner reconciliation remains pending.

---

## 5.4. Templates

### 5.4.1. Purpose

Defines reusable documentary representations and their applicable structural constraints.

---

### 5.4.2. Responsibilities

Standardize structure and support creation through explicit types, schemas, elements, parameters and constraints. A Template definition differs from a concrete document instance. Templates references Metadata, Identity and Classification meanings rather than redefining them; it does not own workflow, policy, Baseline, Registry or storage semantics. Consistency and conformance require actual checks against the applicable contracts, not automatic success from using a template.

---

# 6. Governance Components

Governance defines documentary lifecycle, policy, review and immutable snapshot contracts. It does not itself prove an implemented process engine. Exact-edition review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct decisions/events.

---

## 6.1. Workflow

### 6.1.1. Purpose

Defines exact-edition lifecycle, transition, responsibility and evidence contracts.

---

### 6.1.2. Responsibilities

Describe documentary state transitions and publication conditions under applicable Policies. A DMS, tool or manual process executes operations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. Logical identity, Version/Revision, exact Status, approval/publication and membership are separate. Illustrative states do not create an unconditional transition graph; older approvals do not approve Draft successors.

---

## 6.2. Policies

### 6.2.1. Purpose

Defines applicable documentary governance rules and evidence requirements.

---

### 6.2.2. Responsibilities

State review, publication, approval and maintenance policies with applicability and responsible authorities. Rules govern identified editions and operations; actual author contribution, authorization, review, validation and approval remain distinct. Policy definition does not prove implementation, grant an operation automatically or replace semantic owners in other domains.

---

## 6.3. Reviews

### 6.3.1. Purpose

Defines review responsibilities and records examined scope, observations and findings.

---

### 6.3.2. Responsibilities

Technical and architectural review assess exact identified artifacts/rules and consistency within recorded coverage. Reviews may use results from Validation or Consistency Verification, whose executors record applicable checks; overlapping check domains do not create competing semantics or approval authority. A review result is evidence, not an approval, publication decision, Baseline selection or guarantee of product consequences.

---

## 6.4. Baselines

### 6.4.1. Purpose

Defines separately identified immutable selections of exact approved document editions.

---

### 6.4.2. Responsibilities

Preserve explicit selected member identity/edition coordinates and relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Approval eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion are separate checks. Release snapshots and historical traceability require scope and selection evidence; a current path or time label alone is insufficient. Draft successors do not retarget older members or inherit membership. This UPDATE creates no Baseline or missing historic approval.

---

# 7. Discovery Components

Discovery defines typed connections, catalog/network projections and access to identified entities/editions. Directories remain physical locations rather than semantic authority. Draft, historical and snapshot-specific discovery is allowed with explicit state and scope; discoverability does not confer approval.

---

## 7.1. Registry

### 7.1.1. Purpose

Defines catalog/lookup authority for its declared entity/edition scope.

---

### 7.1.2. Responsibilities

Support registration, lookup and discoverability through traceable authoritative source-edition records/projections. Catalog authority does not replace identity, classification, governance or relationship-record meaning. Derived copies retain provenance, refresh and current/stale/historical/snapshot context. Cataloguing does not make Registry an indispensable intermediary for every component or require physical single-copy storage.

---

## 7.2. Relationships

### 7.2.1. Purpose

Defines typed connection records for identified endpoints and their provenance.

---

### 7.2.2. Responsibilities

Map and preserve semantic reference, association, replacement, navigation and required-dependency kinds as applicable. Endpoint domains and identity contracts follow their entity kinds; not every endpoint gets a normalized document ID. Required edges use consumer→provider contract/scope and remain visible, including genuine cycles requiring reconciliation. Explicit records support traceability without fabricating a complete relation catalog.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

### 7.3.1. Purpose

Defines traceable semantic-network projections of identified entities and typed Relationships records.

---

### 7.3.2. Responsibilities

Support semantic navigation, dependency and impact analysis with authoritative source/edition provenance. Derived values do not acquire competing semantic authority; views declare refresh/freshness and current/historical/snapshot scope. No universal Registry-to-Graph routing or complete network/acyclicity is inferred from this capability.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

### 7.4.1. Purpose

Defines logical access through declared entity/edition and relationship views.

---

### 7.4.2. Responsibilities

Support hierarchical/contextual navigation and cross references with resolvable identified targets, state and relevant freshness context. Sources and relation meanings are explicit; navigation does not automatically impose a provider service dependency, confer approval or replace physical storage contracts.

---

## 7.5. Search

### 7.5.1. Purpose

Defines discovery of identified architectural entities through declared indexes/views.

---

### 7.5.2. Responsibilities

Support document, Metadata and semantic search with source-edition provenance and freshness/state limits. Draft and historical results are distinguished from approved/snapshot members. Intended search neither certifies completeness nor requires a universal Registry pipeline or new semantic owner.

---

# 8. Automation Components

Automation defines intended repeatable checking/generation capabilities. Applicable implementations consume authoritative owner contracts on identified inputs and provide execution evidence; architectural definitions alone establish neither installed tools nor verified outcomes.

---

## 8.1. Validation

### 8.1.1. Purpose

Defines scoped evaluation of identified requirements against exact artifacts/editions.

---

### 8.1.2. Responsibilities

Cover Metadata, identity, relationship and consistency requirements supplied by their responsible owners. Actual execution records inputs, rules, checks, observations, coverage, executor and limits. A PASS neither guarantees global correctness nor approves/publishes/selects a Baseline; subsequent changed bytes need their own assessment.

---

## 8.2. Metadata Generator

### 8.2.1. Purpose

Defines generation/completion/synchronization of descriptor representations under applicable owner rules.

---

### 8.2.2. Responsibilities

Identify exact inputs, output edition/representation, applicable Dictionary/Schema/Profile and provenance. Completion derives or requests values through declared rules; it is not permission to invent absent identity, category, lifecycle or approval facts. Generated values require applicable constraint assessment and synchronization/refresh evidence. Capability definition alone proves no implemented generator or successful result.

---

## 8.3. Registry Generator

### 8.3.1. Purpose

Defines creation/update of scoped Registry projections from authoritative source records/editions.

---

### 8.3.2. Responsibilities

Declare source/input and generated-output provenance, applicable catalog/owner rules and refresh/current-stale handling. Consistency checks state examined records, coverage and limits; generation does not replace domain or relationship-record authority. No implemented synchronization service or automatic complete catalog is inferred.

---

## 8.4. Documentation Generator

### 8.4.1. Purpose

Defines generation of documentary artifacts from identified definitions/inputs.

---

### 8.4.2. Responsibilities

Support table-of-contents, index and navigation artifact generation under applicable representation and owner contracts. Record input/output editions, referenced targets and provenance; verify relevant constraints/references in scope. Generated artifacts are representations, not new semantic authorities or automatically approved publications.

---

## 8.5. Consistency Verification

### 8.5.1. Purpose

Defines scoped cross-record/contract verification under applicable authoritative requirements.

---

### 8.5.2. Responsibilities

Check dependency, relationship and architectural consistency against declared records/editions and actual typed requirements. Record executor, examined scope, observations and limits. Shared check domains with Validation/Reviews do not imply competing rule ownership or global integrity; a partial matrix cannot certify the complete framework graph.

---

# 9. Integration Components

Integration defines optional use-case adapters to supported external environments and interfaces. Adapters consume owner/authorization contracts without becoming new semantic owners or approvers. Describing integration does not establish its implementation, completeness, performance or mandatory use.

---

## 9.1. Source Control Integration

### 9.1.1. Purpose

Defines an adapter to supported source-control provenance and versioned representations. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.2. CI/CD Integration

### 9.2.1. Purpose

Defines delivery-pipeline adapters executing scoped checks and authorized publication for identified editions. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.3. IDE Integration

### 9.3.1. Purpose

Defines supported authoring/development adapters under applicable representation and owner contracts. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.4. Documentation Platform Integration

### 9.4.1. Purpose

Defines platform publication adapters following Governance authorization for the exact edition. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

---

## 9.5. AI Integration

### 9.5.1. Purpose

Defines assisted reasoning/authoring against identified domain contracts and source evidence. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred. AI assistance does not acquire domain-semantic or approval authority. They are scoped architectural declarations, not a verified complete graph, implementation inventory or execution sequence.

Circular required dependencies between components, within/across areas, are prohibited in the governed contract scope. Assess actual edges and owner/consumer evidence. A genuine indispensable contract/cycle must remain visible and be reconciled; do not conceal it by changing a relationship label. Documentary definition references do not automatically require an upper-area runtime service, and semantic ownership cannot be reassigned merely to make a graph appear acyclic.

The complete graph requires detailed owner-source reconciliation and context-specific requirements beyond these rows. This source certifies neither global acyclicity nor integrated consumer compatibility.

---

# 16. Conclusion

Components define architectural capability boundaries and intended collaboration. The register, owner distinctions and typed required contracts support assessed modularity, maintainability and traceability; these properties depend on actual contracts and evidence rather than being guaranteed by allocation.

This edition applies eight findings and two warnings as **Corrected—pending validation**. Exact-source validation and consuming-source/integrated reconciliation remain pending. Detailed specifications state requirements, not proof of complete operational implementations. Draft/unassigned confers no approval, publication or Baseline membership.

## 16.1. Compatibility assessment

Received §12 declares an untyped dependency hierarchy, §§5–9 blur semantic owner/operational responsibilities, §11.5 requires harmless extension and §16 states complete operational behavior. V2.0 replaces those interpretations with scoped required contracts/support order, explicit domain and executor boundaries, evidence-limited capability claims and assessed transitions.

This is an **incompatible normative contract reconciliation**, not merely Type reclassification or explanatory links. Version 1.0 increments major to 2.0; declared Revision 0 increments to 1 without reset. DF-ARC-005/path and all 23 capability names/allocations remain unchanged. Component/Class and identity allocations are not invented; the operating policy is linked in §14.

## 16.2. Local edition history

Mixed human/assistant contributions retain their attribution. Later disk edits require resulting-edition/byte assessment; prior results do not transfer automatically or assign responsibility for consequences of the final product. No original author, historic approval or Baseline selection is invented.

## 16.3. Propagation and verification limits

This UPDATE modifies Components and central report/tracking/evidence only. Concepts, Layers and the six Foundation sources retain their earlier exact-source validation scopes; their previous notes about received Components conflicts are event-time evidence, not validation or completed propagation of this successor.

Overview, Principles, Terminology and detailed component owners retain their scheduled cycles and remaining discrepancies. Dictionary/Profile, identity/classification and complete owner/consumer/dependency compatibility need further reconciliation. No general ID/path migration, new component/Layer, Metadata Element record or external implementation specification is introduced.

M11 remains In Progress: Concepts/Layers C, Components S, four peers O; no Components completion date. All 19 global records remain Open and the 77 earlier localized closures retain their own source/scope. The report records input/output/affected hashes, complete before/after and construction evidence; this source's pending UPDATE history is not overwritten by a later result. No integrated conformity, release, publication, selected snapshot or final Context-Reviewed.zip is claimed.

# 4. Architectural Position

Allocation, component ownership, physical containment and documentary classification are separate relationships.

<!-- original-section-view: 4 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §4 — Allocation and documentary containment.**

| Entity | Relation | Target | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registered component | has one primary structural allocation in | Applicable structural area | Canonical register/Layers contract; cross-cutting participation remains possible |
| Component documentation set | describes contracts of | Identified component | Documentary membership does not create another component or owner |
| Component directory | physically groups | Functional entry point and category directories | Physical location, not semantic authority or runtime dependence |
| Normalized source | has primary documentary responsibility | One of the four Types | Classification by content, independent of permanent ID and path |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Component documentation can be consulted separately while referencing required owner/consumer contracts. It does not guarantee independent evolution, independent releases or complete understanding without relevant provider definitions. Documentary references and containment are not required runtime-service edges.

---

# 5. Component Directory Structure

A **complete component documentation set** shall provide README.md and the four category directories below. This is an organization requirement, not proof that all required content exists or is correct. The same contract applies to every component; partial supplied sets must be identified as incomplete rather than silently exempted or certified.

<!-- original-section-view: 5 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §5 — Physical component documentation organization.**

| Entry relative to the component root | Kind | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| README.md | Non-normalized file | Entry point, source map, scope and coverage information |
| 01-Architecture/ | Directory | Conceptual foundations, principles, models and decisions |
| 02-Structure/ | Directory | Organization, schemas, composition, relationships and structural restrictions/catalogs |
| 03-Behavior/ | Directory | Subject-specific lifecycle, validation, governance, processes and extensibility |
| 04-Reference/ | Directory | Consolidated specifications, consultation, terminology, examples and recommendations |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Applicable documents are placed according to primary responsibility. Titles such as Schema, Dictionary, Lifecycle and Specification are role names, not additional Type values or automatic placement rules. A directory does not assign semantic authority, change Family or recalculate identity.

An empty directory satisfies only its presence check, not content coverage. Do not manufacture empty documents or an implemented capability to make a set appear complete. Required source roles and unfilled responsibilities are assessed under §16. The received corpus may contain partial sets; that evidence records an unmet requirement, not an exception to this contract.

---

# 6. Component README

Every complete component documentation set shall provide README.md as its functional entry point. It remains non-normalized under §3.

Its content shall identify the component, purpose, responsibilities, scope and primary architectural position; map actual supplied documents and relevant editions; distinguish present, planned, absent and not-applicable roles with evidence; identify owner references, dependencies/related components, applicable roadmap and conformance coverage. A recommended reading order may be given where useful, with advisory meaning under §11.

Document maps and roadmap references shall resolve to actual intended targets. A canonical name may differ from its directory alias, such as Document Identity versus DocumentIdentity. Preserve the distinction and assess stale maps explicitly. A map is a representation of sources, not a competing semantic owner or proof of approval.

Required dependencies shall identify consumer, provider, contract and scope; reference/navigation associations remain separately typed. Do not conceal a genuinely indispensable provider or cycle by calling it a documentation link. No complete dependency graph is inferred from a README.

---

# 7. Architecture Documentation

The 01-Architecture category organizes conceptual foundations of the component. Typical roles include the following; they are examples, not universally mandatory filenames.

| Role | Responsibility and applicability |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Defines purpose, boundaries, principles and owner/consumer architecture |
| Concepts | Defines conceptual meaning and distinctions |
| Model | Defines the domain's conceptual entities and relationships |
| Elements | Defines conceptual elements where that is the source's primary responsibility |

Additional conceptual documents require demonstrated need and clear owner boundaries. A domain-specific Elements source may instead primarily organize a structural catalog; its content and applicable owner contract determine Type/placement. This overview does not automatically reclassify or move every similarly titled source.

---

# 8. Structure Documentation

The 02-Structure category defines composition and structural constraints without taking over domain semantic ownership.

| Role | Responsibility and applicability |
|---|---|
| Schema | Organizes/references domain definitions and structural constraints; does not independently redefine their semantics |
| Relationships | Defines structural connection organization when that is its primary responsibility; actual relation kinds and endpoint contracts remain explicit |
| Constraints | Defines structural restrictions where that is the primary responsibility |
| Dictionary or entry catalog | Organizes authoritative domain definitions/records when catalog composition is primary; not limited to terminology |

A terminology consultation document can use Type Reference and its corresponding category even when titled Dictionary. A structural entry catalog uses Type Structure when that is the demonstrated primary responsibility. Domain definitions, source composition and consultation purpose must be assessed together; title or received path alone decides neither.

Metadata Dictionary defines Metadata Elements and their semantics; Schema organizes references, Profile constrains applicable usage and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain meanings even when Metadata represents their values. This summary creates no canonical Element record, missing Profile or automatic consistency guarantee.

The exact document set depends on the domain and declared requirements. Received README maps and actual paths can disagree; reconcile the responsible sources and consumers through their scheduled cycles rather than silently relocating files in this UPDATE.

---

# 9. Behavior Documentation

The 03-Behavior category defines subject-specific processes, transitions and controlled evolution. It does not by itself establish an executing system.

| Role | Responsibility and applicability |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | Identifies the governed entity, states, permitted transitions and scope; may govern definitions, elements, instances or document editions |
| Validation | Defines applicable rules, examined artifacts/context, coverage and result evidence |
| Governance | Defines domain responsibilities, change/decision contracts and required evidence |
| Extensibility | Defines controlled extension, owner/consumer impact and transition requirements |

A Classification-definition lifecycle is distinct from a document edition's Version/Revision/Status and Workflow governance. Component maturity, implementation state and Baseline membership are also separate facts. State lists do not imply a complete universal transition graph or permission model.

DF defines these contracts; the applicable DMS/tool/manual executor supplies actual inputs, actions and observations. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or exact Baseline selection. Review, validation, approval, publication and membership remain separate events. A scoped check result transfers neither to unseen sources nor later changed bytes.

---

# 10. Reference Documentation

The 04-Reference category contains consultation and consolidated reference roles, which may carry explicitly scoped normative or informative statements.

| Role | Responsibility and authority limit |
|---|---|
| Specification | Consolidates identified applicable requirements, references and conformance obligations; states its normative scope explicitly |
| Best Practices | Provides recommendations, declared informative unless an applicable contract explicitly adopts particular requirements |
| Examples | Provides illustrative usage with declared scope and limits; not evidence of implementation or universal compliance |
| Terminology reference | Provides domain-term consultation when that is its primary responsibility; canonical owners remain identified |

Normative or informative authority follows explicit applicable declarations and incorporation of identified sources/editions. It does not follow directory, Type=Reference or the word Specification alone. Supporting Architecture, Structure or Behavior sources can define normative requirements, and other Reference roles can be explicitly normative in scope. The received blanket statement that all remaining documents are informative is not retained.

A consolidated specification must identify the responsible sources it incorporates and how conflicts/applicability are assessed. This organization contract does not replace those domain requirements. Presence, normative wording or successful checking does not approve or publish a Draft edition, grant Baseline membership or establish implemented conformance.

---

# 14. Optional Documents

Not every component requires the same document count. Security, Performance, Compliance, Migration, Interoperability and Integration are example topic roles, not new Type values or obligatory files.

Introduce a role when justified by domain requirements. Assign its primary responsibility to the existing four-Type taxonomy and corresponding category. Record applicability, owner, affected consumers and references; avoid duplicating semantic authority or manufacturing missing specifications. A required responsibility may be covered by an identified consolidated source if the applicable owner contract permits that coverage and the mapping is explicit.

Optional content does not waive the complete-set organization in §5 or a declared required source responsibility in §16. Missing required content is an unmet requirement; a not-applicable role needs its reason and owner evidence.

---

# 10. Responsibilities

All fourteen received responsibilities remain, qualified to their own subjects rather than an assertion that all detailed definitions or implementations are complete.

| Received subject | Current qualified responsibility / limit |
|---|---|
| defining the architectural concept of document classification; | Own the applicable classification concept under common Architecture, not general document or descriptor semantics. |
| defining the classification model; | Own the intended conceptual Model contract; authentic supplied DF-CLS-003 content is unresolved and not manufactured here. |
| defining classification elements; | Own classification dimension/category/value roles with explicit definitions, not every Metadata descriptor. |
| defining the classification schema; | Own classification structure/assignment conditions while Metadata owns represented descriptors/schema/profile duties; no accepted merged schema is invented. |
| defining classification lifecycle concepts; | Own domain definition/assignment state meaning and applicability; do not copy document Status or DID lifecycle as universal aliases. |
| establishing the semantic basis for classification validation; | Provide responsible classification validation conditions; actual Automation checking contract and real executor/evidence are separate. |
| defining classification governance requirements; | Provide domain governance/usage/change conditions to responsible decisions; do not implement common Workflow/Policies/Reviews/Baselines operations. |
| defining classification relationships; | Own classification relation meanings and assignment context; Relationships owns actual typed connection/endpoints/provenance contracts. |
| defining classification constraints; | Own applicable classification constraints with exact source/subject/context and coverage, not invented complete cardinalities. |
| supporting controlled classification extensibility; | Distinguish ordinary compatible extension from necessary assessed normative revision under §28. |
| establishing classification best practices; | Maintain explicitly informative recommendations; citation or Type does not turn all advice into mandatory rules. |
| maintaining the classification dictionary; | Maintain scoped classification vocabulary with owner/source/context references, not a blanket universal glossary takeover. |
| providing the consolidated classification specification; | Provide scoped normative integration subject to real source agreement; file presence and Model reference do not prove complete consolidation. |
| providing classification examples. | Provide informative illustrations, not new requirements, actual allocations, observed validation or implementation proof. |

The historical documentary progression is preserved in §§22/29/37. It is not a runtime execution sequence, automatic completion or evidence of an authentic missing Model.

---

# 11. Non-Responsibilities

The ten received non-responsibilities remain with their actual owner boundaries.

| Received subject | Current qualified responsibility / limit |
|---|---|
| assign permanent document identities; | Document Identity defines applicable document allocation/preservation contracts; actual authorized executor differs. Categories/assignments are not automatically document allocations. |
| define general document metadata; | Metadata owns general descriptor/schema/profile/instance contracts; Classification still owns its represented category/assignment meanings under common rules. |
| manage physical document storage; | Physical storage/execution remains with the actual system/process; logical classification representations and their evidence obligations remain applicable. |
| manage repositories; | Repository operation/custody is not Classification authority; actual movement can affect reference/index context without redefining category meaning. |
| define document content; | Document content authoring is separate, though content and descriptors/assignments may need coordinated changes and checks. |
| implement document workflows; | Common Workflow contracts and actual DMS/tool/manual process remain separate from Classification domain lifecycle/governance conditions. |
| maintain the document registry; | Registry owns registration/index records and their provenance/freshness, not classification meanings. |
| implement discovery mechanisms; | Registered Discovery components own their contracts; Classification supplies semantic inputs without guaranteeing a deployed outcome. |
| implement automation; | Automation components define scoped checking/generation/consistency responsibilities; actual authorized executor/observations must be evidenced. |
| define external system integration. | Integration components/adapters own actual exchange interfaces; applicable classification meaning, authorization, mappings/provenance/checks remain required. |

Providing information, reusing definitions or maintaining a legitimate projection does not assume another owner's semantic responsibility. These exclusions do not waive Classification's own schema/lifecycle/validation/governance/interface requirements.

---

# 12. Relationship with Metadata

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                Metadata
                    │
                describes
                    │
                    ▼

                 Document
                    │
             is organized by
                    │
                    ▼

              Classification

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Metadata | Descriptor/representation owner, including Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles; category semantics are not transferred by representation |
| describes | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| is organized by | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |

**Relation scope:** Metadata description and document classification association; actual required Classification→Metadata scope is separately stated.

Metadata and Classification are complementary: Metadata represents standardized descriptors and Classification owns their classification category/value/assignment meanings in applicable contexts. Dictionary defines descriptors; Schema organizes them; Profile constrains usage for a declared context without redefining owner semantics; Instance supplies values under one effective Profile. No canonical Element IDs, complete Profile, actual instance or accepted merged field catalog is created by these summaries.

The received Metadata→Document→Classification arrows express description and assignment/semantic organization, not a required execution sequence. Classification→Metadata is an actual required provider declaration where governed metadata representation is indispensable for the document classification in scope. Exact inputs/outputs, source editions, owner/consumer interfaces and real uses must still be assessed; merely changing the relation name cannot dissolve a genuine cycle.

The functional Classification README§10 currently states “However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.” That actual unchanged assertion is a pending owner-source discrepancy: for normalized-document classification meaning, current ARC-003§§5.4/5.6, ARC-005§§5.1/5.3 and Policy3 retain Classification/common rule ownership while Metadata owns descriptor representation. This does not transfer every unrelated field named Type or all Metadata meanings to Classification. The README and Metadata owner-source coordination must be separately traced before integrated agreement is claimed (§39).

---

# 13. Relationship with Document Identity

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                    Document
                    │
                    ├── Document Identity
                    │        └── identifies the document
                    │
                    └── Classification
                             └── organizes the document

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| Document Identity | Qualified assigned document-key/domain/association meaning provider; not current classification or every support record |
| identifies the document | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |
| organizes the document | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |

**Relation scope:** Two distinct capabilities about one document; ordinary classification change does not reconstruct governing K.

Document Identity defines governing qualified Domain+Identifier and applicable assignment/preservation contracts. Ordinary reclassification changes category/assignment/descriptive context without reconstructing assigned K or its same-logical-document association. Current Family/Type/component/path/Status/Version/Revision does not recalculate a valid stable DF allocation-series code.

The Documentation Framework corpus uses DF-SSS-NNN: DF renders the governing domain, SSS is a registered stable uppercase three-letter allocation series, NNN is 001–999 and 000 is excluded. Allocated/retired numbers are not reused; a gap proves no availability; at 999, register an unused governed continuation series rather than recycle or widen syntax. Other entity/domain contracts are not automatically DF document IDs. No allocation or series reservation occurs here.

Mutable identity support records, definition/assignment states, descriptors, references and exact editions differ from K. Current DID-014 V2.0 R1 distinguishes K from complete supporting R with all five mandatory logical roles, scoped State assertion and canonical-target descriptor; incoming0..N connections remain separate. That local working decision has remaining field/interface/peer/consumer propagation and is not an approved merged classification/Metadata record.

Necessary governing normative/domain/representation change follows actual prior/new authority and §28 transition evidence; it is not arbitrary reassignment, silent historical retargeting or an inference that every effect is harmless. Preserve category/assignment identities, exact historical definition/edition/context and snapshot continuity under their own owners.

---

# 14. Relationship with Templates

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
                 Template
                    │
            provides structure
                    │
                    ▼

                 Document
                    │
     receives semantic classification
                    │
                    ▼

              Classification

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Template | Reusable representation definition/constraint owner; applicable instance and required use differ from semantic category meaning |
| provides structure | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Document | Applicable logical-document subject; not every file/entity automatically normalized, assigned or classified |
| receives semantic classification | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |

**Relation scope:** Template representation and semantic assignment; no mandatory Template runtime route or classification authority transfer.

Templates defines reusable documentary representations and structural constraints. Classification owns category/assignment meanings; Metadata owns represented descriptors. A template definition differs from its concrete document instances, and an entity described by a template is not automatically a normalized document allocation.

The received Template→Document→Classification view shows representation and semantic assignment, not that Templates controls classification meaning or every assignment must pass through a template service. Classification→Templates is required only where an actual indispensable template representation contract applies; otherwise the collaboration is optional/contextual. Actual source/schema/profile/instance compatibility, authority and checks remain needed. Using a template alone does not prove conformance, approve a successor or populate a canonical classification/Metadata catalog.

---

# 19. Relationship with Validation

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
              Classification
                    │
       defines semantic conditions
                    │ 
                    ▼

                Validation
                    │
                verifies
                    │
                    ▼

        Classification Assignment

```

| Original label | Current typed subject / role |
|---|---|
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |
| defines semantic conditions | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Validation | Automation scoped evaluation contract; Classification supplies domain rule meanings and actual authorized executor/evidence remains separate |
| verifies | Received relation label qualified by this section; semantic/record/required/execution/decision meanings are not interchangeable |
| Classification Assignment | Actual intended subject-to-definition/value association under scheme/edition/time/context and authority, not automatically a document allocation |

**Relation scope:** Domain rule provision and evaluation of an assignment; structural required direction/executor/permission are not granted by data flow.

Classification supplies semantic validation conditions for actual subjects; detailed CLS-007 owns applicable classification checking requirements, including its own declared outcomes/coverage. Automation's Validation component defines scoped evaluation responsibilities; an actual authorized tool/manual/DMS executor performs checks and records inputs/rules/source editions/context/observations/limits. No installed executor or indispensable upward Classification→Automation runtime edge is inferred merely from the received arrows. In their rule-consumption scope, Validation→Classification uses the domain's rules; selected rule provision/data flow and structural dependency are different relations.

Declare the claim (definition/category/assignment/relationship/document context), exact applicable mandatory rules and governing authority before claiming success. A successful subset is narrower evidence; missing/unperformed/conflicting mandatory evidence withholds broader conformity without fabricating a violation. Keep actual negative observations and unresolved owner-source limitations. DID-007 result labels are not imported as universal CLS outcome vocabulary: received CLS-007 has its own Valid/Valid with Warnings/Invalid and severity definitions, pending its scheduled reconciliation.

Evaluation does not mutate what is checked. Writing a result is a separate record; correcting a document/assignment requires its own authorized change/provenance/version and later assessment. Validation supplies evidence, not operational permission, governance acceptance, formal architectural approval, publication or exact Baseline selection. Authentic Model and conflicting source authority gaps are explicit limits, not fabricated completed checks.

---

# 20. Architectural Dependencies

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

```text
               Foundation
                    │
                    ▼

              Architecture
                    │
                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

              Classification

```

|---|---|
| Foundation | Declared support/allocation area; exact registered component/contract meaning applies, not mandatory page-order execution |
| Architecture | Declared support/allocation area; exact registered component/contract meaning applies, not mandatory page-order execution |
| Documentation Layer | Declared support/allocation area; exact registered component/contract meaning applies, not mandatory page-order execution |
| Classification | Classification component/domain meaning in this view; actual category/assignment subjects and provider interfaces are qualified in the section |

**Relation scope:** Common support/allocation context, not mandatory Foundation→Architecture→Documentation→Classification execution.

Classification uses common Foundation/Architecture definitions and structural contracts. The received Foundation→Architecture→Documentation→Classification chain expresses support/allocation context, not universal serial operational dependence. A required dependency identifies an indispensable provider contract in a declared subject/context; direction is consumer→provider, regardless of page placement or data-flow arrows.

Apply ARC-004§§12–13 and ARC-005§12: Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration are support precedence, not a requirement to consume every earlier provider or adjacent area. Required cross-Layer providers precede consumers in that governed order. Same-Layer contracts need explicit ownership/interfaces and cycle assessment; required cycles are prohibited. Changing this structural rule needs separately assessed architectural revision, not an arbitrary exception or renamed edge.

Common documentary authority, allocation, semantic association, representation, projection, navigation and execution differ. A detailed consumer/provider/required-interface inventory and actual owner-source reconciliation remain necessary before complete compatibility/acyclicity claims. Section33's received not-implementation-dependency disclaimer does not make genuinely indispensable provider contracts optional.

---

# 21. Required Supporting Capabilities

All three received supporting capability subjects remain, with actual scope:

| Received subject | Current qualified responsibility / limit |
|---|---|
| Metadata; | Classification→Metadata where governed document descriptor/schema/profile/instance representation is required; exact context/owner interfaces and reciprocal claims remain assessed, not universally independent. |
| Document Identity; | Classification→Document Identity for applicable assigned normalized documents being classified/referenced; category/assignment identities and pre-allocation subjects keep their own contracts. |
| Templates where classification information must be represented structurally. | Classification→Templates only where the actual template representation is indispensable; not every category or assignment requires a template or runtime service. |

No duplication of semantic authority is allowed by implementation, but legitimate repeated values, aliases, representations and projections are not by themselves competing definitions. MTD-001§8.1 currently says Metadata depends only upon Foundation/Architecture, while its support table and actual DID sources/functional README contain peer required claims. Current DID-009 and README retain Metadata→Document Identity and Document Identity→Metadata in their declared scopes. Preserve actual statements and assess responsible core/descriptor/provider interfaces; scope names alone do not prove independence or dissolve a genuine required cycle. These sources are unchanged and no full DAG is certified.

---

# 22. Architectural Boundaries

**Received conceptual view retained at its original section; current meaning is qualified below.**

# Classification Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, assigning and governing the semantic classification of documents within the Documentation Framework.

# 1. Overview

The **Classification** component defines how documents are organized into semantic categories according to a defined classification model.

Classification provides a semantic mechanism for organizing documents within the Documentation Framework while remaining independent of their physical representation.

The component establishes the concepts, models, elements, structures, rules and governance required to define and maintain classification systems.

---

# 2. Purpose

The purpose of the Classification component is to provide a consistent and controlled mechanism for classifying documentation.

Classification enables documents to be organized according to their semantic characteristics rather than according to their physical location.

The component provides the architectural foundation required for:

- semantic organization;
- document discovery;
- document grouping;
- classification-based relationships;
- validation;
- governance;
- automation.

---

# 3. Architectural Position

Classification belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

Conceptually:

```text

                         Documentation Layer

                    ┌───────────────────────────┐
                    │ Metadata                  │
                    │ Document Identity         │
                    │ Classification            │
                    │ Templates                 │
                    └───────────────────────────┘

```

Classification works together with Metadata and Document Identity while maintaining its own architectural responsibility.

---

# 4. Responsibility

The Classification component is responsible for:

- defining classification concepts;
- defining classification models;
- defining classification elements;
- defining classification schemas;
- defining classification assignments;
- defining classification relationships;
- defining classification constraints;
- defining classification lifecycle;
- defining classification validation;
- defining classification governance;
- defining classification extensibility;
- defining authoritative classification terminology.

Classification does not define:

- document identity;
- document metadata in general;
- document templates;
- document workflows;
- physical repository organization.

Those responsibilities belong to other components of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 5. Architectural Independence

Classification is independent of the physical representation of documentation.

The semantic organization defined by Classification shall not depend on:

- directory structures;
- filenames;
- repositories;
- storage technologies;
- document formats;
- implementation technologies.

A physical organization may reflect conceptual distinctions established by Classification, but the physical representation does not define those distinctions.

The relationship is therefore:

```text

         Classification Semantics
                    │
                    ▼

       Architectural Representation
                    │
                    ▼

          Physical Representation

```

and not:

```text

          Physical Representation
                    │
                    ▼

         Classification Semantics

```

---

# 6. Relationship with Other Components

## 6.1. Metadata

Metadata provides descriptive information about documents that may participate in classification.

Classification uses that information without redefining the responsibility of Metadata.

---

## 6.2. Document Identity

Document Identity provides the logical identity of the documents to which classifications may be assigned.

Classification does not establish document identity.

---

## 6.3. Templates

Templates may define standardized structures for representing classification information.

Classification defines the semantic classification model rather than the template used to represent it.

---

## 6.4. Workflow

Workflow may use classification information when determining or controlling document processes.

Classification does not define workflow behavior.

---

## 6.5. Policies

Policies may establish rules governing the use or administration of classifications.

Classification provides the classification structures to which such policies may apply.

---

## 6.6. Registry and Discovery

Classification may provide semantic information used by Registry and Discovery mechanisms to organize and locate documentation.

---

## 6.7. Knowledge Graph

Classification concepts and relationships may contribute semantic information to the Knowledge Graph.

---

# 7. Documentation Structure

The Classification component is defined through the following documents:

| Order | Document | Description |
|------:|----------|-------------|
| 1 | DF-CLS-001 — Classification Architecture | Defines the architectural position, responsibility and boundaries of Classification. |
| 2 | DF-CLS-002 — Classification Concepts | Defines the fundamental concepts of Classification. |
| 3 | DF-CLS-003 — Classification Model | Defines the conceptual model governing classification. |
| 4 | DF-CLS-004 — Classification Elements | Defines the elements that constitute a classification system. |
| 5 | DF-CLS-005 — Classification Schema | Defines the formal structure of classification systems. |
| 6 | DF-CLS-006 — Classification Lifecycle | Defines the lifecycle of classification structures and assignments. |
| 7 | DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation | Defines classification validation and conformance rules. |
| 8 | DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance | Defines governance and control of classification systems. |
| 9 | DF-CLS-009 — Classification Relationships | Defines relationships between classification elements and related entities. |
| 10 | DF-CLS-010 — Classification Constraints | Defines constraints that preserve classification integrity. |
| 11 | DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility | Defines mechanisms for extending classification systems. |
| 12 | DF-CLS-012 — Classification Best Practices | Documents recommended practices for classification design and maintenance. |
| 13 | DF-CLS-013 — Classification Dictionary | Defines authoritative Classification terminology. |
| 14 | DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification | Consolidates the normative Classification specification. |
| 15 | DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples | Provides representative examples of Classification usage. |

---

# 8. Documentation Progression

The documentation follows four major stages.

## 8.1. Conceptual Foundation

```text

    DF-CLS-001
    DF-CLS-002
    DF-CLS-003

```

Defines the architectural and conceptual foundations of Classification.

## 8.2. Structural Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-004
    DF-CLS-005

```

Defines the elements and structures used to represent classifications.

## 8.3. Operational Definition

```text

    DF-CLS-006
    DF-CLS-007
    DF-CLS-008
    DF-CLS-009
    DF-CLS-010
    DF-CLS-011

```

Defines lifecycle, validation, governance, relationships, constraints and extensibility.

## 8.4. Consolidation and Reference

```text

    DF-CLS-012
    DF-CLS-013
    DF-CLS-014
    DF-CLS-015

```

Provides best practices, terminology, normative specification and examples.

---

# 9. Classification Model

The Classification component establishes a conceptual distinction between:

```text

                    Classification System
                    │
                    ├── Classification Model
                    │
                    ├── Classification Elements
                    │
                    ├── Classification Relationships
                    │
                    ├── Classification Constraints
                    │
                    └── Classification Assignments

```

The detailed definitions of these concepts belong to the respective Classification specifications.

---

# 10. Classification and Metadata Type

Metadata `Type` may participate in classification.

However, the semantic meaning of `Type` remains defined by Metadata.

Classification shall not redefine Metadata `Type` merely to support its own model.

The relationship between `Type`, semantic classification and physical organization shall be addressed consistently across the Documentation Framework.

In particular, the existence of physical directory distinctions shall not be interpreted as evidence that those directories define the semantics of `Type`.

---

# 11. Validation

Classification shall support validation at multiple levels:

1. element existence;
2. structural validity;
3. value validity;
4. semantic validity;
5. cross-element consistency;
6. cross-document consistency;
7. architectural consistency.

The detailed validation rules are defined by **DF-CLS-007 — Classification Validation**.

---

# 12. Governance

Classification systems shall be subject to controlled governance.

Governance concerns include:

- ownership;
- responsibility;
- approval;
- change control;
- review;
- publication;
- deprecation;
- retirement.

The detailed governance model is defined by **DF-CLS-008 — Classification Governance**.

---

# 13. Extensibility

Classification shall support controlled evolution.

Extensions may include:

- new classification categories;
- new classification elements;
- new attributes;
- schema extensions;
- new relationships;
- additional classification models.

Extensions shall preserve established semantics and maintain compatibility with existing classification definitions where required.

The detailed extensibility model is defined by **DF-CLS-011 — Classification Extensibility**.

---

# 14. Authoritative Specification

The complete normative definition of Classification is consolidated in:

**DF-CLS-014 — Classification Specification**

The other Classification documents provide the concepts, models, structures, rules and supporting material from which the specification is established.

The specification is therefore the authoritative reference for the complete Classification component.

---

# 15. Examples

Representative examples are maintained separately in:

**DF-CLS-015 — Classification Examples**

Examples are intended to demonstrate the application of the Classification specification without becoming normative definitions themselves.

---

# 16. Roadmap

The development sequence of the Classification component is defined by:

**DF-RDM-030 — Classification Roadmap**

The roadmap describes the progressive development of the component but does not itself define the Classification architecture.

---

# 17. Design Principles

The Classification component follows the following principles:

- **Semantic Independence** — Classification represents semantic organization rather than physical storage.
- **Architectural Separation** — Classification maintains clear boundaries with other Documentation Framework components.
- **Explicit Semantics** — classification concepts shall have explicit and unambiguous meanings.
- **Consistency** — classification definitions shall remain internally and cross-component consistent.
- **Traceability** — classification changes shall remain traceable.
- **Controlled Evolution** — classification systems shall evolve through defined lifecycle and governance mechanisms.
- **Extensibility** — classification shall support controlled extension.
- **Single Source of Truth** — authoritative classification concepts shall have a single canonical definition.
- **Technology Independence** — classification shall not depend on implementation technologies.

---

# 18. Component Completion

The Classification component is considered architecturally complete when its documentation establishes:

- the architectural responsibility of Classification;
- its fundamental concepts;
- its conceptual model;
- its elements;
- its schema;
- its lifecycle;
- its validation rules;
- its governance;
- its relationships;
- its constraints;
- its extensibility mechanisms;
- its best practices;
- its authoritative terminology;
- its normative specification;
- representative examples.

---

# 19. Future Evolution

Future versions of the Classification component may introduce additional capabilities such as:

- advanced taxonomy models;
- ontology-based classification;
- semantic classification;
- automated classification;
- AI-assisted classification;
- classification quality metrics;
- interoperability mechanisms;
- semantic impact analysis.

Such extensions shall preserve the architectural boundaries and principles established by the Documentation Framework.

---

# 20. Change History

| Date | Version | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| 2026-08-09 | 1.0 | Initial Classification component README. |

---

**End of Document**

---

# 4. Scope

The component's scope includes identity concepts, models, elements/schema, constraints, identity lifecycle, validation, governance, typed relationships, assessed extensibility, specifications and examples. Detailed sources retain their responsibilities; this architecture does not invent a canonical merged field catalog or certify all peer requirements.

For applicable normalized documents, logical identity remains associated with the same document across ordinary content/descriptor, classification, representation, repository and document-edition changes. Exact edition coordinates, document Status, identity-record assignment/preservation/retirement evidence, maturity and Baseline membership are separate facts. A mutable state record is not a replacement for the stable identity key.

Unassigned concerns a pre-allocation subject, not an already assigned Domain+Identifier key. Retirement preserves allocated-number reservation, document association/history and reference interpretation; it does not guarantee a running resolver or retrievable content. Document lifecycle and identity-record lifecycle can have distinct subjects/contracts. The source does not prescribe a universal transition or permission graph.

DID-003/004/005/006/010/014 currently disagree on reference cardinality, mandatory State/Canonical Reference fields and identity state terminology. Those actual claims are preserved in §12.3 for full owner cycles. The architectural distinctions here neither merge incompatible schemas nor silently remove/add their mandatory fields. No Metadata Dictionary Element, Profile or canonical state record is fabricated.

---

# 5. Out of Scope

The following roles are separate from document identity semantic ownership. Area labels, registered capability contracts and operational executors are identified separately; naming an owner proves no implemented service.

| Received responsibility | Responsible contract/role | Operational or semantic boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document metadata | Metadata plus applicable semantic domain owners | Dictionary defines, Schema organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile; descriptive representation does not replace identity |
| Document classification | Classification | Family/Type and other category meanings remain mutable and separately owned |
| Registry management | Registry | Catalog/lookup contracts and provenance; actual registration/lookup executed by an applicable system/process |
| Discovery services | Discovery area: Registry, Relationships, Knowledge Graph, Navigation, Search | Area groups capabilities; it is not another component or mandatory routing intermediary |
| Workflow management | Workflow and applicable Policies | Subject-specific transitions/rules; DMS/tool/manual operation, not an implemented DF workflow engine |
| Version control | Documentary edition contracts versus source-control systems/adapters | Version/Revision/Status semantics follow applicable governance/edition contracts; repository commits and Source Control Integration adapters do not define them |
| Repository management | DMS or other applicable external system | Organization, storage, permissions and physical-location execution |
| Storage technologies | Applicable implementations/external systems | Persistence mechanisms preserve applicable representation/provenance requirements |
| Identifier generation algorithms | Applicable allocation executor | Generate/allocate under identity-domain rules and collision/reservation evidence; no algorithm supplied here |
| Persistence mechanisms | Applicable implementation/external system | Store identity/edition/context records without acquiring identity semantics |

Governance is an area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines; it is not a single invented component owning all operational management. Reviews records examined scope/results; Baselines defines immutable selected exact approved editions and context. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or snapshot inclusion.

---

# 8. Dependencies

The following supplied sources provide documentary architecture/process authority and orientation. These links are not themselves required runtime service edges; actual required contract consumption is typed in §9. Each source retains its own applicable clauses and exact examined-edition scope.

- [DF-FND-001 — Framework Manifest](../../../00-Foundation/DF-FND-001-FrameworkManifest.md) — Framework interpretation and responsibility boundaries.
- [DF-FND-004 — Architectural Blueprint](../../../00-Foundation/DF-FND-004-ArchitecturalBlueprint.md) — Foundational contracts and selected required pairs.
- [DF-ARC-001 — Architecture Overview](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-001-ArchitectureOverview.md) — Common model, allocation and actual evidence limits.
- [DF-ARC-002 — Architectural Principles](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-002-ArchitecturalPrinciples.md) — Applicable AP clauses, evolution and evidence boundaries.
- [DF-ARC-003 — Architectural Concepts](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-003-ArchitecturalConcepts.md) — Entity/edition/relationship interpretation.
- [DF-ARC-004 — Architectural Layers](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-004-ArchitecturalLayers.md) — Support order, same-Layer interfaces and prohibited-cycle assessment.
- [DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-005-ArchitecturalComponents.md) — Registered identity capability, allocation and owner roles.
- [DF-ARC-006 — Terminology](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-006-Terminology.md) — Qualified identity, domain, identifier, edition and state meanings.
- [DF-FND-006 — Design Rationale](../../../00-Foundation/DF-FND-006-DesignRationale.md) — Rationale for identity/description/governance boundaries.
- [DF-ARC-007 — Component Documentation Structure](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-007-ComponentDocumentationStructure.md) — Source-role organization and scoped conformance requirements.
- [DF-RVW-001 — Review Policy](../../../03-Governance/Reviews/03-Behavior/DF-RVW-001-ReviewPolicy.md) — Adopted corpus allocation/classification/edition/tracking rules.
- [DF-RVW-002 — Review Report](../../../03-Governance/Reviews/04-Reference/DF-RVW-002-ReviewReport.md) — Actual examined hashes, corrections and pending peer/global reconciliation.

Required dependencies are consumer→provider contracts with scope, exact responsible editions and interfaces. Cross-Layer provider precedence and same-Layer ownership/cycle assessment follow ARC-004 §§12–13. Circular required dependencies are prohibited in the governed scope and actual conflicts remain visible. Documentary authority, allocation, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are distinct; no label change hides an indispensable requirement. The UPDATE map pins compared editions/scopes; this source claims no complete globally acyclic graph or deployed interface inventory.

---

# 9. Component Relationships

The following are scoped architectural contract declarations for documentary uses. They do not establish an operational service call, every-component routing requirement or complete dependency graph.

| Consumer | Provider | Required contract/use | Source/scope boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document described | DID-009 §5.1 declaration; descriptive values retain their own semantic owners |
| Classification | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document being classified | DID-009 §5.2; category/definition entity identity is a separate qualified contract |
| Templates | Document Identity | Identity of normalized Template documentation/document instances | DID-009 §5.3; Template definition/instance keys are not automatically DF document IDs |
| Registry | Document Identity | Logical document identity for a document catalog entry | DID-001 §9.4; source-edition provenance and exact lookup context required |
| Relationships | Document Identity | Identity of document endpoints | DID-001 §9.5; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Logical document node identity | ARC-005 §12; typed edges remain Relationships records, not document identities |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | ARC-005 §12; exact edition/descriptive/context evidence additionally required |
| Workflow | Document Identity | Identified normalized document subject | DID-009 §6.1; applicable transition execution remains with the actual process |

## 9.1. Metadata

Identity identifies the logical document; Metadata defines/represents descriptors and owner meanings. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles remain separate under one effective Profile. Identity data can be represented descriptively without transferring identity semantics or creating missing Metadata Element/catalog records.

**Unresolved reciprocal declarations:** supplied README states Document Identity→Metadata for descriptive concepts, while DID-009 §§5/10 states Metadata→Document Identity and no dependency on consuming components. Both source claims remain visible as required-dependency evidence pending owner/context/interface reconciliation. Distinguish core identity meaning from identity-record descriptor use, but do not silently downgrade a genuinely required contract into navigation or declare the apparent cycle resolved. Different stated uses alone do not prove operational independence or global acyclicity. Full Metadata/DID source cycles must establish the actual required scopes and cycle treatment under ARC-004.

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meanings and uses identity when categorizing a normalized document. Current Family/Type/Component labels are independent from stable allocation series and do not automatically reconstruct an assigned valid ID. Classification definitions and their own lifecycle/keys are different subjects from document editions; their actual identity contracts need qualification. Nominal CLS-003/CLS-001 collision reconciliation remains scheduled, not corrected by this source.

## 9.3. Templates

Templates owns reusable documentary structures and definition/instance contracts. A normalized document describing or applying a Template can require document identity; Template entities and graph/relationship identifiers are not thereby allocated normalized document IDs. Templates consumes appropriate owner meanings without redefining document identity, Metadata or Classification. Source presence and using a Template prove neither consistency nor approved publication.

## 9.4. Registry

Registry catalogs/looks up identified documentary entities or editions under declared provenance and freshness/current-historical-snapshot context. It does not redefine identity. A document lookup needs its domain/canonical key; an exact-edition lookup additionally needs edition/context evidence. No universal Registry intermediary, implemented resolver or persistent content availability is implied.

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns the contract for document endpoints. Other endpoint kinds use their own qualified identity domains. Canonical document reference validity requires the intended document/edition context and actual evidence; logical reference preservation does not imply live-content retrieval. Required edges remain required even when their data comes through a projection; a reference label cannot conceal a genuine cycle.

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph projects identified entities and Relationships records with source/edition provenance and refresh limits. Document nodes use document identity; graph edges or non-document entities need appropriate other contracts. Projections do not create competing identity/relationship authority or certify complete network correctness. No Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain is prescribed.

## 9.7. Governance

Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines define documentary transition, decision, review and snapshot requirements; actual operation remains with DMS/tool/manual processes and CMS change scope. Identity-record lifecycle, document Status/Version/Revision, maturity, review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct. A state list alone is neither a universal permission graph nor an implemented workflow.

Baselines selects an explicitly identified immutable set of exact approved document editions with relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Identity alone cannot select an exact member; eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion remain separate checks. Draft successors neither inherit membership nor retarget older snapshots. Retired identities preserve reservations/history without implying current document publication or resolver availability.

---

# 10. Architectural Constraints

Architectural definitions remain independent of unnecessary programming language, repository, storage or serialization prescriptions. Explicit logical domain, syntax, allocation, canonicalization, reference and integration requirements are architectural contracts, not implementations of generation/storage algorithms. Actual representations and adapters must preserve applicable meaning and supply examined-input/output and executor evidence; concept independence proves neither universal-format compatibility nor tool availability.

Keep one responsible identity semantic owner while permitting explicit cooperation and supporting projections. Preserve compatible meaning where feasible; necessary contract or representation/allocation changes require justified previous/new mapping, exact affected editions, dependencies, consumers and transition checks. Valid identity continuity, non-reuse and historical snapshot evidence remain obligations; an extension is not automatically harmless.

For working document editions, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to 0. Every changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes. Validation of unchanged source changes neither coordinate and is tracked centrally. Other entity-domain lifecycle/numbering requires its own qualified owner, not an implied copy of document edition rules.

---

# 12. Summary

Document Identity owns qualified logical document identity and its applicable allocation, preservation, reference and validation/governance contracts. Normalized document applicability, Domain+Identifier boundaries, stable series independent of classification and actual executor/evidence requirements prevent unqualified identity/service guarantees. Supporting state/reference records and exact editions remain separate subjects.

The ten local corrections are **Corrected—pending validation**. Full peer schema/lifecycle/assignment/reciprocal required-contract reconciliation and global identity/classification/collision, source maps, Metadata catalog/Profile, planning and implementation work remain pending. No approval, publication, Baseline selection, complete graph or deployed assignment/resolution is established.

A result applies only to exact examined bytes/editions and declared checks. Actual contribution, authorization, review, validation, ownership and approval remain separate. Later human/tool disk edits require assessment of their resulting bytes and do not inherit earlier outcomes or assign the previous contributor responsibility for consequences of a changed final product.

## 12.1. Compatibility assessment

Received identity guarantees/applicability, immutable representation and governance-independent meanings are unqualified; §10 excludes all implementation detail without separating logical representation/allocation requirements, while §12 claims guaranteed permanent identities. V2.0 replaces universal interpretations with explicit normalized/domain/edition/key-record distinctions, actual contract/executor and reference evidence, visible pending reciprocal requirements, and assessed necessary representation/allocation contract migration rather than an unconditional prohibition or arbitrary reassignment permission.

This is **incompatible normative contract reconciliation**. Version 1.0 increments major to 2.0/minor 0; declared Revision 0 increments monotonically to 1. Family correction alone is compatible; Type remains Architecture. Links, title/catalog/editorial corrections alone would also be compatible. Original twelve chapters and 19 numbered sections remain traceable; added §§12.1–12.3 record compatibility, history and propagation. The sole original unnamed allocation view retains provenance externally; no historic view ID is invented. DF-DID-001/path and all fifteen catalog IDs remain unchanged.
