# 3. Canonical Schema

The first view preserves the original Domain/Identifier/Identity References subjects while distinguishing key composition from an incoming association population. It is a logical contract view, not mandatory physical containment, a complete merged identity record or an execution/dependency graph.

<!-- original-section-view: 3 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §3 — Schema subjects.**

| Subject | Relation kind | Related subject | Scope/cardinality |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assigned Document Identity | governing domain qualification | Identity Domain | Exactly1 domain per assigned key |
| Assigned Document Identity | canonical representation | Identifier | Exactly1 canonical identifier under that domain's rules |
| Identity References | typed incoming document-targeting associations | Intended Document Identity or exact edition | Incoming population0..N; each valid reference identifies its intended qualified target/context |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

The first two rows describe the qualified key and its interpretation. The third is not an identifier segment or a required contained connection store. Original view text/digest is preserved in external UPDATE evidence under its original section; no historical diagram ID is invented. Selected peer requirements in §6 remain explicit.

---

# 4. Schema Elements

The three received labels and their Purpose/Cardinality/Characteristics headings are retained. Logical role and subject are distinguished from mandatory fields in a particular complete record. State/Canonical Reference differences remain declared in §6 rather than guessed away here.

---

## 4.1. Identity Domain



### 4.1.1. Purpose

Identity Domain establishes the declared qualification, owner and scope within which an assigned document key shall be unique. Defining a domain imposes a requirement; actual allocation/collision/reservation evidence establishes observations within a stated population and history scope. An unqualified string is not universally unique across other domains.

---

### 4.1.2. Cardinality

```text
Exactly one
```

One governing domain per applicable assigned identity. This is membership cardinality; a domain's population may be0..N unless a separately applicable domain-owner contract sets another minimum. Pre-allocation subjects do not yet have an assigned key. No external-domain registry or live allocation is created by this rule.

---

### 4.1.3. Characteristics

- **Mandatory:** governing domain qualification is required for the applicable assigned key.
- **Immutable:** ordinary changes preserve domain/key association under the governing contract; a necessary governed migration first requires §11 reconciliation.
- **Permanent:** domain/assignment history and non-reuse reservations remain traceable; this does not guarantee future content retrieval.

Namespace/non-overlap claims require explicit domain rules, owners, cross-domain qualification and checked allocation coverage, not presumed global separation.

---

## 4.2. Identifier



### 4.2.1. Purpose

Identifier is the canonical representation of assigned identity under its governing domain/canonicalization rules. The logical document, qualified key, rendered string and any permitted alias are distinct. Alternative representations must identify the intended existing key; they do not license another document to reuse it.

For this corpus, the domain is **Documentation Framework**, represented by **DF**. The adopted identifier convention is **DF-SSS-NNN**, where SSS is a registered uppercase three-letter stable allocation series and NNN is a positive three-digit allocation001–999. Full qualified identifiers, not numeric suffixes alone, determine collisions. The series records its allocation origin; current Family, Type, Component, path, Version/Revision and Status do not regenerate an assigned ID.

000 is not allocated and is not a README code. Gaps do not prove availability; allocated and retired numbers remain reserved. Allocation requires explicit series records and checks of relevant current/historical/reserved identities and references. At999, register an unused three-letter continuation series with traceability; do not widen syntax or recycle silently. Policy§4 and DID-001/003/004 establish these corpus rules. This schema integrates their scoped representation; other domains require explicit rules and no new allocation or migration occurs here.

Canonical interpretation states the responsible domain/rules and intended existing target. Alias/canonicalization handling must be explicit and preserve historical interpretation. Neither this format nor a syntax match proves allocation, uniqueness, a running resolver or retrieval availability.

---

### 4.2.2. Cardinality

```text
Exactly one
```

One canonical identifier representation per applicable assigned identity. Domain qualification remains required. Multiple aliases or physical representations do not create multiple logical document identities or erase the canonical interpretation requirement.

---

### 4.2.3. Characteristics

- **Mandatory:** a canonical identifier represents the applicable assigned identity.
- **Unique:** the qualified Domain+Identifier shall identify the intended document; actual collision/reservation coverage is recorded separately.
- **Immutable:** ordinary content/classification/status/edition/repository changes preserve the assigned key under its governing contract.
- **Permanent:** preserve same-document association and allocated/retired reservations; never reassign to another document.

Deterministic interpretation is a governed representation requirement, not proof of an implemented generator/resolver. Necessary contract/migration changes require the prior/new assessment in §11 rather than silent reallocation.

---

## 4.3. Identity References



### 4.3.1. Purpose

Identity References is the population of typed incoming associations targeting an intended qualified document identity or exact edition. They are logical associations, external to the identifier; they need not be physically stored within an identity record.

Document Identity owns document endpoint meaning; Relationships owns connection semantics/records and provenance. Registry owns registration/index records; graph projections do not create alternative identity authority. Other endpoint kinds use their own applicable identity contracts rather than automatically receiving normalized DF document IDs. Exact-edition targeting additionally identifies intended coordinates/bytes and context; logical identity alone is insufficient.

---

### 4.3.2. Cardinality

```text
Zero or more
```

An assigned identity can exist without any incoming reference. This preserves the received0..N and agrees with DID-003 §6 and DID-004 §§4.5/7.5. Incoming population cardinality differs from each reference's valid target: a valid document-targeting association must identify its intended qualified document/edition under its relation contract. This schema does not define every possible multi-endpoint relationship format.

---

### 4.3.3. Characteristics

- **Optional:** incoming reference population0..N; absence does not invalidate an assigned identity.
- **Extensible:** additional governed associations or endpoint types preserve existing meaning/ownership; a new reference does not redefine its target.
- **Implementation independent:** semantic target/owner/provenance rules do not prescribe a storage layout or require every consumer to route through Registry/Knowledge Graph.

Reference records can evolve under their owner rules without reallocating the target identity. Dangling, ambiguous, stale or unavailable targets are observations requiring evidence and correction, not permission to create or silently retarget an identity. Historical interpretation differs from current retrieval.

---

# 5. Cardinality

| Element | Cardinality | Actual subject and interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Identity Domain | 1 | One governing domain per applicable assigned key; domain population is a different subject |
| Identifier | 1 | One canonical representation under governing domain rules; aliases do not allocate another document |
| Identity References | 0..N | Optional incoming document-targeting association population; each valid association identifies its intended qualified target/context |

These three original rows are retained. The first two concern the assigned key; the last concerns external associations, not a mandatory identifier segment or schema-owned record collection. They do not settle complete-record State/Canonical Reference obligations in §6 or create cardinalities for every other endpoint kind.

---

# 7. Schema Principles

The four original principles are retained as bounded requirements. Their headings are not invented framework AP identifiers or proof of implemented outcomes.

---

## 7.1. Single Responsibility

Each schema role has one stated responsibility and subject. Domain/key meanings,reference association records,Metadata descriptions,registration and execution are separately owned. A logical view may reference related records without transferring their ownership or declaring every concept a mandatory stored field.

---

## 7.2. Stability

Preserve assigned same-document identity and compatible consumer meaning during ordinary evolution. Schema stability is a design objective with controlled contract evolution, not a claim that all future editions are compatible by definition.

Prefer compatible/additive extensions where they preserve the governing contract. A necessary incompatible change first identifies previous/new meaning,affected owners/consumers,dependencies,exact editions and transition/migration evidence under §11. It does not silently override still-applicable peer constraints. Working document Version/Revision successors follow Policy§5; entity allocation and lifecycle are distinct.

---

## 7.3. Canonical Representation

Applicable assigned identities conform to the declared governing domain/representation contract, not an unqualified universal format for all external domains. In this corpus, DF-SSS-NNN and Domain+Identifier rules in §4.2 apply independently of current classification.

Alternative implementations preserve intended target interpretation,qualified key/association meaning,cardinality and responsible provenance under explicit mappings. Syntax validity differs from actual allocation/uniqueness,record completeness,reference validity and exact-edition/Baseline selection. The partial view here does not silently replace DID-014's mandatory complete-record claims; §6 records pending reconciliation.

---

## 7.4. Technology Independence

The logical schema does not choose programming languages,databases,serialization formats,repositories or storage mechanisms. Implementations and adapters still need to satisfy applicable logical domain/representation/interface,record and evidence requirements. Technology independence is not evidence that every implementation already interoperates.

Assess actual artifacts/editions/context against applicable owner rules,with checks,observations,executor,coverage and unresolved conditions. DMS/tool/manual execution and CMS change evidence do not replace DF domain semantics,formal approval or actual Baseline inclusion.

---

# 8. Schema Constraints

The following requirements concern the stated assigned key and incoming-association subjects. Requirement text is not execution evidence. Record responsible contracts/editions,artifacts/domain/context,executor,coverage,observations and unresolved conditions for any claimed check.

---

## 8.1. Identity Domain

- A governing domain shall qualify every applicable assigned key; pre-allocation subjects and excluded functional files differ.
- Ordinary evolution preserves the assigned domain/key association under its governing contract.
- Domain qualification,owner,rules and namespace/collision/reservation coverage shall be explicit; a domain declaration does not prove actual uniqueness.
- A necessary migration affecting the governing contract requires §11 prior/new reconciliation and continuity checks before application; no silent domain reassignment is authorized.

---

## 8.2. Identifier

- Each applicable assigned identity has one canonical identifier representation under its domain rules.
- Full qualified key uniqueness requires actual allocation/collision/reservation evidence; matching syntax alone does not prove it.
- Assigned identifiers remain stable across ordinary classification,content,edition,location and document-status changes; current Family/Type does not reconstruct allocation series.
- Allocated and retired identifiers shall never be reassigned to another document. Preserve old representations,reservations and historical references/snapshot selections through any necessary governed transition.
- Apply §4.2 corpus syntax and canonicalization scope; no new series,identifier,alias or migration is created by this UPDATE.

---

## 8.3. Identity References

- A valid document-targeting reference identifies its intended existing qualified document or exact edition/context; other endpoint kinds follow their own contracts.
- Incoming population remains optional0..N; an identity does not need an incoming reference merely to exist.
- References never allocate or redefine their target and remain external to the identifier.
- Connection records retain their relationship owner and provenance; mutations do not automatically change the target key.
- Record dangling,ambiguous,stale or unavailable references as actual observations; preserve historical interpretation and never silently retarget. Identity stability alone guarantees no live-content retrieval or universal future reference validity.

---

# 9. Ownership

| Schema Element | Definition responsibility | Related record/execution boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Identity Domain | Document Identity and declared domain authority | Namespace/allocation rules and actual records/registrations need scoped evidence |
| Identifier | Document Identity under governing domain rules | Actual generator/adapter/resolver executes applicable contracts; no service supplied here |
| Identity References | Document Identity for document endpoint meaning | Relationships owns typed connections/provenance; Registry registration and other endpoint kinds retain their owners |

These three original rows remain. Other components shall not silently redefine document identity,but exclusive identity meaning does not transfer all Metadata values,registrations,connections or governance operations to Document Identity. Descriptors can represent identity/state under their semantic owners without fabricating a Metadata Element,Profile or merged schema catalog.

---

# 10. Relationship with Other Components

| Component / retained area label | Usage | Contract / evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Associates descriptors with identified documents | Domain meanings remain with identity/state owners;Schema/Profile/Instance/Dictionary roles need their own applicable contracts |
| Classification | Classifies identified documents | Mutable Family/Type/Component labels do not recalculate stable allocation series |
| Registry | Registers/indexes qualified identities or editions | Owns registration records;exact-edition context and freshness evidence needed;registration alone proves no allocation/approval |
| Relationships | Creates typed semantic connections between qualified endpoints | Owns connection semantics/records;Document Identity owns document endpoint meaning;other endpoints use applicable contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Projects identified entities and typed connections | Projection is not a new identity authority or universal routing intermediary |
| Governance (area label retained) | Workflow,Policies,Reviews and Baselines govern their stated subjects | Area,not a new component;identity alone selects no approved exact-edition Baseline member |

Six original interaction labels are preserved with qualified roles. Actual required dependencies use consumer→provider direction and state the contract,scope,provider/consumer/source editions and interfaces under ARC-004 §§12–13. Semantic association,documentary reference,projection,navigation and execution are distinct,not ways to hide a required cycle.

DID-009 §§5/10 declares Metadata→Document Identity/no consuming-component dependency,while the functional DID README Component Dependencies/Metadata declares identity consumption of Metadata descriptive concepts. These actual claims remain pending owner/core-versus-descriptor/interface reconciliation;different names alone prove neither independence nor acyclicity. No universal Registry/Graph service chain or complete graph proof is supplied.

---

# 12. Dependencies

The four original documentary dependencies remain:

- [DF-DID-001 — Document Identity Architecture](../01-Architecture/DF-DID-001-DocumentIdentityArchitecture.md): scoped domain/assignment,preservation and component boundaries.
- [DF-DID-002 — Document Identity Concepts](../01-Architecture/DF-DID-002%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Concepts.md): logical document,key,representation,reference and descriptor distinctions.
- [DF-DID-003 — Document Identity Model](../01-Architecture/DF-DID-003%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Model.md): qualified entities and selected cardinality0..N.
- [DF-DID-004 — Document Identity Elements](../01-Architecture/DF-DID-004%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Elements.md): elements,state/reference roles,constraints and ownership boundaries.

Consult [Lifecycle](../03-Behavior/DF-DID-006%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Lifecycle.md),[Relationships](DF-DID-009%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Relationships.md),[Constraints](DF-DID-010%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Constraints.md) and [Specification](../04-Reference/DF-DID-014%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Specification.md) for actual responsible peer requirements and unresolved integration. Those links are source-contract references,not a runtime call order or completed peer approval. The [functional DID README](../README.md) retains the actual Metadata dependency declaration for comparison,not a normalized ID allocation.

Required contract interpretation and allocations follow [Layers](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-004-ArchitecturalLayers.md) and [Components](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-005-ArchitecturalComponents.md);descriptive roles are compared with [Metadata Model](../../Metadata/01-Architecture/DF-MTD-003-MetadataModel.md),without claiming complete Metadata owner consistency. Working classification,identity,edition,authorship and evidence follow [Review Policy](../../../03-Governance/Reviews/03-Behavior/DF-RVW-001-ReviewPolicy.md);actual operations and limits are in [Review Report](../../../03-Governance/Reviews/04-Reference/DF-RVW-002-ReviewReport.md).

# 5. Relationships with Documentation Components

The three original Documentation subjects remain. Dependencies below are requirements for the specified document-targeting scope, not automatic requirements for every entity or execution route.

---

## 5.1. Metadata

Metadata describes documents and other applicable subjects through its own descriptor/model/schema/profile/instance contracts. Identity supplies the qualified document-key meaning, not every Metadata Element definition.

---

### 5.1.1. Dependency

Metadata→Document Identity remains the required declaration for identification of the applicable assigned normalized document described.

The functional DID README also states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Retain Document Identity→Metadata as an actual reciprocal required claim, not optional navigation. The exact README bytes/edition evidence and comparison source hashes are in the REVIEW/UPDATE map.

Responsible owners must reconcile which indispensable concepts/interfaces are required by identity core versus descriptive records, their exact governing editions and actual use. Different scope names alone do not dissolve a real required cycle. This UPDATE corrects the blanket denial of consumer dependencies; it does not certify that these reciprocal requirements are independent or globally reconciled.

---

### 5.1.2. Purpose

Associate descriptors with the existing qualified document or exact edition/context intended. Metadata owns descriptive records and can legitimately update them; Document Identity owns document identity meaning. Reading descriptors does not validate the entire Metadata schema/profile, allocate an absent Metadata Element or authorize an operation. Actual mandatory State/Canonical Reference and lifecycle authority conflicts remain pending owner reconciliation, not waived by a local relationship definition.

---

## 5.2. Classification

Classification owns category meaning, distinct from the key of a classified normalized document.

---

### 5.2.1. Dependency

Classification→Document Identity is the required document-identification contract for an applicable assigned normalized document receiving classification. It is not a requirement that each category/definition/assignment entity has a DF document key.

---

### 5.2.2. Purpose

Classification categorizes the intended document under its own contracts. Family/Type/Component changes do not regenerate the stable allocated series/key. A category entity's identity and a normalized document describing that category are different subjects. Classification does not redefine document-key meaning.

---

## 5.3. Templates

Templates owns template definition and usage contracts. Distinguish a template entity, an instance, a physical output and an applicable normalized Template document.

---

### 5.3.1. Dependency

Templates→Document Identity is the required identification contract for an applicable assigned normalized Template document. This does not allocate IDs automatically to every template instance, output file or functional document.

---

### 5.3.2. Purpose

An assigned normalized Template document follows the governing document-identity contract like other applicable normalized documents. Template entity/instance keys follow their own rules. Templates preserves existing document-key meaning and cannot fabricate allocation, approval or Baseline evidence through generated header fields.

---

# 10. Dependency Overview

The received overview mixed semantic provision, component collaboration and area order. Replace its untyped arrows with this typed view while preserving all nine original labels. It is not a mandatory serial pipeline.

<!-- original-section-view: 10 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §10 — Scoped dependency and collaboration overview.**

| Original subject | Kind / relation to Document Identity | Direction / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Semantic owner/provider and actual declared consumer | Provides document-key meaning; reciprocal Metadata requirement remains unresolved |
| Metadata | Descriptor owner / required consumer and provider claims | Metadata→Document Identity (§5.1.1); Document Identity→Metadata (functional README) |
| Classification | Category owner / required document-key consumer | Classification→Document Identity for applicable classified document (§5.2.1) |
| Registry | Registration owner / required document-key consumer | Registry→Document Identity for document registrations (§7.1) |
| Relationships | Connection owner / document endpoint consumption | Relationship semantics remain with Relationships; intended document endpoints use identity contracts (§7.2) |
| Knowledge Graph | Logical projection owner / required document-node consumer | Knowledge Graph→Document Identity; typed connections also require Relationships (§7.3) |
| Governance | Area: Workflow, Policies, Reviews, Baselines | Documentary state/rule/review/exact-snapshot contracts, not one component or an executor (§6) |
| Automation | Area: five registered components | Applicable checking/generation/verification contracts, not obligatory routing (§8) |
| Integration | Area: five registered components | Actual scoped exchange/adapter contracts, not an obligatory final stage (§9) |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Required dependency direction is consumer→provider. Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration form the architectural support order under ARC-004/005; they are not a universal serial chain. Same-Layer required contracts need explicit scope/interfaces and no required cycles. Semantic ownership, documentary reference, projection, data flow and operational execution are different relations.

Selected actual requirements also include Registry→Metadata (descriptors), Knowledge Graph→Relationships (typed connections), Workflow→Metadata (state/edition), Workflow→Policies (rules), Baselines→Document Identity (logical member) and Baselines→Metadata (exact edition/pinned context), under ARC-004§§12–13 and ARC-005§12/selected component clauses. These are selected declarations, not a complete graph or supplied implementation interfaces.

The former blanket claim “Document Identity has no dependency on the consuming components” is not accepted as the current general rule: the actual README declares the reciprocal Metadata requirement. Preserve both claims and exact source evidence; responsible owner/interface reconciliation is pending. Core-versus-descriptor naming, changing relation labels or omitting an indispensable edge does not prove acyclicity. No global DAG certification follows from this source-local correction. Received view text/digest remains external evidence at this original section.

---

# 13. Dependencies

The five original documentary dependencies remain, with intended identity/path references:

- [DF-DID-001 — Document Identity Architecture](../01-Architecture/DF-DID-001-DocumentIdentityArchitecture.md): domain, owner and actual consumer boundaries.

- [DF-DID-004 — Document Identity Elements](../01-Architecture/DF-DID-004%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Elements.md): semantic versus supporting-record responsibilities.
- [DF-ARC-005 — Architectural Components](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-005-ArchitecturalComponents.md): registered areas/components and selected actual required contracts.

Compare [Layers](../../../01-Architecture/DF-ARC-004-ArchitecturalLayers.md), [Schema](DF-DID-005%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Schema.md), [Lifecycle](../03-Behavior/DF-DID-006%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Lifecycle.md), [Validation](../03-Behavior/DF-DID-007%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Validation.md), [Governance](../03-Behavior/DF-DID-008%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Governance.md), [Constraints](DF-DID-010%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Constraints.md) and [Specification](../04-Reference/DF-DID-014%20-%20Document%20Identity%20Specification.md) for actual owner requirements and unresolved field/state/dependency authority. Documentary references do not by themselves establish an executable dependency graph, completed peer reconciliation or approval.

# 3. Architectural Overview

Document Identity is the Documentation component owning document-key/domain meaning and applicable allocation, preservation, lifecycle, validation and identity-governance contracts under common Architecture/Policy. Its supporting architectural role does not allocate it to the structural Foundation area or make every component a required consumer.

The component defines contracts; actual allocation, checking, retirement and document-management execution belong to the applicable DMS, tool or manual process, with CMS governing changes in its scope. Real operations need actual authority/decision, exact rules/source editions, subject/domain/artifacts/context, executor, observations and coverage. Naming an owner or generating a string/header is not an allocation, installed engine or permission.

Assigned K shall remain associated with the same logical document under its governing contract; actual uniqueness and preservation claims need assignment, canonicalization, population/collision/reservation/history evidence. R and other supporting records may evolve under responsible rules without reallocating K. A specification requirement is not proof that every actual document or implementation is already conformant.

---

# 6. Conceptual Model

The received conceptual view's five labels remain, with typed key/record/assertion/descriptor roles rather than untyped composition or runtime dependencies. Exact original text/digest is external evidence at this original section; no historical view identifier is invented.

<!-- original-section-view: 6 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §6 — Assigned subject and supporting identity-record roles.**

| Original label | Working subject / typed relation | Scope and authority |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Logical assigned subject K represented by R | Not a recursively embedded key or new document allocated for the record |
| Identifier | Canonical representation/interpretation of K under its governing domain | One qualified assigned-key meaning; legitimate aliases retain responsible mappings |
| Identity Domain | Governing qualification/allocation/preservation contract for K | Domain+Identifier interprets K; domain label alone proves no actual uniqueness |
| Identity State | Mandatory R lifecycle assertion about the assigned subject in §7 | Mutable supporting assertion with actual event/decision/provenance, not a key coordinate or document Status |
| Canonical Reference | Mandatory R canonical-target descriptor in §7 | Intended qualified document/exact-edition/context; not an incoming Relationships connection or guaranteed URL |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Received Document Identity→Identifier/Domain/State arrows are qualified logical roles, not mandatory storage pointers, ownership transfer or required service edges. Received Identifier→Canonical Reference depicts canonical rendering/target interpretation, not a rule that a reference is part of the immutable identifier string or that every target needs an incoming edge. The exact original arrow text remains in maps; mandatory R scope is explicit in §7, not silently removed by drawing a different view.

---

# 7. Canonical Elements

The five received rows remain mandatory for a **complete supporting assigned identity record R** claimed under this V2.0 R1 working specification. This is an explicit correction of the received unqualified every-identity composition: it separates the logical assigned key K from supporting record/assertion/descriptor roles. It does not make State or Canonical Reference optional to pass a complete-R claim, nor add them as immutable coordinates of K.

| Element | Qualified description / subject | Mandatory for complete assigned R |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Intended assigned logical document K and same-document association represented by this record; not a second allocated identity or required recursive object field | Yes |
| Identifier | Canonical identifier interpretation/representation qualifying the intended K under responsible rules | Yes |
| Identity Domain | Governing semantic/allocation/preservation scope qualifying K | Yes |
| Identity State | Supporting actual lifecycle assertion for the assigned subject, mapped to Lifecycle State in §8 with responsible event/decision/source evidence | Yes |
| Canonical Reference | Supporting descriptor identifying the intended canonical qualified document target, or declared exact edition with required coordinates/bytes/context; it may reuse governed key rendering without an additional runtime locator | Yes |

**State role.** Identity State and Lifecycle State are controlled names for the same R assertion role here, not universal aliases for Metadata State or document Status. In assigned-R scope, Assigned, Preserved or Retired is interpreted under actual DID-006 subject/event/decision rules and its selected eight-transition contract. Unassigned denotes pre-allocation and is not an assigned R with a nonexistent K. No global permission graph or undocumented edge is granted. Supporting assertion records can change while K remains stable.

**Canonical-target role.** Canonical Reference states the intended target/interpretation and applicable source/context evidence; it is not a promised permanently available URL or a new independent identity allocation. It can concern K as a logical document, or an explicitly selected edition with additional context. A complete R needs this descriptor role, but it does not require an incoming Relationships record: external incoming document-reference population remains0..N under DID-003/005. Descriptor presence, connection validity and observed retrieval are separate checks; a historical intended target can remain interpretable while live content is unavailable. Never silently create/retarget K or immutable snapshot members.

A consumer checking only K can report that narrower coverage; it cannot call a missing-State/Canonical-Reference record a fully conformant R or infer full implementation conformance. Conversely, a pre-allocation or non-document subject is not an invalid assigned R merely because it is outside that declared claim. Full conformance needs explicit applicable subject/rule inventory (§§15/18), actual checks and unresolved-authority limits.

No implementation claiming complete R may remove an applicable mandatory role. These are logical record responsibilities, not a newly registered Metadata Element/Profile, prescribed serialization, actual populated record or approved merged implementation schema. The current working contract uses existing DID-006 assertion and DID-009/013 document-target meanings; it does not manufacture missing canonical catalogs or imply peer rollout.

**Prior/new authority and affected sources.** V1.0 R0 §§6–8 declared universal composition/mandatory State/Canonical Reference without these subjects. V2.0 R1 retains all five Yes requirements but qualifies complete assigned-R scope, Identity State↔Lifecycle State and canonical descriptor versus incoming association. DID-003/004/005/006/013 and affected consumers require comparison/propagation at their exact recorded editions. DID-005§6's selected key/association view is not silently overwritten or a waiver of R obligations. Their prior references and unresolved-field notes remain historical/current source evidence until a separately traced update qualifies them. This local decision is explicit; full owner-source agreement, canonical field registration and implementation transition are not certified.

---

# 8. Canonical Schema

The second received view retains its five labels and logical organization, with explicit subjects. It does not prescribe a runtime object layout, serialization or complete Metadata schema.

<!-- original-section-view: 8 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §8 — Assigned identity-record roles versus stable key.**

| Original schema label | Typed interpretation | Working relationship / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Assigned logical subject K represented by supporting R | The record is about the same document, not another allocation |
| Identifier | Canonical representation role qualifying K | Interpreted with Identity Domain; not all mutable record contents |
| Identity Domain | Governing domain role qualifying K | Responsible domain/canonicalization/allocation/reservation evidence required |
| Lifecycle State | Mandatory R supporting lifecycle assertion | Controlled §7 name for Identity State in this record scope; not document Status or nonexistent assigned key in Unassigned |
| Canonical Reference | Mandatory R canonical-target descriptor | Qualified target/edition/context responsibility, not optional incoming0..N association, immutable key field or live resolver guarantee |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

K has governing Domain+Identifier meaning; R has the five mandatory roles of §7. The received tree's parent/child lines express this qualified logical organization, not universal physical field containment, event order or required consumer edges. Complete-R mandatory roles remain; the selected DID-005 key/association schema and detailed record/field owners keep their scoped responsibilities. Actual additional representation/profile rules, field definitions/values, authority and consumer compatibility require their own evidence. No accepted complete framework-wide schema or populated record is inferred from this view.

---

# 9. Lifecycle Specification

The received four-label overview is retained as a subject/assertion view, not an exhaustive transition graph or operational permission pipeline.

<!-- original-section-view: 9 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §9 — Lifecycle subjects and actual assertion evidence.**

| Original label | Subject / meaning | Evidence / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Unassigned | Applicable documentary pre-allocation subject | No assigned K or complete assigned R is presumed; allocation needs an actual responsible decision |
| Assigned | Evidenced qualified K association with intended logical document | Actual allocation/association rules, collision/reservation/history and resulting assertion |
| Preserved | Evidenced continuing same-document association through qualifying evolution | Supporting records may change; actual event/context and selected transitions govern |
| Retired | Evidenced end of active use in its declared scope | Same-document history and reserved K retained; no reuse or perpetual content availability |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Compare the eight selected current DID-006§7 rows, including the five Preserved self-loops omitted from the received overview:

| Current State | Event | Next State | Actual applicability / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unassigned | Identity Assignment | Assigned | Pre-allocation subject; responsible allocation/association decision and actual collision/reservation/history checks |
| Assigned | Document Evolution | Preserved | Actual qualifying evolution with continuing same-document assignment evidence |
| Preserved | Content Revision | Preserved | Qualifying content evolution; exact edition/context and preserved K |
| Preserved | Metadata Update | Preserved | Metadata Evolution alias in its actual subject/context; descriptor owner retained |
| Preserved | Classification Update | Preserved | Classification Evolution alias; changed categories do not reconstruct allocated key |
| Preserved | Repository Migration | Preserved | Actual movement/context and preserved K; references/index freshness separately assessed |
| Preserved | Governance Transition | Preserved | Governance Evolution alias; actual process/state evidence, not automatic snapshot/key change |
| Preserved | Identity Retirement | Retired | Actual responsible retirement scope/decision, same-document history/reservation retained |

These selected rows are not proof of real permission or successful execution. No unlisted edge is granted by implication; a real case not covered, including direct Assigned retirement without qualifying prior evolution, needs an explicit responsible owner decision/change with impact/evidence assessment rather than event relabelling. Retired has no outgoing edge in this selected scope; that does not define every external contract. Maintaining an unchanged assertion without an event is not automatically a new self-loop.

Document-edition Draft/Review/Approved/Published/Archived/Obsolete/Deleted statuses and identity assertions are different subjects. Status, file/edition/index deletion, archiving or unavailable content does not by itself allocate or retire K, grant a missing edge or select a Baseline. Actual State/Canonical Reference record semantics are §7's local working decision with remaining owner/consumer propagation, not a claim of complete implementation/lifecycle authority across all sources. Preserve immutable historical exact editions and selected relationship context; Draft successors inherit no approval/membership.

---

# 10. Validation Requirements

The six received validation subjects remain. For any claim, identify K/R/operation/domain scope, exact artifacts/editions/bytes/context, actual applicable mandatory rules/source editions/interfaces, executor/method, performed/unperformed checks, observations, population/coverage and limits. Requirements are not evidence that checks ran.

| Validation subject | Qualified requirement / evidence |
|---|---|
| structural validity | Applicable K representation or complete R roles, actual governing rules and subject; no universal record format assumed |
| uniqueness | Full qualified assignments/canonicalization/population/collision/reservation/history coverage, not syntax or partial index alone |
| completeness | Every applicable mandatory role for the declared R/other claim; selected K-only success does not waive State/Canonical Reference |
| integrity | Actual responsible association/provenance/authenticity rules and observations; no invented security mechanism or automatic guarantee |
| consistency | Exact subject/source/context meanings and records; legitimate edition/history differences distinguished from actual conflicts |
| reference validity | Actual typed intended qualified document/exact-edition/context, canonical descriptor and connection/resolution observations; no perpetual live guarantee |

DID-007 distinguishes Valid, Invalid, Inconsistent and Unresolvable observations. An actual violation requires applicable rule/context and observed nonconformance. Missing/unperformed/conflicting mandatory evidence withholds broader success without fabricating Invalid/Unresolvable. Preserve all supported negative observations and coverage limits rather than suppressing them through a silent precedence rule. A successful subset is narrower evidence, not full R, component or framework Valid.

Actual §7 working requirements do not complete every peer field/profile/interface decision or implementation rollout. Where applicable responsible authority remains conflicting, retain it and withhold the broader claim until reconciliation; do not silently waive mandatory roles or invent accepted field instances. Evaluation, writing a result record and separately authorized remediation are distinct. A result grants no mutation/allocation/approval/publication/Baseline selection; changed artifacts/rules/context need their own assessment.

---

# 11. Governance Requirements

All six original governance subjects remain under common governing architecture and actual domain contracts.

| Governance subject | Qualified obligation / authority boundary |
|---|---|
| permanence | Preserve assigned same-document association, reservations/history and intended recognition; not perpetual retrieval |
| uniqueness | Actual governing qualification, allocation/canonical interpretation, collision/reservation/history evidence |
| immutability | Stable K through ordinary evolution versus mutable supporting records; necessary governing change follows §14 |
| traceability | Actual assignment/decision/change/reference/edition provenance, observations, coverage and limits |
| canonical ownership | Document-key meaning with Document Identity; other descriptor/category/connection/registration/projection owners remain |
| architectural consistency | Applicable exact common/owner contracts and scoped observed checks, with unresolved authority/interfaces visible |

Governance is Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines documentary contracts, not one operational owner/engine. Actual DMS/tool/manual execution and CMS change scope require real authority/rules, exact subject/edition/context, decision/executor and observations. Authorship, custody, a normative statement or local PASS alone grants no operational permission.

Ordinary governance operations do not silently redefine identity meaning. Necessary assessed normative revision under common AP-015–018 is distinct from arbitrary override; §14 specifies prior/new authority, owner/consumer/interface, compatibility/version and continuity evidence. Baselines requires exact eligible approved-edition selection and relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Logical identity, R completeness, review or validation alone neither approves/publishes a Draft successor nor selects its membership or retargets historical snapshots.

---

# 12. Relationship Specification

All nine received subjects remain with actual semantic/record and area/component roles. Required dependencies mean consumer→provider with explicit contract/scope, source editions and interfaces; documentary authority reference, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are different relations.

| Original subject | Kind | Qualified relationship / owner boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Component | Descriptor/model/schema/profile/instance owner; Metadata→Document Identity for identity of the applicable normalized document described; reciprocal requirement below remains |
| Classification | Component | Category/assignment owner; applicable classified-document key consumption does not allocate DF IDs to every category/entity |
| Templates | Component | Template definition/instance contracts; applicable normalized Template-document key consumption differs from every template entity/output |
| Registry | Component | Registration/index owner; intended qualified key/edition/context and source/freshness evidence; registration is not allocation or a mandatory intermediary |
| Relationships | Component | Typed connection/endpoint/provenance owner; document endpoints consume identity meanings, other endpoint kinds retain theirs |
| Knowledge Graph | Component | Logical node/edge projection/properties with authoritative identity/connection source/context and refresh limits; no competing authority or complete graph proof |
| Governance | Area | Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines documentary contracts; actual management/decision executor and CMS scope separate |
| Automation | Area | Validation, Metadata Generator, Registry Generator, Documentation Generator and Consistency Verification capabilities; actual input/output/rule/observation/executor evidence |
| Integration | Area | Source Control Integration, CI/CD Integration, IDE Integration, Documentation Platform Integration and AI Integration optional adapters; actual authorization/mappings/contributors/checks required |

The functional DID README states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Current DID-009§5.1.1/§10 retains Document Identity→Metadata alongside Metadata→Document Identity. Preserve both actual required declarations pending responsible core-versus-descriptor/interface/source-edition reconciliation. Different scope names, projection or navigation relabelling do not dissolve a genuine required cycle.

The received all-relationships-unidirectional-towards-Identity claim is replaced, not accepted as the current general rule. Ownership/authority and typed association are not required edges; actual indispensable providers remain required even through projections. Apply ARC-004/005 support order and same-Layer explicit-interface/cycle rules; these do not require every earlier provider or a serial pipeline. No complete globally acyclic graph or integrated consumer compatibility is certified. Repeated descriptors, aliases, copies/editions and projection records are not alone duplicate allocations or semantic ownership transfer.

---

# 13. Constraint Specification

The eight original constraint subjects remain with explicit K/R/operation applicability and actual responsible rules.

| Constraint subject | Qualified requirement |
|---|---|
| exactly one identity per document | One governing assigned identity for the applicable normalized logical document/domain contract; functional/pre-allocation/other entity scope differs |
| exactly one canonical identifier | One responsible canonical interpretation for assigned K under its domain, with legitimate traceable aliases distinguished |
| immutable identity | Assigned K/same-document association stable through ordinary evolution; supporting records can change; necessary governing revision follows §14 |
| permanent identity | Preserve historical same-document association/reservations; no perpetual content-retrieval guarantee |
| unique identity | Actual qualified assignments/canonicalization and collision/reservation/population/history coverage, not syntax/index-only success |
| non-reusable identity | No allocated/retired K assigned to another logical document; gaps or unavailable content do not establish availability |
| technology independence | Logical semantic separation with legitimate representation/interface/integration and evidence obligations |
| repository independence | Location/custody/index changes do not reconstruct K; actual target/freshness/consumer/history effects assessed |

DID-010 owns the detailed applicable constraint subjects; this consolidation does not silently rewrite all peers or turn a missing record into an observed violation. Establish actual mandatory rule/subject/context and observed nonconformance before claiming failure. Full success needs all applicable mandatory requirements/authority/evidence for its declared scope; narrower observations retain their limits. No automatic repair, allocation or permission is supplied.

---

# 14. Extensibility Specification

**Current V2.0 R1 decision.** Ordinary compatible implementation extensions preserve applicable owner meanings, mandatory requirements and assigned same-document continuity. Necessary normative/foundational/responsibility/interface revision is permitted only through actual assessed common Architecture AP-015–018 and responsible change authority; it is not falsely labelled compatible merely because it is called an extension.

All five received extension subjects remain:

| Original condition | Current qualified application |
|---|---|
| preserve backward compatibility | Preserve compatible meaning where feasible for ordinary extension; necessary incompatibility requires explicit actual prior/new authority/rationale/consumer and transition evidence |
| preserve canonical identity semantics | Ordinary implementations do not silently replace owner meaning; necessary normative revision is separately assessed, not an arbitrary key reassignment |
| preserve interoperability | Evaluate actual provider/consumer/adapter/source editions and transition checks; no completed global rollout inferred |
| preserve mandatory constraints | Ordinary additions do not waive applicable requirements; necessary normative changes explicitly identify old/new mandates, authority, compatibility and affected exact sources before propagation |
| remain additive | Prefer additive compatible change when it meets the actual need; not an absolute prohibition on necessary justified normative revision |

**Received restriction and affected sources.** V1.0 R0 required every extension to be additive/backward-compatible and stated “Core identity semantics are not extensible.” That exact prior claim remains in original/map/diff/history evidence. This V2.0 R1 replaces this specification's absolute extension-only prohibition with the scoped ordinary-extension/necessary-revision contract above under common architecture. It does not leave the old absolute clause simultaneously governing the same current operation, silently rewrite the past or grant arbitrary mutation of an assigned K.

DID-005§11, DID-010§12, DID-011§§4.2/9 and DID-013§9 currently cite that received restrictive claim or its unresolved authority. Their exact current bytes/editions/hashes are in the affected-source map. They are not edited or automatically revalidated here; their prior-source references and pending notes must be qualified through a separately traced propagation step before claiming integrated agreement. Other K/R field/interface and consumer decisions likewise need actual reconciliation. The current local decision and remaining propagation are separate facts.

For any necessary term/mandate/owner/normative/domain/path/representation transition:

1. Preserve original exact artifacts, rules/editions, actual observations and failed checks. Identify prior/new meaning or mandate, actual responsible authority, intended subject/domain/context, need, alternatives and rationale.
2. Assess exact semantic/record owners, consumers and indispensable consumer→provider interfaces, mandatory field/state/reference/lifecycle effects and actual reciprocal/cycle claims. Resolve governing authority for the actual operation before asserting broader conformity; do not rename away a real required edge.
3. Record compatibility and exact old→new role/term/key/alias mappings, domain qualification, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and intended reference/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot effects. Never reassign allocated/retired K to another document or silently retarget immutable historical members.
4. Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contributor/event provenance, coordinated transition evidence and working edition/history. Compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract/convention change increments major and resets minor to0. Every persisted changed document edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions; other entity allocation/lifecycle contracts remain separate.
5. Validate resulting exact artifacts/editions in the subsequent appropriate operation, recording actual checks/executor/observations/coverage/remaining peer work. Unchanged-source validation increments neither source coordinate; later changed bytes need their own assessment. Preserve earlier pending/failed events rather than rewriting them as historical success.

This UPDATE changes documentary requirements only. It executes no identity/domain migration, owner transfer, allocation, retirement, implementation rollout, formal approval, publication or Baseline selection.

---

# 15. Compliance Requirements

Conformance is a declared actual claim, not a property inferred from specification presence or a list of citations. Identify implementation/record/population scope, K/R/operation subjects/domain, exact artifacts/editions/bytes/context, applicable responsible mandatory clauses/source editions/interfaces, authority/executor, performed/unperformed checks, observations, coverage and limits before deciding the result.

The ten original owner-source subjects remain, with applicability governed by their exact responsible clauses (§17). Their requirements are not all interchangeable universal rules for every entity/context. A complete supporting-R claim retains all five §7 roles; K-only or pre-allocation observations do not imply full R/implementation conformity. Implementation conformance here includes every applicable current specification requirement and actual applicable independent owner requirements, not just a convenient subset.

# Document Identity Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

---

> The architectural component responsible for defining, assigning, preserving and governing the permanent identity of documents within the Documentation Framework.

---

# Overview

The **Document Identity** component defines the canonical identity model of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the concepts, structures, lifecycle, governance and specifications required to uniquely identify documents throughout their entire lifetime, independently of their content, storage location or implementation technology.

Document Identity provides the persistent identification foundation upon which document traceability, governance and discovery are built.

---

# Purpose

The Document Identity component is responsible for defining:

- the Document Identity architecture;
- Document Identity concepts;
- Document Identity models;
- Document Identity elements;
- Document Identity schemas;
- Document Identity lifecycle;
- Document Identity validation;
- Document Identity governance;
- Document Identity extensibility.

The component does **not** define:

- document metadata;
- document content;
- document classification;
- repositories;
- workflows;
- implementation technologies.

---

# Responsibilities

The Document Identity component is responsible for:

- defining canonical Document Identity concepts;
- defining Document Identity Elements;
- defining Document Identity Schemas;
- defining Identity Relationships;
- defining Identity Constraints;
- defining the Identity Lifecycle;
- defining Identity Validation;
- defining Identity Governance;
- defining Identity Extensibility;
- maintaining the Document Identity Dictionary;
- publishing the Document Identity Specification.

---

# Component Scope

The Document Identity component defines **what a document identity is** and **how it is architecturally described** within the Documentation Framework.

It does not define:

- document metadata;
- document lifecycle management;
- repository organization;
- document storage;
- document implementation;
- document classification.

Those responsibilities belong to other Documentation Framework components.

---

# Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework architecture, Document Identity is a **Documentation Component**.

Conceptually.

```text

                    Documentation Framework
....................│
                    ├── Foundation
                    ├── Architecture
                    ├── Documentation
                    │   ├── Metadata
                    │   ├── Document Identity
                    │   ├── Classification
                    │   └── Templates
                    │
                    ├── Governance
                    ├── Discovery
                    ├── Automation
                    ├── Integration
                    ├── Resources
                    ├── Guides
                    └── Reference

```

Document Identity provides the permanent identification model used throughout the Documentation Framework while remaining independent of document content and implementation.

---

# Document Organization

The Document Identity component documentation is organized into four architectural areas.

```text

                    DocumentIdentity/

The Metadata component is founded upon a collection of architectural concepts that define the semantics of document description within the Documentation Framework.

These concepts establish the canonical vocabulary required to model, describe and evolve Metadata consistently across the framework.

This document defines those concepts independently of any implementation technology, serialization format or storage mechanism.

---

# 4. Conceptual Principles

The Metadata conceptual model follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Explicit Semantics

Every Metadata concept shall possess one clearly defined meaning.

---

## 4.2. Single Source of Truth

Each concept shall have one authoritative definition.

---

## 4.3. Technology Independence

Concepts shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

# 5. Core Concepts

## 5.1. Metadata

### 5.1.1. Definition

Metadata is structured descriptive information that characterizes a document independently of its content.

Metadata provides architectural information about a document rather than the knowledge contained within it.

### 5.1.2. Purpose

To make every document self-describing.

---

## 5.2. Metadata Element

### 5.2.1. Definition

A Metadata Element is an individual architectural unit of Metadata representing one specific descriptive characteristic of a document.

Each Metadata Element has a single architectural meaning.

### 5.2.2. Examples

- Document ID
- Title
- Version
- Language

The complete definition of Metadata Elements is provided by the Metadata Elements specification.

---

## 5.3. Metadata Value

### 5.3.1. Definition

A Metadata Value is the information assigned to a Metadata Element for a specific document.

The same Metadata Element may possess different values in different documents while preserving its semantic meaning.

---

## 5.4. Metadata Model

### 5.4.1. Definition

The Metadata Model defines the conceptual organization of Metadata and the relationships between Metadata concepts.

It establishes the abstract structure used by the Documentation Framework.

The Metadata Model is independent of any concrete representation.

---

## 5.5. Metadata Schema

### 5.5.1. Definition

A Metadata Schema specifies the formal structure used to organize Metadata Elements.

It defines which Metadata Elements may exist and how they are organized.

The Metadata Schema does not define implementation formats.

---

## 5.6. Metadata Profile

### 5.6.1. Definition

A Metadata Profile is a constrained view of a Metadata Schema intended for a specific category of documents.

A profile selects the Metadata Elements required by a particular document type without modifying the underlying Metadata Schema.

---

## 5.7. Metadata Dictionary

### 5.7.1. Definition

The Metadata Dictionary is the authoritative catalog of every Metadata Element defined by the Documentation Framework.

It provides the canonical definition of each Metadata Element together with its semantic meaning.

---

## 5.8. Metadata Specification

### 5.8.1. Definition

The Metadata Specification formally defines the Metadata architecture, model, elements, constraints and behavior.

It constitutes the normative reference for Metadata within the Documentation Framework.

The Metadata Model defines the conceptual structure of Metadata within the Documentation Framework.

It specifies how Metadata is organized as an architectural model, the relationships between its constituent concepts and the rules governing their interaction.

The Metadata Model provides the abstract foundation upon which Metadata Schemas, Metadata Profiles and Metadata Specifications are built.

---

# 5. Architectural Position

The Metadata Model belongs to the Metadata architectural component.

Conceptually.

```text

            Metadata Component

               Architecture
                    │
                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

                    │

                    │

                    │
                    ▼

```

The Metadata Model bridges conceptual definitions and formal specifications.

# 6. Metadata Abstraction Levels

The Metadata component is organized into successive abstraction levels.

```text

                 Level 1
            Metadata Concepts
                    ↓

                 Level 2
              Metadata Model
                    ↓

                 Level 3
             Metadata Schema
                    ↓

                 Level 4
            Metadata Profiles
                    ↓

                 Level 5
            Metadata Instances

```

Each level refines the previous one without altering its semantics.

---

# 7. Conceptual Entities

The Metadata Model is composed of the following conceptual entities.

## 7.1 Metadata

Represents the complete descriptive information associated with a document.

Metadata is composed of Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.2 Metadata Element

Represents one descriptive property of Metadata.

Each Metadata Element has one semantic meaning.

Metadata Elements are defined independently.

---

## 7.3 Metadata Value

Represents the value assigned to a Metadata Element for a specific document.

Values instantiate Metadata Elements.

---

## 7.4 Metadata Schema

Represents the formal organization of Metadata Elements.

The Schema determines which Metadata Elements may appear within a Metadata instance.

---

## 7.5 Metadata Profile

Represents a specialization of a Metadata Schema for a particular category of documents.

Profiles constrain, but do not redefine, the underlying Metadata Schema.

---

## 7.6 Metadata Instance

Represents the complete Metadata associated with one individual document.

Each Metadata Instance conforms to exactly one Metadata Profile.

# 8. Conceptual Relationships

| Source | Relationship | Target |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| Metadata | is composed of | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Element | possesses | Metadata Value |
| Metadata Schema | defines | Metadata Elements |
| Metadata Profile | specializes | Metadata Schema |
| Metadata Instance | conforms to | Metadata Profile |
| Metadata Instance | contains | Metadata Values |

                    Metadata

                    ├── Metadata Element

                    │
                    ├── Metadata Element

                    │

                    │   │
                    │   └── Metadata Value
                    │
                    └── ...

```

The order of Metadata Elements is not architecturally significant unless explicitly specified by a Metadata Profile.

---

# 10. Metadata Specialization

Metadata evolves through specialization.

The Metadata Schema defines the complete vocabulary.

Metadata Profiles define subsets of that vocabulary.

Metadata Instances implement one Metadata Profile.

                    ▼

# 1. Introduction

The Metadata Dictionary is the authoritative catalog of all Metadata Elements defined by the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the canonical definitions, meanings and architectural characteristics of every Metadata Element.

The Metadata Dictionary serves as the single source of truth for Metadata semantics and ensures that every Metadata Element is interpreted consistently throughout the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Dictionary Principles

The Metadata Dictionary follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Canonical Definition

Every Metadata Element shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Stability

Metadata definitions shall remain stable throughout their lifecycle.

---

## 4.3. Uniqueness

Each Metadata Element shall appear exactly once in the Metadata Dictionary.

---

## 4.4. Technology Independence

Metadata definitions shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.5. Traceability

Changes to Metadata definitions shall remain historically traceable.

---

---

## 4.4. Technology Independence

---

---

# 5. Purpose of a Dictionary Entry

Each Dictionary Entry defines one Metadata Element.

A Dictionary Entry provides the complete architectural description of that Metadata Element independently of any implementation.

---

# 6. Dictionary Organization

The Metadata Dictionary is organized as a collection of Dictionary Entries.

Conceptually.

```text

                    Metadata Dictionary
                    │
                    ├── Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    ├── Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    ├── Dictionary Entry
                    │
                    └── ...

```

Each Dictionary Entry describes one Metadata Element.

---

# 7. Dictionary Entry Structure

Every Dictionary Entry should contain the following architectural information.

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Identifier | Unique Metadata Element identifier |
| Name | Canonical Metadata Element name |
| Category | Metadata Group or conceptual category |
| Definition | Canonical architectural definition |
| Purpose | Why the Metadata Element exists |
| Semantics | Architectural meaning |
| Value Type | Abstract value classification |
| Cardinality | Permitted occurrence |
| Required | Whether required by the canonical Metadata architecture |
| Default Value | Default value, if applicable |
| Lifecycle Status | Current lifecycle state |
| Version | Current architectural version |
| Revision | Current revision |
| Related Elements | Architecturally related Metadata Elements |
| Constraints | Applicable Metadata Constraints |
| Notes | Additional architectural observations |

The precise representation of Dictionary Entries is implementation independent.

---

# 8. Dictionary Classification

Metadata Elements may be classified according to their architectural purpose.

Typical classifications include:

- Identity Metadata
- Descriptive Metadata
- Structural Metadata
- Lifecycle Metadata
- Governance Metadata
- Traceability Metadata
- Discovery Metadata
- Automation Metadata

These classifications improve organization without affecting semantics.

---

# 12. Dictionary Relationships

The Metadata Dictionary interacts with several Metadata specifications.

| Document | Relationship |
|----------|--------------|
| Metadata Concepts | Defines the conceptual foundation of Metadata Elements. |
| Metadata Model | Defines how Metadata Elements relate. |
| Metadata Elements | Defines the architectural characteristics of Metadata Elements. |
| Metadata Schema | Organizes Metadata Elements structurally. |
| Metadata Profiles | Select Metadata Elements for specific document categories. |
| Metadata Lifecycle | Governs Metadata Element evolution. |
| Metadata Validation | Uses Dictionary definitions during validation. |
| Metadata Governance | Approves Dictionary evolution. |

The Dictionary references Metadata Elements but does not redefine their architecture.

---

# 13. Dictionary Entry Example

The following example illustrates the architectural structure of a Dictionary Entry.

| Attribute | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| Identifier | MTD-001 |
| Name | Document Identifier |
| Category | Identity Metadata |
| Definition | Unique identifier assigned to a document. |
| Purpose | Enables unambiguous document identification. |
| Value Type | Identifier |
| Cardinality | Exactly One |
| Required | Yes |
| Lifecycle Status | Published |
| Version | 1.0 |

The example is illustrative only.

It does not define canonical Metadata Elements.

---

# 14. Architectural Characteristics

The Metadata Dictionary possesses the following characteristics.

## 14.1. Authoritative

Provides the canonical definition of every Metadata Element.

---

## 14.2. Consistent

Maintains one semantic definition for each Metadata Element.

---

Independent of implementation technologies.

## 14.4. Traceable

Preserves historical evolution.

---

## 14.5. Stable

Definitions evolve through controlled governance.

---

## 14.6. Reusable

Supports all Metadata Profiles and Metadata Schemas.

Metadata is not a static architectural artifact.

Like every architectural asset within the Documentation Framework, Metadata evolves throughout its existence while preserving semantic consistency and architectural stability.

This document defines the lifecycle of Metadata from its introduction through its retirement.

The Metadata Lifecycle governs the evolution of Metadata independently of implementation technologies, repositories and storage mechanisms.

---

# 4. Lifecycle Principles

The Metadata Lifecycle follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through controlled architectural processes.

---

## 4.2. Semantic Stability

The semantic meaning of Metadata shall remain stable throughout its lifecycle.

---

## 4.3. Traceability

All lifecycle transitions shall be traceable.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

Metadata evolution shall preserve compatibility whenever reasonably possible.

Every Metadata artifact shall possess an explicit lifecycle status.

---

## 4.4. Backward Compatibility

---

## 4.5. Explicit Status

---

# 5. Lifecycle Overview

The Metadata Lifecycle is composed of six architectural states.

```text

                 Proposed
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                 Approved
                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Each state represents a well-defined architectural maturity level.

---

# 6. Lifecycle States

## 6.1. Proposed

A Metadata artifact has been identified as necessary but has not yet been formally defined.

Characteristics:

- architectural proposal;
- no normative status;
- subject to review.

---

## 6.2. Defined

The Metadata artifact has received a complete architectural definition.

Characteristics:

- canonical definition exists;
- semantics established;
- under architectural review.

---

## 6.3. Approved

The Metadata artifact has been formally accepted by architectural governance.

Characteristics:

- approved semantics;
- approved structure;
- eligible for publication.

---

## 6.4. Published

The Metadata artifact becomes part of the official Documentation Framework.

Characteristics:

- normative status;
- publicly referenced;
- available for use by Metadata Profiles.

---

## 6.5. Deprecated

The Metadata artifact should no longer be used for new specifications.

Characteristics:

- retained for compatibility;
- superseded by newer Metadata;
- still documented.

Existing Metadata remains valid.

---

## 6.6. Retired

The Metadata artifact has reached the end of its architectural lifecycle.

Characteristics:

- no longer recommended;
- preserved for historical traceability;
- excluded from future Metadata Profiles.

Historical Metadata Instances remain interpretable.

---

```text

                Proposed

                    │
                    ▼

                    │
                    ▼

                Published
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Reverse transitions shall not occur except through formal architectural governance.

---

# 8. Lifecycle Responsibilities

The Metadata Lifecycle defines responsibilities for each stage.

| Lifecycle Stage | Responsibility |
|-----------------|----------------|
| Proposed | Identify new Metadata requirements. |
| Defined | Produce canonical architectural definitions. |
| Approved | Validate architectural consistency. |
| Published | Make Metadata available for framework use. |
| Deprecated | Preserve compatibility while discouraging new usage. |
| Retired | Preserve historical reference only. |

---

# 10. Lifecycle Constraints

The Metadata Lifecycle shall satisfy the following constraints.

## 10.1. Controlled Introduction

New Metadata shall enter the lifecycle through the Proposed state.

---

## 10.2. No Implicit Approval

Metadata shall never become normative without explicit approval.

The Documentation Framework relies on Metadata to provide consistent, structured and reliable descriptions of documents.

To preserve architectural integrity, Metadata shall satisfy a set of validation rules that ensure compliance with the Metadata Architecture, Metadata Model and Metadata Schema.

This document defines the architectural principles governing Metadata Validation.

---

# 4. Validation Principles

Metadata Validation follows the principles below.

## 4.1. Architectural Validation

Validation verifies architectural conformance.

It shall not introduce new Metadata.

---

## 4.2. Deterministic Validation

Given the same Metadata and the same specification, validation shall always produce the same result.

---

## 4.3. Independent Validation

Validation shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 4.4. Non-Destructive Validation

Validation shall never modify Metadata.

It only evaluates conformance.

---

## 4.5. Explicit Validation

Validation outcomes shall be explicit and reproducible.

```text

---

---

## 7.4. Consistency Validation

They represent recommended approaches for designing, extending and managing Metadata within the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Guiding Principles

The following principles should guide every Metadata design decision.

## 4.1. Prefer Simplicity

Metadata should remain as simple as possible while fulfilling its intended purpose.

Avoid unnecessary complexity.

---

## 4.2. Preserve Semantic Clarity

Every Metadata Element should possess one explicit and easily understandable meaning.

Avoid ambiguous terminology.

---

## 4.3. Promote Reuse

Existing Metadata Elements should be reused whenever possible.

Introducing new Metadata should always be justified.

---

## 4.4. Maintain Consistency

Metadata should remain consistent throughout the Documentation Framework.

Similar concepts should be described in similar ways.

---

## 4.5. Design for Evolution

Metadata should be designed with future extension in mind.

Avoid designs that unnecessarily restrict future architectural evolution.

This document constitutes the normative specification of the Metadata component within the Documentation Framework.

It consolidates the architectural principles, concepts, constraints and specifications defined throughout the Metadata documentation family into a single authoritative specification.

This document defines the contractual requirements that every Metadata implementation shall satisfy in order to conform to the Documentation Framework.

---

# 5. Specification Principles

This specification is founded upon the following principles.

## 5.1. Architectural Consistency

All Metadata shall conform to the Documentation Framework architecture.

---

## 5.2. Semantic Stability

Metadata semantics shall remain stable throughout the Metadata Lifecycle.

---

## 5.3. Technology Independence

The Metadata specification shall remain independent of implementation technologies.

---

## 5.4. Canonical Definition

Every Metadata concept shall possess one authoritative definition.

---

## 5.5. Controlled Evolution

Metadata shall evolve only through the governance mechanisms defined by the Documentation Framework.

Metadata shall satisfy the following semantic requirements.

- Every Metadata Element shall possess one canonical meaning.
- Semantic definitions shall remain stable.
- Equivalent Metadata Elements shall not coexist.
- Metadata terminology shall remain consistent.
- Metadata interpretation shall be deterministic.

---

# 13. Constraint Requirements

All Metadata Constraints defined by the Documentation Framework shall be respected.

Constraint violations shall be detectable through Metadata Validation.

---

# 15. Conformance Levels

This specification defines two levels of conformance.

## 15.1. Core Conformance

An implementation conforms at the Core level when it satisfies every mandatory requirement defined by this specification.

---

## 15.2. Extended Conformance

An implementation conforms at the Extended level when it:

- satisfies Core Conformance;
- supports Metadata extensibility;
- supports Metadata governance;
- supports Metadata lifecycle management.

# 4. Example 1 — Metadata Element

The following example illustrates a Metadata Element.

| Attribute | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| Identifier | MTD-DOC-001 |
| Name | Document Identifier |
| Category | Identity Metadata |
| Definition | Uniquely identifies a document within a Documentation Framework repository. |
| Value Type | Identifier |
| Cardinality | Exactly One |
| Required | Yes |
