# 5. Example 2 — Metadata Group

Metadata Elements may be organized into logical groups.

```text

                    Identity Metadata
                    │
                    ├── Document Identifier
                    ├── Document Version
                    ├── Document Revision
                    └── Baseline

```

The grouping improves organization without altering the semantics of individual Metadata Elements.

---

# 6. Example 3 — Metadata Schema

A Metadata Schema organizes Metadata Elements.

```text

                    Metadata Schema
                    │
                    ├── Identity Metadata
                    │   ├── Document Identifier
                    │   ├── Version
                    │   └── Revision
                    │
                    ├── Classification Metadata
                    │   ├── Category
                    │   ├── Status
                    │   └── Language
                    │
                    └── Lifecycle Metadata
                        ├── Created Date
                        ├── Updated Date
                        └── Lifecycle State

```

The schema defines the architectural organization of Metadata.

```text

                    Canonical Metadata Schema

                    ▼                              ▼

                    ▼

# Metadata Component

> **Documentation Framework — Documentation Component**

---

> The architectural component responsible for defining, organizing, governing and standardizing the metadata that describes documents within the Documentation Framework.

---

# Overview

The **Metadata** component defines the canonical metadata architecture of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the concepts, structures, lifecycle, governance and specifications required to describe documents in a consistent, technology-independent and architecturally stable manner.

Metadata provides the common semantic foundation upon which the remaining Documentation Framework components are built.

---

# Purpose

The Metadata component is responsible for defining:

- the Metadata architecture;
- Metadata concepts;
- Metadata models;
- Metadata elements;
- Metadata schemas;
- Metadata validation;
- Metadata governance;
- Metadata extensibility.

The component does **not** define:

- document content;
- document storage;
- repositories;
- workflows;
- permissions;
- implementation technologies.

---

# Responsibilities

The Metadata component is responsible for:

- defining canonical Metadata concepts;
- defining Metadata Elements;
- defining Metadata Schemas;
- defining Metadata Profiles;
- defining Metadata Relationships;
- defining Metadata Constraints;
- defining Metadata Lifecycle;
- defining Metadata Validation;
- defining Metadata Governance;
- defining Metadata Extensibility;
- maintaining the Metadata Dictionary;
- publishing the Metadata Specification.

---

# Component Scope

The Metadata component defines **what metadata is** and **how it is architecturally described** within the Documentation Framework.

It does not define:

- how documents are managed;
- how repositories operate;
- how metadata is physically stored;
- how metadata is implemented;
- how metadata is exchanged between systems.

Those responsibilities belong to other Documentation Framework components.

---

# Architectural Position

Within the Documentation Framework architecture, Metadata is a **Documentation Component**.

Conceptually.

```text

					Documentation Framework
					│
					├── Foundation
					├── Architecture
					├── Documentation
					│   ├── Metadata
					│   ├── Document Identity
					│   ├── Classification
					│   └── Templates
					│
					├── Governance
					├── Discovery
					├── Automation
					├── Integration
					├── Resources
					├── Guides
					└── Reference

```

Metadata provides the semantic foundation for multiple Documentation Framework components while remaining independent of their individual responsibilities.

---

# Document Organization

The Metadata component documentation is organized into four architectural areas.

```text

					Metadata/
					│
					├── README.md
					│
					├── 01-Architecture/
					│
					├── 02-Structure/
					│
					├── 03-Behavior/
					│
					└── 04-Reference/

```

Each directory groups documents according to a specific architectural responsibility.

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the **Template Schema** of the Documentation Framework.

The Template Schema provides the structural representation required to describe a Template according to the concepts and relationships defined by the Templates component.

It establishes how a Template, its structural components, and their associations are represented at schema level.

The Template Schema is technology-independent and does not prescribe a particular serialization format, implementation technology, storage mechanism, or repository structure.

### 1.2. Scope

This document defines the structural schema for:

* Templates;
* Template Types;
* Template Structures;
* Template Sections;
* Template Elements;
* Template Parameters;
* Template Constraints;
* Template Relationships;
* Template Versions;
* structural references between Template components;
* structural representation of Template composition;
* structural representation of Template specialization;
* structural representation of Template Instances.

This document does not define the detailed semantics of:

* Template lifecycle;
* Template validation;
* Template governance;
* Template relationships;
* Template constraints;
* Template extensibility.

Those concerns are defined by the corresponding Templates component documents.

### 1.3. Schema Position

The Template Schema is the structural representation of the Template Model.

The conceptual progression is:

```text

            Template Concepts
                    │
                    ▼

              Template Model
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Elements
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Schema
            │
            ├───▶  Template Lifecycle
            │
            ├───▶  Template Validation
            │
            ├───▶  Template Governance
            │
            ├───▶  Template Relationships
            │
            ├───▶  Template Constraints
            │
            └───▶  Template Extensibility

```

| Level             | Responsibility                                                  |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Concepts**      | Defines what Template concepts mean                             |

| **Schema**        | Defines their structural representation                         |

| **Governance**    | Defines controlled management                                   |

The Element Name provides the human-readable name of the Element.

### 7.4. Position

Position represents the Element's structural order within its parent structure when ordering applies.

### 7.5. Occurrence

Occurrence represents the permitted number of occurrences of the Element.

### 7.6. Applicability

Applicability identifies whether the Element participates in the Template Structure and, where applicable, the conditions under which it applies.

### 7.7. Content

Content represents the content definition associated with a Content Element or another Element for which content is applicable.

The schema does not prescribe a concrete content format.

The category identifies the structural role of the Element.

The Element Identifier provides a stable reference within the Template Schema.

### 7.7. Content

The schema does not prescribe a concrete content format.

---

## 8. Ordering Representation

Ordering represents the relative structural position of Sections and Elements.

Example:

```text

            Template Structure
            │
            ├── Section A  [Position 1]
            │
            ├── Section B  [Position 2]
            │
            └── Section C  [Position 3]

```

Within a Section:

```text

            Section
            │
            ├── Element A  [Position 1]
            │
            ├── Element B  [Position 2]
            │
            └── Element C  [Position 3]

```

Ordering is semantic structural information.

It must not be interpreted as:

* file-system order;
* directory order;
* serialization order;
* database record order.

A concrete implementation may serialize components in another order provided that the defined structural ordering remains recoverable.

---

## 9. Occurrence Representation

Occurrence defines the allowed number of instances of a structural component.

Abstract representation:

```text

            Occurrence
            │
            ├── Minimum
            │
            └── Maximum

```

Occurrence may represent:

* mandatory components;
* optional components;
* repeated components;
* bounded repetition;
* unbounded repetition.

Examples:

```text

    Required:
        Minimum = 1
        Maximum = 1

    Optional:
        Minimum = 0
        Maximum = 1

    Repeated:
        Minimum = 0
        Maximum = *

```

These examples illustrate structural representation only.

Detailed occurrence constraint semantics belong to the Template Constraints documentation.

---

## 10. Parameter Schema

A Template Parameter represents controlled variation within a Template.

The schema represents the parameter definition.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── TemplateParameter
                │
                ├── Name
                │
                ├── Definition
                │
                ├── Applicability
                │
                └── Constraints

```

The distinction between definition and value is maintained:

```text

            Template Schema
            │
            └── Parameter Definition
                        │
                        ▼

                Template Instance
                │
                └── Parameter Value

```

The Template Schema therefore defines what may vary without defining the concrete value selected for a particular Template Instance.

The schema does not prescribe a programming-language type system or parameter implementation.

---

## 11. Constraint Representation

The Template Schema represents constraints as associations between a constraint definition and its target.

Abstract representation:

```text

            TemplateConstraint
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            └── Definition

```

Possible targets include:

```text

Template
Section
Element
Parameter
Relationship

```

The schema establishes where a constraint applies.

It does not define:

* constraint semantics;
* constraint evaluation;
* validation algorithms;
* validation results;
* enforcement mechanisms.

Those concerns are defined by DF-TPL-010 and DF-TPL-007.

---

## 12. Relationship Representation

The Template Schema represents relationships independently from structural containment.

Abstract representation:

```text

            TemplateRelationship
            │
            ├── Source
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            └── Definition

```

This permits a relationship to connect entities that do not have a parent-child relationship.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── relationship  ─────►  Template B

```

or:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── relationship  ─────►  Element B

```

The schema defines the structural representation of the association.

Detailed relationship semantics and relationship categories are defined by DF-TPL-009.

---

## 13. Template Composition Representation

Template Composition permits a Template Structure to incorporate reusable structures from another Template or reusable Template component.

Abstract representation:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── Structure
                │
                └── Composition Reference
                              │
                              ▼

                     Template B Structure

```

The schema represents the composition reference and its structural position.

It does not define:

* composition resolution algorithms;
* composition conflict resolution;
* composition precedence;
* implementation mechanisms.

Those concerns belong to the applicable Templates behavior and extensibility documentation.

---

## 14. Template Specialization Representation

Template Specialization represents a Template derived from another Template while preserving the conceptual relationship between them.

Abstract representation:

```text

              Base Template

                    ▲
                    │
               specializes
                    │
           Specialized Template

```

The schema represents the reference to the specialized Template's source Template.

Specialization does not imply that the specialized Template is a new unrelated Template.

Detailed specialization rules are addressed by the Templates component's extensibility model.

---

## 15. Template Version Representation

The schema identifies the Template Version associated with the represented Template definition.

Abstract representation:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── TemplateVersion
                │
                └── VersionIdentifier

```

Template Version represents the evolution state of the Template definition.

It is distinct from:

```text

    Template Version
           !=
    Document Identity

    Template Version
           !=
    Document Revision

    Template Version
           !=
    Document Edition

    Template Version
           !=
        Baseline

```

A document created using a particular Template Version retains its own Document Identity independently of the Template Version.

---

## 16. Template Instance Representation

A Template Instance represents a concrete application of a Template.

The structural relationship is:

```text

                 Template
                    │
                    ▼

             Template Schema
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance

```

A Template Instance may contain concrete:

* content;
* parameter values;
* structural occurrences;
* applicable sections;
* applicable elements.

The Template Instance must remain distinguishable from the Template definition.

```text

           Template Definition
                    │
            defines structure
                    │
                    ▼

            Template Instance
                    │
          represents application
                    │
                    ▼

            Document Instance

```

The Templates component does not assign Document Identity to the resulting Document Instance.

---

## 18. Schema Invariants

The following invariants apply to the Template Schema.

### 18.1. Template Root Invariant

Every Template Schema has one Template as its root conceptual entity.

### 18.2. Structure Invariant

Every represented Section belongs to a Template Structure.

### 18.3. Element Context Invariant

Every represented Element has a defined structural context.

### 18.4. Reference Resolution Invariant

Every schema reference identifies a resolvable schema entity.

### 18.5. Parameter Resolution Invariant

Every parameter reference corresponds to a defined Template Parameter.

### 18.6. Relationship Invariant

Every represented relationship identifies its participating entities.

### 18.7. Occurrence Invariant

Occurrence information is associated with the structural component to which it applies.

### 18.8. Version Invariant

Every Template Schema identifies the Template Version represented by the schema.

### 18.9. Semantic Preservation Invariant

The schema representation must preserve the semantics established by the Template Model.

### 18.10. Responsibility Invariant

The Template Schema must not assume responsibility for concepts owned by other Documentation Framework components.

### 18.11. Technology Independence Invariant

The schema must remain independent of any particular implementation technology, serialization format, repository, or storage mechanism.

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the relationship model used by the Templates component of the Documentation Framework.

It establishes the semantic meaning, participants, categories, directionality, cardinality, and representation of relationships between Templates and their structural elements.

The purpose of the relationship model is to provide an explicit and consistent mechanism for expressing how Templates, Template Structures, Template Sections, and Template Elements are related.

# 3. Relationship Model

A **Template Relationship** represents an explicitly defined relationship between two Template model entities.

A relationship has:

* a source participant;
* a target participant;
* a relationship type;
* a direction;
* a defined semantic meaning;
* an applicable cardinality;
* an optional set of additional properties.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Source
            │
            ├── Relationship Type
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Direction
            │
            ├── Cardinality
            │
            └── Applicability

```

The relationship model does not require a particular serialization or implementation technology.

---

# 4. Relationship Participants

Template Relationships may involve entities defined by the Template Model.

The principal participants are:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Template Structure
            │
            ├── Template Section
            │
            ├── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Parameter
            │
            ├── Template Constraint
            │
            ├── Template Version
            │
            └── Template Instance

```

Not every entity participates in every relationship category.

The most important relationship participants are:

* Template;
* Template Structure;
* Template Section;
* Template Element.

Template Version provides version context for relationships but does not replace the relationship between the underlying entities.

Template Instance represents an application of a Template and is therefore treated separately from relationships between Template definitions.

---

# 5. Relationship Representation

A relationship should be conceptually representable by the following structure:

```text

            Relationship
            │
            ├── Source
            │
            ├── Type
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Direction
            │
            ├── Cardinality
            │
            └── Applicability

```

Where:

| Property          | Meaning                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **Source**        | Entity from which the relationship originates    |
| **Type**          | Semantic category of the relationship            |
| **Target**        | Entity toward which the relationship is directed |
| **Direction**     | Directional interpretation of the relationship   |
| **Cardinality**   | Number of permitted participants                 |
| **Applicability** | Conditions under which the relationship applies  |

Additional properties may be introduced by the Template Schema and Constraint models.

Relationship representation must not imply a particular database, file format, programming language, or repository structure.

---

# 6. Relationship Categories

Template Relationships are classified according to their semantic purpose.

The principal categories are:

```text

            Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Containment
            │
            ├── Reference
            │
            ├── Dependency
            │
            ├── Composition
            │
            ├── Specialization
            │
            └── Association

```

## 6.1. Containment Relationship

A **Containment Relationship** expresses structural membership of one Template entity within another.

Examples include:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Structure

            Template Structure
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Section

            Template Section
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

Containment defines structural ownership within a Template Structure.

The detailed schema representation of containment is defined by DF-TPL-005.

## 6.2. Reference Relationship

A **Reference Relationship** expresses an explicit link to another Template entity without making the target a structural child.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Template B

```

A reference does not imply:

* containment;
* composition;
* specialization;
* physical co-location.

References provide explicit semantic linkage without changing structural ownership.

## 6.3. Dependency Relationship

A **Dependency Relationship** indicates that one Template or Template Element relies on another Template entity for a defined purpose.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Template B

```

Dependency does not by itself imply composition or specialization.

The existence and semantics of a dependency must remain explicit.

## 6.4. Composition Relationship

A **Composition Relationship** expresses that a Template incorporates another Template or Template Structure as part of its reusable structure.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

```

Composition is stronger than a simple reference because the target contributes structurally to the resulting Template.

Composition is a defined reuse mechanism of the Template Model.

## 6.5. Specialization Relationship

A **Specialization Relationship** expresses that one Template derives from another Template while preserving its general semantic basis.

Conceptually:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── specialized by  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The specialized Template may extend, restrict, or otherwise refine the structure of the base Template subject to the applicable Template Constraints.

Specialization is distinct from Composition:

```text

            Specialization
                Base Template
                │
                └─────►  Derived Template

            Composition
                Template A
                │
                └─────►  incorporates Template B

```

## 6.6. Association Relationship

An **Association Relationship** expresses a semantic relationship between Template entities that does not correspond to containment, reference, dependency, composition, or specialization.

Association provides a general relationship category for explicit semantic links that require representation without implying stronger structural semantics.

---

## 6.1. Containment Relationship

A **Containment Relationship** expresses structural membership of one Template entity within another.

Examples include:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Structure

            Template Structure
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Section

            Template Section
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

Containment defines structural ownership within a Template Structure.

The detailed schema representation of containment is defined by DF-TPL-005.

## 6.2. Reference Relationship

A **Reference Relationship** expresses an explicit link to another Template entity without making the target a structural child.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Template B

```

A reference does not imply:

* containment;
* composition;
* specialization;
* physical co-location.

References provide explicit semantic linkage without changing structural ownership.

## 6.3. Dependency Relationship

A **Dependency Relationship** indicates that one Template or Template Element relies on another Template entity for a defined purpose.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Template B

```

Dependency does not by itself imply composition or specialization.

The existence and semantics of a dependency must remain explicit.

## 6.4. Composition Relationship

A **Composition Relationship** expresses that a Template incorporates another Template or Template Structure as part of its reusable structure.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

```

Composition is stronger than a simple reference because the target contributes structurally to the resulting Template.

Composition is a defined reuse mechanism of the Template Model.

## 6.5. Specialization Relationship

A **Specialization Relationship** expresses that one Template derives from another Template while preserving its general semantic basis.

Conceptually:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── specialized by  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The specialized Template may extend, restrict, or otherwise refine the structure of the base Template subject to the applicable Template Constraints.

Specialization is distinct from Composition:

```text

            Specialization
                Base Template
                │
                └─────►  Derived Template

            Composition
                Template A
                │
                └─────►  incorporates Template B

```

## 6.6. Association Relationship

An **Association Relationship** expresses a semantic relationship between Template entities that does not correspond to containment, reference, dependency, composition, or specialization.

Association provides a general relationship category for explicit semantic links that require representation without implying stronger structural semantics.

---

# 7. Template-to-Template Relationships

Templates may have relationships with other Templates.

Examples include:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

            Template A
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template B

```

These relationships must retain their semantic distinction.

A reference must not be interpreted as composition.

A dependency must not automatically be interpreted as specialization.

A composition must not automatically be interpreted as inheritance.

A specialization must not automatically be interpreted as physical reuse.

---

# 8. Template-to-Element Relationships

A Template may relate directly to Template Elements.

The principal structural relationship is containment:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

A Template may also establish other relationships when explicitly required by the Template Model.

For example:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Reusable Element

```

The relationship type determines the semantic interpretation.

An Element referenced by a Template is not necessarily structurally contained by that Template.

---

# 9. Element-to-Element Relationships

Template Elements may be related to other Template Elements.

Examples include:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── references  ─────►  Element B

            Element A
            │
            └── depends on  ─────►  Element B

            Element A
            │
            └── associates with  ─────►  Element B

```

Element-to-Element relationships allow structural semantics to be represented without requiring every relationship to be expressed through a Template or Section.

Such relationships must remain explicit and must not introduce implicit containment.

---

# 10. Relationship Directionality

Relationships may be directional or conceptually symmetric.

## 10.1. Directional Relationships

Directional relationships have a defined source and target.

Examples:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template B

```

The direction is semantically significant.

Reversing the relationship changes its meaning:

```text

            Template B
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Template A

```

is not equivalent to the original relationship.

## 10.2. Symmetric Associations

Some associations may be interpreted symmetrically.

For example:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── associated with  ─────►  Element B

```

When the semantics are symmetric, the relationship representation must not introduce an artificial directional meaning.

## 10.3. Inverse Interpretation

A directional relationship may have an inverse interpretation.

For example:

```text

            Derived Template
            │
            └── specializes  ─────►  Base Template

```

may be viewed inversely as:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── has specialization  ─────►  Derived Template

```

The inverse view does not create a second independent relationship.

---

```

may be viewed inversely as:

```

---

# 11. Relationship Cardinality

Relationship cardinality defines how many instances of one participant may be related to another.

Typical cardinalities include:

```text

    1 : 1
    1 : N
    N : 1
    N : N

```

Examples:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Structure

```

may establish a one-to-one relationship where the Template Model requires a single Template Structure.

Conversely:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Template Element

```

may permit multiple Elements.

Cardinality is a structural property of the relationship and must be represented consistently with the Template Schema.

Detailed cardinality constraints are defined by DF-TPL-010.

---

# 12. Relationship Identity

A Template Relationship must be distinguishable from other relationships when required for traceability.

Relationship identity may be established by its conceptual combination of:

```text

                  Source
                    +
            Relationship Type
                    +
                  Target
                    +
        Applicable Version Context

```

The exact technical representation of relationship identity is implementation-independent.

Relationship identity must support:

* traceability;
* validation;
* controlled evolution;
* relationship-specific governance where required.

---

# 13. Relationship Version Context

Relationships may exist in the context of a specific Template Version.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Version
            │
            └── defines  ─────►  Relationship

```

A relationship may therefore:

* be introduced by a Template Version;
* remain unchanged across versions;
* be modified in a later version;
* become obsolete in a later version.

Template Version remains distinct from the relationship itself.

A relationship change does not create a new semantic relationship merely because the containing Template has a new version.

---

# 14. Relationship and Composition

Composition establishes a structural reuse relationship.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B
                                  │
                                  └── contributes structure

```

The composed Template may contribute:

* Sections;
* Elements;
* reusable structures;
* defined parameters;
* other reusable Template structures.

Composition must remain explicit.

A simple reference to a Template does not constitute composition.

Composition semantics must also remain compatible with Template Constraints and Template Validation.

---

# 15. Relationship and Specialization

Specialization establishes a derivational relationship between Templates.

Conceptually:

```text

          Base Template
                │
                └── specialization relationship
                    │
                    ▼

             Derived Template

```

A specialized Template retains a defined semantic relationship with its base Template.

Specialization may be used to:

* refine a general Template;
* provide a more specific Template;
* extend a reusable Template;
* establish controlled structural variation.

Specialization must not be confused with Template Version.

A new Template Version represents evolution of the same Template definition.

A specialized Template represents a distinct Template related to another Template.

---

# 16. Relationship and Validation

Relationships are subject to Template Validation.

Validation may determine whether:

* the relationship is structurally valid;
* the relationship type is applicable;
* the participants are compatible;
* cardinality requirements are satisfied;
* composition is valid;
* specialization is valid;
* referenced entities exist;
* cross-template relationships conform to applicable rules.

Validation does not define relationship semantics.

The responsibility boundary is:

```text

            Template Relationships
            │
            └── defines relationship meaning

            Template Constraints
            │
            └── defines relationship restrictions

            Template Validation
            │
            └── evaluates conformance

```

---

# 19. Cross-Component Relationship Boundaries

Template Relationships may interact with concepts defined by other Documentation Framework components.

These interactions do not transfer responsibility to Templates.

| Component             | Relationship with Templates                                                  |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Metadata**          | Templates may require metadata-related structural locations or compatibility |
| **Document Identity** | Templates may define identity-related structural locations                   |
| **Classification**    | Templates may define classification-related structural locations             |
| **Workflow**          | Workflow may operate using Template-derived structures                       |
| **Validation**        | Validation evaluates relationship conformance                                |
| **Automation**        | Automation may process Template relationships                                |
| **Registry**          | Registry may reference Templates and their relationships                     |

Templates do not define:

* metadata semantics;
* document identity semantics;
* classification semantics;
* workflow semantics;
* registry semantics;
* repository relationships.

---

# 20. Relationship Invariants

The following invariants apply to Template Relationships.

### 20.1. Invariant 1 — Explicit Semantics

Every relationship must have a defined semantic type.

### 20.2. Invariant 2 — Explicit Participants

Every relationship must identify its applicable participants.

### 20.3. Invariant 3 — Explicit Direction

A directional relationship must define its direction.

### 20.4. Invariant 4 — No Implicit Composition

A reference or dependency must not implicitly become a composition.

### 20.5. Invariant 5 — No Implicit Specialization

A composition or dependency must not implicitly become specialization.

### 20.6. Invariant 6 — Structural Consistency

Containment relationships must remain consistent with the Template Schema.

### 20.7. Invariant 7 — Version Distinction

Template Version and Template Relationship are distinct concepts.

### 20.8. Invariant 8 — Component Independence

Template Relationships must remain independent of physical storage and repository organization.

### 20.9. Invariant 9 — Responsibility Separation

Relationship definitions must not redefine concepts owned by other DF components.

### 20.10. Invariant 10 — Traceability

Relationship changes must remain traceable when required by Template governance.

            │
            ├── Composition
            │
            ├── Specialization
            │
            └── Association

```

The model distinguishes:

* structural containment from semantic association;
* reference from dependency;
* composition from specialization;
* Template relationships from Template Versions;
* relationship definition from relationship validation;
* relationship semantics from relationship constraints.

This provides the structural basis required for consistent Template reuse, composition, specialization, traceability, and controlled evolution.

### 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the constraint model used by the Templates component of the Documentation Framework.

Template Constraints establish restrictions and conditions that govern the valid structure, composition, relationships, parameters, and applicability of Templates and their Elements.

### 1.3. Architectural Position

Template Constraints are part of the structural definition of a Template.

They refine the Template Model and Template Schema defined by:

* DF-TPL-003 — Template Model;
* DF-TPL-005 — Template Schema.

Constraints provide rules against which conformance may subsequently be evaluated by DF-TPL-007 — Template Validation.

The responsibility boundary is therefore:

```text

            Template Model
            │
            └── defines conceptual structure

            Template Schema
            │
            └── represents structural definition

            Template Constraints
            │
            └── defines restrictions and conditions

            Template Validation
            │
            └── evaluates conformance

```

---

# 3. Constraint Model

A **Template Constraint** is a defined restriction or condition applicable to a Template entity or relationship.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Constraint
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Constraint Type
            │
            ├── Rule
            │
            ├── Applicability
            │
            └── Severity

```

A constraint may apply to:

* a Template;
* a Template Structure;
* a Template Section;
* a Template Element;
* a Template Parameter;
* a Template Relationship;
* a Composition;
* a Specialization.

The constraint model defines the semantics of the restriction but does not prescribe how the restriction is implemented.

---

# 4. Constraint Participants

Constraints may target the entities defined by the Template Model.

```text"

            Template
            │
            ├── Template Structure
            │   │
            │   └── Template Section
            │       │
            │       └── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Parameter
            │
            ├── Template Relationship
            │
            ├── Template Composition
            │
            └── Template Specialization

```

A constraint may apply to a single entity or to a relationship between entities.

---

# 5. Constraint Categories

The principal categories are:

```text

            Template Constraint
            │
            ├── Structural Constraint
            │
            ├── Element Constraint
            │
            ├── Occurrence Constraint
            │
            ├── Cardinality Constraint
            │
            ├── Parameter Constraint
            │
            ├── Relationship Constraint
            │
            ├── Composition Constraint
            │
            ├── Specialization Constraint
            │
            └── Applicability Constraint

```

These categories describe the semantic purpose of a constraint.

They are not necessarily mutually exclusive.

A single constraint may involve more than one aspect of a Template.

---

# 6. Structural Constraints

A **Structural Constraint** restricts the organization of a Template Structure.

Examples include requirements concerning:

* required Sections;
* permitted Elements;
* Section ordering;
* permitted nesting;
* structural dependencies between Sections;
* permitted structural arrangements.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template Structure
            │
            └── Structural Constraints
                │
                ├── required Section
                │
                ├── permitted Element
                │
                └── ordering rule

```

Structural Constraints must remain consistent with the Template Schema.

---

# 8. Occurrence Constraints

An **Occurrence Constraint** controls how many times an Element or Section may occur within a defined structural context.

Typical occurrence semantics include:

```text

0 occurrences
1 occurrence
0..1 occurrences
1..N occurrences
0..N occurrences

```

For example:

```text

            Template Section
            │
            └── contains  ─────►  Element
                                  │
                                  └── occurrence: 1..N

```

Occurrence constraints are structural restrictions.

They must not be interpreted as workflow requirements.

---

# 9. Cardinality Constraints

A **Cardinality Constraint** restricts the number of permitted participants in a relationship.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

```

may be constrained so that a particular Template can compose one or more Templates.

Cardinality constraints may apply to:

* Template-to-Template relationships;
* Template-to-Element relationships;
* Element-to-Element relationships;
* containment relationships.

Cardinality semantics must remain consistent with DF-TPL-005 and DF-TPL-009.

---

# 11. Relationship Constraints

A **Relationship Constraint** restricts the permitted use of Template Relationships.

Relationship Constraints may govern:

* permitted relationship types;
* permitted source entities;
* permitted target entities;
* direction;
* cardinality;
* relationship applicability;
* prohibited relationships;
* dependency conditions.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── Relationship Constraint
                │
                ├── specialization  ─────►  permitted
                │
                ├── composition     ─────►  permitted
                │
                └── other type      ─────►  restricted

```

Relationship semantics themselves are defined by DF-TPL-009.

---

# 12. Composition Constraints

A **Composition Constraint** restricts how Templates may be composed.

Composition Constraints may define:

* permitted composed Templates;
* prohibited compositions;
* composition cardinality;
* composition applicability;
* structural compatibility requirements;
* composition dependency restrictions.

Composition Constraints must prevent an unrestricted interpretation of Template reuse.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── composes  ─────►  Template B

```

may be valid only when the relationship satisfies the applicable Composition Constraints.

---

# 13. Specialization Constraints

A **Specialization Constraint** restricts how a Template may specialize another Template.

Specialization Constraints may define:

* permitted base Templates;
* permitted derived Templates;
* structural compatibility;
* restrictions on inherited structure;
* permitted specialization scope;
* prohibited specialization patterns.

Conceptually:

```text

            Base Template
            │
            └── specialization constraint
                            │
                            ▼

                     Derived Template

```

Specialization Constraints must preserve the semantic distinction between specialization and Template Version.

---

# 14. Applicability Constraints

An **Applicability Constraint** defines the conditions under which a Template entity, Element, Parameter, or Relationship applies.

Applicability may depend on:

* Template context;
* structural context;
* another Template Element;
* a Template Parameter;
* a defined Template Relationship.

Conceptually:

```text

            Element A
            │
            └── applicable when  ─────►  defined condition

```

Applicability Constraints allow controlled structural variation without requiring separate Templates for every possible variation.

---

# 15. Constraint Representation

A Template Constraint should be conceptually representable as:

```text

            Constraint
            │
            ├── Target
            │
            ├── Type
            │
            ├── Rule
            │
            ├── Applicability
            │
            └── Severity

```

Where:

| Property          | Meaning                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Target**        | Entity or relationship to which the constraint applies |
| **Type**          | Semantic category of the constraint                    |
| **Rule**          | Restriction or condition being defined                 |
| **Applicability** | Context in which the rule applies                      |
| **Severity**      | Significance assigned to non-conformance               |

The exact representation may be defined by the Template Schema.

No particular syntax, serialization format, database representation, or programming language is required.

---

# 16. Constraint Scope

A constraint may operate at different structural scopes.

### 16.1. Template Scope

Applies to the Template as a whole.

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Constraint

```

### 16.2. Section Scope

Applies to a Template Section and its contents.

```text

            Template Section
            │
            └── Constraint

```

### 16.3. Element Scope

Applies to an individual Template Element.

```text

            Template Element
            │
            └── Constraint

```

### 16.4. Relationship Scope

Applies to a relationship between participants.

```text

            Entity A
            │
            └── Relationship
                │
                └── Constraint

```

### 16.5. Parameter Scope

Applies to a Template Parameter.

```text

            Template Parameter
            │
            └── Constraint

```

---

```

```text

```

---

# 17. Constraint Combination

Multiple constraints may apply to the same Template entity.

For example:

```text

            Template Element
            │
            ├── Element Constraint
            │
            ├── Occurrence Constraint
            │
            ├── Applicability Constraint
            │
            └── Relationship Constraint

```

When multiple constraints apply, their combined interpretation must remain deterministic.

Constraints must not be interpreted in isolation when their scope overlaps.

Conflicting constraints must be identifiable and must not result in an undefined Template interpretation.

---

# 18. Constraint Precedence

When constraints operate at different scopes, their applicability must remain explicit.

For example:

```text

            Template Constraint
            │
            └── Section Constraint
                │
                └── Element Constraint

```

A more specific constraint may refine a broader constraint when such refinement is explicitly permitted.

A specific constraint must not silently override a broader constraint when the resulting interpretation would violate the Template Model.

Detailed precedence rules may be refined by future Template Constraint specifications.

---

# 19. Constraint and Validation

Template Constraints define the conditions for permitted Template structures.

Template Validation evaluates whether those conditions are satisfied.

Therefore:

```text

            Constraint
            │
            └── defines  ─────►  permitted condition

            Validation
            │
            └── evaluates  ─────►  actual conformance

```

A constraint does not itself produce a validation result.

Validation may classify a Template as:

* Conformant;
* Non-Conformant;
* Indeterminate.

These results are defined by DF-TPL-007.

---

# 22. Constraint and Template Version

Constraints are interpreted within the context of the Template Version in which they are defined.

Conceptually:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── Version
                │
                └── Constraints

```

A change to a constraint may therefore constitute a Template Version change.

Template Version remains distinct from:

* Document Edition;
* Document Revision;
* Document Baseline;
* Document Instance.

---

# 23. Constraint and Relationships

Constraints may restrict the relationships defined by DF-TPL-009.

For example:

```text

            Template A
            │
            └── Relationship
                │
                └── Relationship Constraint

```

Relationship Constraints may restrict:

* participant types;
* direction;
* cardinality;
* applicability;
* composition;
* specialization.

Constraints must not redefine relationship categories.

---

# 24. Constraint and Metadata, Identity, and Classification

Templates may define structural locations for Metadata, Document Identity, and Classification information.

Constraints may therefore establish requirements concerning those locations.

However, Templates do not redefine the semantics of those components.

The responsibility boundary remains:

```text

            Metadata
            │
            └── defines metadata semantics

            Document Identity
            │
            └── defines identity semantics

            Classification
            │
            └── defines classification semantics

            Templates
            │
            └── define structural requirements

```

Compatibility constraints may therefore reference these components without incorporating their responsibilities into Templates.

---

# 26. Constraint Invariants

The following invariants apply to Template Constraints.

### 26.1. Invariant 1 — Explicit Target

Every constraint must have an identifiable target.

### 26.2. Invariant 2 — Explicit Semantics

Every constraint must define the restriction or condition it establishes.

### 26.3. Invariant 3 — Defined Scope

The applicability scope of a constraint must be determinable.

### 26.4. Invariant 4 — Structural Consistency

Constraints must remain consistent with the Template Model and Template Schema.

### 26.5. Invariant 5 — No Implicit Override

A constraint must not silently override another applicable constraint.

### 26.6. Invariant 6 — Validation Separation

Constraints define conditions; validation evaluates conformance.

### 26.7. Invariant 7 — Version Traceability

Constraint changes must be attributable to the applicable Template Version.

### 26.8. Invariant 8 — Responsibility Separation

Constraints must not redefine concepts owned by other Documentation Framework components.

### 26.9. Invariant 9 — Technology Independence

Constraint semantics must not depend on a specific implementation technology.

### 26.10. Invariant 10 — Deterministic Interpretation

Applicable constraints must produce an unambiguous structural interpretation.

```text

            │
            ├── Occurrence Constraint
            │
            ├── Cardinality Constraint
            │
            ├── Parameter Constraint
            │
            ├── Relationship Constraint
            │
            ├── Composition Constraint
            │
            ├── Specialization Constraint
            │
            └── Applicability Constraint

```

The fundamental distinction is:

```text

    Template Model
        ─────►  defines what exists

    Template Schema
        ─────►  defines how it is structurally represented

    Template Constraints
        ─────►  define what is permitted

    Template Validation
        ─────►  determines whether the definition conforms

```

This separation provides an explicit and technology-independent foundation for controlled Template structures, reuse, specialization, composition, and evolution.

## 1.1. Purpose

This document defines the normative specification of the **Templates Component** of the Documentation Framework.

It consolidates the architectural, conceptual, structural, behavioral, and extensibility requirements established by the Templates documentation and provides a canonical reference for Template conformance.

The specification defines what a Template is, how Templates are structurally represented, how their elements and relationships are defined, how constraints are expressed, and how Templates are versioned, instantiated, validated, governed, and extended.

This document does not replace the detailed Templates documents. It provides their normative synthesis and establishes the requirements that implementations and dependent Documentation Framework components must respect.

---

# 2. Normative Language

The following terms are used with their normative meaning:

* **MUST** — a mandatory requirement.
* **MUST NOT** — a mandatory prohibition.
* **SHOULD** — a recommended requirement that may be omitted only for a justified reason.
* **SHOULD NOT** — a recommendation against a practice that may be used only for a justified reason.
* **MAY** — an optional capability.

Requirements in this document apply to conformant Template definitions and Template implementations within the scope of the Documentation Framework.

---

# 4. Template Structural Model

The canonical Template structural model is:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Template Type
            │
            ├── Template Structure
            │   │
            │   └── Template Section
            │       │
            │       └── Template Element
            │
            ├── Template Schema
            │
            ├── Template Parameter
            │
            ├── Template Constraint
            │
            ├── Template Relationship
            │
            └── Template Version

```

A conformant Template MUST preserve the distinctions represented by this model.

The Template Model defines the conceptual relationships between these entities.

The Template Schema defines their structural representation.

The Template Constraints define what is permitted.

Template Validation determines whether a Template conforms to its applicable requirements.

---

# 5. Template Type

A **Template Type** identifies the conceptual category of a Template.

Template Types provide semantic classification of Templates without replacing the Classification Component.

A Template MUST be associated with a Template Type where such association is required by the applicable Template Schema.

Template Types MUST NOT be used to redefine document Classification.

---

# 8. Template Elements

A **Template Element** is an identifiable structural or content-bearing component of a Template.

The canonical Template Element categories are:

```text

            Template Element
            │
            ├── Structural Element
            │
            ├── Content Element
            │
            ├── Reference Element
            │
            ├── Metadata Element
            │
            ├── Identity Element
            │
            ├── Classification Element
            │
            ├── Parameterized Element
            │
            └── Reusable Element

```

A Template Element MUST have a defined purpose within its Template Structure.

Template Elements MAY be:

* mandatory or optional;
* singular or repeated;
* ordered;
* parameterized;
* reusable;
* constrained;
* related to other elements.

Metadata Elements, Identity Elements, and Classification Elements provide structural locations or requirements for information belonging to their respective components.

They MUST NOT redefine the semantics of:

* Metadata;
* Document Identity;
* Classification.

---

# 13. Template Composition

**Template Composition** defines the construction of a Template through the combination of existing Template structures or reusable Template Elements.

Composition SHOULD be used to promote:

* reuse;
* consistency;
* modularity;
* controlled structural construction.

Composition MUST preserve the semantic identity of the participating Templates and Elements.

Composition MUST NOT be used merely to create implicit dependencies.

Composition Constraints MAY restrict which Templates or Elements can participate in a composition.

---

# 16. Template Instance

A **Template Instance** is a concrete application of a Template.

A Template Instance represents the use of a Template definition to establish the structure of a concrete documentation artifact.

The distinction MUST be preserved:

```text

            Template
            │
            └── defines reusable structure

            Template Version
            │
            └── identifies a particular Template definition version

            Template Instance
            │
            └── represents a concrete application of the Template

```

A Template Instance MUST NOT redefine the Template itself.

Template Instance management MUST NOT be confused with Document Instance lifecycle management.

---

# 17. Template Lifecycle

A Template MUST follow the applicable Template Lifecycle.

The canonical lifecycle states are:

```text

                  Draft
                    │
                    ▼

                 Defined
                    │
                    ▼

                  Active
                    │
                    ▼

                Deprecated
                    │
                    ▼

                 Retired

```

Additional permitted transitions include:

```text

    Defined     ─────►  Draft
    Deprecated  ─────►  Active
    Active      ─────►  Retired

```

Lifecycle state and Template Version MUST remain distinct.

Lifecycle state identifies the current lifecycle condition of a Template.

Template Version identifies a particular version of its definition.

Retirement MUST NOT imply automatic deletion or loss of historical information.

Historical Template definitions SHOULD be preserved when required for traceability, conformance, or knowledge preservation.

---

# 21. Cross-Component Compatibility

Templates interact with other Documentation Layer components while remaining responsible only for Template concerns.

## 21.1. Metadata

Templates MAY define locations and requirements for Metadata through Metadata Elements.

Templates MUST NOT define Metadata semantics.

Metadata compatibility MAY be evaluated during Template Validation.

---

## 21.2. Document Identity

Templates MAY define structural locations and requirements for Document Identity information through Identity Elements.

# 23. Canonical Abstract Template Definition

The canonical abstract representation of a Template is:

```text

            Template
            │
            ├── Type

### 24.9. Traceability

# Templates Componnet

The **Templates** component is an architectural component of the Documentation Framework responsible for defining, organizing, governing and standardizing reusable structures for documentation.

Templates provide consistent structural patterns for documents that share common purposes, characteristics or organizational requirements.

---

## Purpose

The purpose of the Templates component is to provide a standardized and reusable mechanism for defining documentation structures.

Templates enable recurring documentation patterns to be defined once and reused consistently across the Documentation Framework.

The component contributes to:

* structural consistency;
* documentation reuse;
* predictable organization;
* maintainability;
* structural validation;
* documentation generation.

---

## Architectural Position

Templates belongs to the **Documentation Layer** of the Documentation Framework.

```text

            Documentation Framework
            │
            ├── Foundation
            ├── Architecture
            │
            ├── Documentation
            │   ├── Metadata
            │   ├── DocumentIdentity
            │   ├── Classification
            │   └── Templates
            │
            ├── Governance
            ├── Discovery
            ├── Automation
            └── Integration

```

Templates operates alongside other Documentation Layer components while maintaining clear separation of responsibilities.

---

## Responsibilities

The Templates component is responsible for:

* defining template architecture;
* defining template concepts;
* defining template models;
* defining template elements;
* defining template structures;
* defining template schemas;
* defining template lifecycle;
* defining template validation;
* defining template governance;
* defining template relationships;
* defining template constraints;
* defining template extensibility;
* defining reusable documentation structures;
* supporting standardized documentation creation;
* supporting structural conformance.

---

## Boundaries

Templates defines **documentation structure**.

It does not define or own:

* permanent document identity;
* Metadata semantics;
* document classification semantics;
* document storage;
* document repositories;
* document permissions;
* document workflows;
* document governance policies;
* document registries;
* knowledge graph semantics;
* implementation technologies.

When a template represents information owned by another component, the authoritative definition remains with that component.

---

## Relationships with Other Components

### Metadata

Metadata defines the information used to describe documents.

Templates may define where and how Metadata is structurally represented within a document.

Templates do not redefine Metadata semantics.

### Document Identity

Document Identity defines the permanent identity of documents.

Templates may provide a structural location for document identity information.

Templates do not assign or redefine document identity.

### Classification

Classification defines the classification of documents.

Templates may provide a structural location for classification information.

Templates do not define classification semantics.

### Workflow

Workflow may consume template definitions when standardized document structures are required during document lifecycle activities.

### Registry

Registry may use template information to support the identification or organization of documents according to established structures.

### Validation

Validation may use template definitions to verify structural conformance.

### Automation

Automation may consume template definitions for automated documentation generation and related activities.

---

## Design Principles

The Templates component follows these principles:

1. **Structural Responsibility**
   Templates are responsible for documentation structures.

2. **Reusability**
   Equivalent documentation structures should be defined once and reused.

3. **Consistency**
   Equivalent documentation purposes should use consistent structural patterns.

4. **Separation of Responsibilities**
   Templates shall not assume responsibilities belonging to other components.

5. **Technology Independence**
   Templates shall remain independent of specific implementation technologies.

6. **Repository Independence**
   Templates shall remain independent of document repositories.

7. **Storage Independence**
   Templates shall remain independent of storage mechanisms.

8. **Single Source of Truth**
   Each template concept shall have one authoritative definition.

9. **Controlled Evolution**
   Template definitions shall evolve through controlled changes.

10. **Extensibility**
    Template structures shall support controlled extension and specialization.

---

## Documentation Structure

The Templates component documentation is organized according to the component development roadmap.

```text

            Templates/
            ├── README.md
            │
            ├── DF-TPL-001-Templates-Architecture.md
            ├── DF-TPL-002-Template-Concepts.md
            ├── DF-TPL-003-Template-Model.md
            ├── DF-TPL-004-Template-Elements.md
            ├── DF-TPL-005-Template-Schema.md
            ├── DF-TPL-006-Template-Lifecycle.md
            ├── DF-TPL-007-Template-Validation.md
            ├── DF-TPL-008-Template-Governance.md
            ├── DF-TPL-009-Template-Relationships.md
            ├── DF-TPL-010-Template-Constraints.md
            ├── DF-TPL-011-Template-Extensibility.md
            ├── DF-TPL-012-Template-Best-Practices.md
            ├── DF-TPL-013-Template-Dictionary.md
            ├── DF-TPL-014-Template-Specification.md
            └── DF-TPL-015-Template-Examples.md

```

The exact physical location of these documents is determined by the Documentation Framework component structure and the Templates roadmap.

---

## Development Roadmap

The Templates component is developed through the following stages:

| Stage | Document   | Purpose                 |
| ----- | ---------- | ----------------------- |
| 1     | DF-TPL-001 | Templates Architecture  |
| 2     | DF-TPL-002 | Template Concepts       |
| 3     | DF-TPL-003 | Template Model          |

| 13    | DF-TPL-013 | Template Dictionary     |
| 14    | DF-TPL-014 | Template Specification  |
| 15    | DF-TPL-015 | Template Examples       |

The roadmap defines the sequence in which the Templates component is developed.

---

## Architectural Independence

Templates is independent of:

* programming languages;
* databases;
* file systems;
* document editors;
* repositories;
* storage technologies;
* rendering engines;
* documentation generators;
* version-control systems.

Concrete implementations may provide representations or processing mechanisms for templates without changing their architectural meaning.

---

## Conformance

A Templates implementation conforms to the component architecture when it:

* preserves the responsibility boundaries of Templates;
* uses reusable documentation structures;
* maintains separation from Metadata semantics;
* maintains separation from Document Identity semantics;
* maintains separation from Classification semantics;
* remains independent of repositories and storage;
* remains independent of implementation technologies;
* supports controlled template evolution;
* maintains authoritative template definitions.
